California lawmakers are pushing to stop AI from being used as a full-on therapist as interest in chatbot-based mental healthcare has skyrocketed in recent years.

Under Senate Bill 903, companies would be banned from advertising chatbots as therapy, and AI systems themselves would not be allowed to make therapeutic decisions without review from a licensed professional. The bill would also require patients’ permission for health providers to use AI to record therapy sessions or triage care.

“AI has many upsides, and the possibility to improve the lives of Californians across the state, but only if we ensure it is used responsibly,” state Senator Steve Padilla of San Diego, author of the legislation, said earlier this year when introducing the measure.

“AI algorithms are not fit to take over the job of human therapists, who have skills and training that AI is incapable of replicating,” he added. “We must act and place guardrails that prevent AI algorithms from being deployed in a way that is potentially harmful to patients.”

Critics of the bill say it will stifle legitimate uses of AI and could harm the ability of health providers to use AI tools to direct patients toward treatment.

open image in gallery California lawmakers are pushing to ban AI chatbots explicitly offering themselves as therapists ( Getty/iStock )

“At a time when every county in California faces a shortage of behavioral healthcare workers, SB 903 still puts a clinician bottleneck in front of the intake and screening tools that help patients reach care faster,” Robert Boykin, California executive director of the industry group TechNet, told CalMatters this week.

The National Union of Healthcare Workers, which supports the bill, has filed a complaint with California regulators alleging the Kaiser Permanente health system used an automated “e-visit” system without oversight by clinicians to make care recommendations and provide initial evaluations of patients who may be facing anxiety or depression.

The company has said it “does not use AI to diagnose patients, make clinical decisions, or determine medical necessity,” and argues the group has mischaracterized its process.

Data indicates massive interest in using AI for therapy, though health experts warn that chatbot-based care is an area that needs further study and regulation to compare with genuine medical care.

A 2025 study from RAND, the Brown University School of Public Health and Harvard University found that about one in eight adolescents and young adults are turning to chatbots for mental health care.

“There are few standardized benchmarks for evaluating mental health advice offered by AI chatbots, and there is limited transparency about the datasets that are used to train these large language models,” Jonathan Cantor, a senior policy researcher at RAND, told the Brown University website of the research.

A study this year from the American Psychological Association, meanwhile, found that 77 percent of psychologists have spoken with patients who have used AI for support, engagement or other reasons.

open image in gallery The makers of multiple popular AI tools have faced lawsuits accusing them of being partially responsible for suicides ( AFP/Getty )

In October, OpenAI, maker of the popular ChatGPT, disclosed an estimated 1.2 million per week send messages to the chatbot with “explicit indicators of potential suicidal planning or intent.”

Health experts say the phenomenon has flourish amid difficulties access in-person mental health care.

“Given long waiting lists and difficulty accessing mental health care and therapy in many countries, it’s perhaps not a surprise that increasing numbers [of people] are turning to generative AI for support with their emotional wellbeing,” Hamilton Morrin, a clinical fellow in neuropsychiatry at King’s College London, told Harvard Business Review in June.

The makers of popular AI applications, which can speak with humans in remarkably lifelike ways and resemble human beings with full personalities and consciousness, have faced lawsuits alleging chat tools played a role in youth suicides.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the US, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

Even a slight reduction in daily vigorous exercise could elevate cancer risk by 15 per cent, new research suggests.

Experts warn that replacing physical activity with sedentary habits, such as sitting at a desk or watching TV, directly contributes to this increased risk.

The study also highlights the importance for people who have maintained an active lifestyle to continue doing so, as even minor decreases in activity levels can negatively impact health.

The finding builds upon previous studies that have consistently demonstrated a strong correlation between higher levels of physical activity and a reduced risk of various cancers, including those affecting the bladder, breast, bowel, kidney, and stomach.

Published in the journal BMC Medicine, the new analysis examined lifestyle data and employed modelling to understand the link between exercise and cancer risk.

The research involved 59,218 participants (55 per cent of whom were female) from the UK Biobank, with an average age of 61.7.

open image in gallery Physical activity is linked with a lower likelihood of developing cancer ( PA Archive )

Over an eight-year follow-up period, 2,385 cancer cases were recorded within the group.

Researchers looked at areas such as how long people spent sleeping, sedentary behaviour such as watching TV, standing, and then any movement and at what intensity.

They found that the more people moved, the lower their risk of cancer.

For example, replacing 15 minutes of sleep or sedentary behaviour with 15 minutes of movement were each linked to a 2 per cent reduced risk of cancer.

Conversely, swapping 30 minutes of movement for 30 minutes of sedentary behaviour increased the risk by 8 per cent, while swapping it for sleep increased the risk by 7 per cent.

open image in gallery People who spend a lot of time sitting down have an increased risk of cancer ( Getty/iStock )

Dr John Mitchell, lead author from University College London (UCL), said: “Our study showed that there’s an increased risk of cancer for those who spend a lot of time sitting down.

“We also explored what might happen if people leading active lives reduced their levels of physical activity and found that they also face a higher cancer risk.

“Based on theoretical modelling, our study showed even losing two to three minutes per day of vigorous activity, such as running for a bus, and replacing it with sitting down, sleep or light activity increased their cancer risk.

“Other examples of vigorous activity – that is, anything which elevates your heart rate and makes you sweat – include sport, rushing up the stairs and carrying home heavy grocery bags.

“The take-home message is that for people already leading physically active lives, it’s really important to maintain that level of activity as you get older.”

What are the NHS exercise guidelines?

Current NHS guidelines say adults should aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate intensity activity a week or 75 minutes of vigorous intensity activity a week.

They should also do strength activities that work all the major muscle groups (legs, hips, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms) on at least two days per week.

Examples of moderate activity include very brisk walking (4mph or faster), cycling at 10mph-12mph, or badminton.

Vigorous activity also includes hiking, jogging at 6mph or faster, fast cycling, basketball or tennis.

U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed had a sharp-elbowed response on Sunday after President Donald Trump posted an image on social media comparing his family to that of the Michigan Democrat.

On Saturday, Trump shared an image featuring himself and First Lady Melania Trump on one side and El-Sayed with his wife, Dr. Sarah Jukaku, a psychiatrist, on the other. The image included the caption “Two VERY DIFFERENT America’s [sic].”

Asked about the post on Sunday on CNN, El-Sayed leaned into Trump drawing a contrast between his family and the president’s.

“Yeah, he’s right,” the former public health official said about Trump’s idea of two “very different” Americas.

“One in which your overlords are two people who don’t like each other, but join in the interest of making billions of dollars off of you —or two people who genuinely love each other, enjoyed some pancakes together, want to come together to build the kind of America where they can raise a family and know that that family is going to have the good things,” he said.

open image in gallery Michigan US Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has responded to Donald Trump’s recent social media post about his family, claiming the Trump and First Lady Melania Trump are more interested in making money than being a genuine couple ( Donald Trump )

“So yes, you’ve got two different visions of America,” he added. “Donald Trump’s vision is the one you’re living in right now. Can you afford your gas? Can you afford your groceries?”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

El-Sayed has faced repeated attacks from the president and his allies, which have veered into profanity, false claims and outright Islamophobia.

The president’s post on Saturday used El-Sayed’s full name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, echoing a common rhetorical tactic the Republican has used in attacks against his Democratic predecessor Barack Obama, whom he makes a point to call Barack Hussein Obama, often writing his middle name in all caps on social media.

Trump rose to prominence in national politics in the 2010s in part by fueling the racist birther conspiracy theory that Obama was not born in the U.S. and by calling for a “total and complete shutdown of Muslims entering the United States” during his first campaign. The first and second Trump administrations later attempted to restrict travelers from numerous Muslim-majority countries.

After El-Sayed’s narrow primary win this week, the president has attacked the Michigan Democrat repeatedly along similar lines.

open image in gallery Trump and his allies have sought to paint El-Sayed, a left-leaning progressive Democrat, as a radical communist ( AFP/Getty )

In a speech in Las Vegas, the president accused El-Sayed of being part of a wave of “communists” who would bring “squalor” and “death” to America.

“When I watch Abdul, he's full of s***,” Trump told a crowd at the Red Rock Casino Resort and Spa.

El-Sayed is not a communist, but rather a progressive who is campaigning on issues including Medicare for all and removing corporate money from politics.

Elsewhere in his remarks, Trump accused El-Sayed — who has been critical of the U.S. for supporting Israel’s “genocide” in Gaza — of being hateful and antisemitic.

“Put him in office, you’re going to find out what he loves,” Trump said. “He doesn't love Israel. He doesn't love Jewish people. He hates them. He hates them with a passion that burns in his heart.”

In a victory speech on Wednesday after his primary win over Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens, El-Sayed thanked Jewish supporters of his campaign and affirmed his commitment to representing people of all faiths.

open image in gallery Donald Trump first rose to political prominence by fueling the racist birther conspiracy about Barack Obama, and over the course of the two Trump administrations, the Republican has attempted to ban travelers from largely Muslim-majority countries ( AFP/Getty )

“To all of my sisters and brothers of the Jewish faith, or any faith at all, or no faith at all, I want you to know that my commitment to your safety, my commitment to Jewish safety, is the same commitment that I have to the safety of my own daughters,” he said.

Outgoing Rep. Nancy Mace, in a separate CNN interview on Sunday, again painted El-Sayed as fueling a “communist” takeover and claimed Americans should be “very concerned” about elected leaders who follow “radical Islam ideology” and criticize the country.

“In the future, when our granddaughters are wearing burkas to school, we’re going to look back and say how did this happen?” Mace said, who claimed “America is not built on those values.”

Freedom of religion, speech and political association are enshrined in the First Amendment of the Constitution. The first president, George Washington, made a point of emphasizing the importance of religious tolerance, famously telling an early Jewish congregation that America “gives to bigotry no sanction.”

El-Sayed’s rival in the general election, Mike Rogers, has accused left-leaning Democrats like El-Sayed of leading a movement that’s “anti-American,” pointing to the progressive’s association with leftist Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, who has made comments he later disavowed that America “deserved 9/11.”

“I want to be held accountable for what I say and do, rather than this idea that ... we’re so stuck in cancel culture that we all agreed was a bad idea back in 2020 but we seem to want to bring back,” El-Sayed told Meet the Press on Sunday.

Britain is bracing for another intense heatwave this week, with forecasters predicting temperatures could soar to 36C or even higher, potentially impacting railway lines and power networks. The Met Office is considering issuing rare amber or red extreme heat warnings.

This marks the fifth heatwave of the summer, as the country continues to endure an unprecedented period of dry, hot weather.

While Monday offers a slight reprieve, temperatures are set to climb again from Tuesday.

Met Office meteorologist Tom Morgan stated: "We’ll probably see highs reaching the mid-30s quite widely on Wednesday, and indeed on Thursday too for England and Wales.

“On Wednesday, probably the Midlands, maybe a little bit further south, the M4 corridor, west of London, up towards the Midlands, is where we might have a small chance of reaching 36C in one or two spots.

Half of England and all of Wales have been plunged into drought and more regions could be declared when officials meet at the National Drought Group on Monday ( Peter Nicholls / AFP via Getty Images )

“But Thursday at this stage looks the most likely hottest day of the week.

“So 36C is a fairly reasonable probability locally on Thursday and there’s a small chance it could get even higher than that.”

Half of England and all of Wales have been plunged into drought and more regions could be declared when officials meet at the National Drought Group on Monday.

Mr Morgan said: “If it wasn’t for this incredible summer that we’re currently seeing, then we’d be talking about these temperatures as being really, very unusual.

“But of course, we’ve had such an exceptional summer, people have become a bit used to it.

“There is a potential for impacts, so impacts to infrastructure, things like railway lines and power networks, impacts to vulnerable people as well.”

Health officials have warned of the effect on vulnerable people in the upcoming hot weather, with significant impacts possible in health and social care settings and a potential rise in deaths because of the heat.

Yellow heat health alerts issued by the UK Health Security Agency are in place for the East Midlands, West Midlands, South East, South West, East of England, Yorkshire and the Humber, and London.

The alerts continue until 9pm on Tuesday, but may well be extended as the hot weather continues.

Meanwhile, the Met Office is considering issuing rare extreme heat warnings ahead of the scorching temperatures forecast later in the week.

“We sometimes issue extreme heat warnings, amber and red warnings, which we did back in June, so that’s under consideration at the moment,” Mr Morgan said.

More than 25 million people have restrictions on water use, the Environment Agency said, with millions under hosepipe bans, including all South East Water and Thames Water customers.

Another record is set to tumble this week after Sunday was the 34th day so far this year when temperatures exceeded 30C somewhere in the UK, equalling the record from 1995.

So far, the extreme weather of summer 2026 has included two record-breaking heatwaves in May and June that led to more than 2,800 excess deaths.

Two more heatwaves in July, the driest July in England and Wales since records began in 1836, have fuelled drought and wildfires.

President Donald Trump spent the weekend insisting that vandals damaged his Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool renovations despite his own administration admitting there wasn’t sufficient evidence, ratcheting up pressure on U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro to reverse course after she dropped related criminal charges.

On Sunday, the president posted an image of court documents on Truth Social, writing that a “highly credible witness” saw David Hearn, a 67-year-old former Olympian, “violently” rip the pool’s newly redone coating.

“The National Park Service employee provided this witness testimony to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in early July,” wrote Trump, making a pointed reference to Pirro’s office, which has argued that park officials failed to turn over relevant information.

The president added that others had done “substantial” harm to the pool but there was “no video or proof” beyond the damage itself.

Hearn has pleaded not guilty and denied any wrongdoing.

open image in gallery President Donald Trump has spent days ripping into his hand-picked DC federal prosecutor over her decision to drop criminal charges tied to his disastrous Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool makeover ( AFP/Getty )

One day earlier, the president posted photos showing peeling coating and apparent graffiti, each marked with the word “Vandalism.”

The move follows sharp criticism from the president on Friday, when he publicly urged Pirro to “re-visit her hastily made decision.”

Pirro’s office previously concluded that contractors working on renovation efforts caused the damage rather than criminal actors.

But Trump has repeatedly blamed maintenance issues and declining water quality on alleged sabotage following a controversial project in which he ordered the pool drained and painted with a “American flag blue” liner.

The rift escalated after Pirro moved to drop charges against Hearn, after court filings revealed the administration failed to produce evidence against him and admitted the damage resulted from a botched installation.

Trump publicly unloaded on the prosecutor from the Oval Office. “I was disappointed in Jeanine Pirro. Really disappointed with Jeanine Pirro. She folded like an umbrella,” he told reporters.

The president claimed she “choked” due to pressure from the judge overseeing the case. “Instead of going after the people who did it, he went after her, and went after her department, and I guess she choked. I don’t know what the hell happened,” he said.

Reporters questioned Trump on whether he planned to fire Pirro over the decision, as reported by CNN, prompting him to tell one journalist that “you’re fake news” and “don’t ever talk again.”

Pirro had initially claimed Hearn “woefully destroyed property” in a “deliberate act,” but her office later acknowledged in court documents that the Interior Department provided “less than fulsome information” and that the blue sealant began peeling “almost immediately” due to a rushed process.

open image in gallery Tensions between the White House and top federal prosecutor Jeanine Pirro spilled into public view after she dismissed a felony case against a 67-year-old former Olympian. Trump accused Pirro of having ‘choked’ under judicial pressure, insisting that photos and video prove the landmark was vandalized ( AFP/Getty )

“The Trump administration's case against Davey Hearn should have never been brought,” according to a statement to The Independent from Hearn’s attorneys. “The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology.”

The high-profile refurbishment project — which bypassed standard competitive bidding to award a $14.7 million contract to Atlantic Industrial Coatings LLC — was meant to be finished quickly for $1.5 million ahead of Fourth of July celebrations, according to the president. However, early rain, wind and missed testing deadlines led to rushed work that quickly deteriorated, with algae soon returning to the pool along with peeling paint.

In addition to the photos posted late Saturday, Trump shared a screenshot from X to support his claims of criminal activity.

open image in gallery Trump continues to insist that vandals were responsible for cutting the recently applied lining of the Reflecting Pool despite his own administration appearing to admit that there is no evidence to support his claims ( Getty )

“The material was cut right where the video tape showed, for 300 feet or more. People were on their knees with their hands in the water at the exact location of the ‘slashes,’” Trump wrote. “Additionally, there were witnesses to the VANDALISM, and the flexible areas of the material were cut with a knife.”

Trump had earlier asserted that vandals used a box cutter or knife to create a nearly 300-foot slit in the lining of the pool, while also claiming that fertilizer was poured into the water to trigger rapid algae growth.

“Jeanine Pirro made a mistake. It was vandalism,” Trump said Monday.

“We have photographs or tapes, like moving cameras, right? Where people are on the side cutting it with a box knife,” he added. “Now, I’m not saying I was 100 percent thrilled with the contractor, but the contractor was rushing. We wanted to get it open for July 4th, and we got it done. But, in addition, there was vandalism.”

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want
News.content:
Liverpool 2 Monaco 3

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

News.title: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion
News.content:
Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho reveals he agreed to REPLACE Fergie at Man Utd before tearful phone call saw Special One return to Chelsea
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO has sensationally revealed he had agreed to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager.

But the Portuguese boss pulled out of the deal at the last minute and rang Sir Alex in tears to tell him the news.



Mourinho, 63, has opened up on the dramatic tale from 2013 during his new self-titled documentary that will premier on Netflix tomorrow.

And the Special One has explained how his “love” for Chelsea made him return to Stamford Bridge, when he could have got the United job ahead of David Moyes.



Speaking in his new doc, Mourinho said: “I go to Chelsea in 2013, but in that period there is something that nobody knows.

“I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth and I think the objective of this work we are doing is to tell the truth.



“When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.

“I was, of course, very flattered, because Man United has an incredible appeal.

“When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Man United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football and another thing is love for a certain club. I think this is more powerful than love for football.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“And, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I am loved.

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach that succeeded Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic.

“But I don’t regret it, because it was a decision that I made with my heart.

“And I think it is nature that says that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it is nature. I did it for love.”



Sir Alex was convinced that Mourinho would be following in his footsteps after the pair held talks.

The Special One was coming off the back of a turbulent three years at Real Madrid where he had fallen out with the dressing room.

Mourinho did, however, win LaLiga during his second season and beat Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona to the Copa del Rey the year before.

The Real Madrid boss eventually took charge of United in 2016, three years after Sir Alex thought he would be the man to directly succeed him.



Sir Alex said in the documentary: “He was offered the job, yes. I sat him down and explained the situation.

“And, as far as I was concerned, he was accepting. And then, within hours, it changed.

“Early evening, he phoned me and he was crying.

“And he says, ‘Alex, I cannot take it, I gave my word to Chelsea and I am not going to break my word.’

“The reason he gave to me I can understand, but I was disappointed.”

Sports.title: John Terry admits Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea once obtained training footage of Sam Allardyce’s BOLTON to boost title bid
Sports.content:
CHELSEA once obtained footage of Bolton training to help their Premier League title challenge.

Long before Southampton were caught out spying on Middlesbrough ahead of last season’s Championship play-offs, Jose Mourinho’s Blues were up to tricks of their own.



An interesting revelation from the new Netflix documentary is Mourinho’s use of video analysis.

Andre Villas-Boas, who would later go on to manage Chelsea and Tottenham, was in charge of that area.



AVB said: “That was the breakthrough in terms of match analysis. Not a lot of people were doing it to the extent that we were doing it at the time.

“It was the old times of the DVD players and sometimes the DVD player didn’t work, and Jose used to destroy the projector or the DVD player!”

One of the video sessions involved footage from Sam Allardyce’s Bolton training session ahead of Chelsea playing them.

Captain John Terry explained: “Big Sam is saying: ‘Hit Gallas, he’s not very good in the air’. He’s spitting and stuff like that on the mic.

“And it was just like – wow, who gets footage from someone’s training ground? I am actually still not sure where he got the footage from!”

Terry says he would have been prepared to be carried out in a “coffin” for former boss Mourinho.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

The pair spent five-and-a-half seasons together across two spells in a trophy-ladden period for Chelsea, winning three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup.

Terry recounts being ignored in the treatment room by the Portuguese because he was injured.

The defender’s response was to take an injection for the pain so that he could join training. The physio argued he was “mad”.

But Terry said: “For him, I would give everything. I would leave that pitch in a coffin for him.”



There was – Terry insists – a “soft side” to Mourinho and every Sunday players were told to bring their kids to the training ground.

The Special One would crack jokes with them and showcase a part of his personality many did not see.

Even with an influx of big names, the core of Mourinho’s Chelsea during his first spell were England duo Terry and Frank Lampard.

They were his lieutenants in the dressing room and former skipper Terry vividly recalls the mood among the squad.

Mourinho described the players like “an army going into battle”.



Terry said: “There was a picture of the Premier League up in the dressing room.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And there was a very clear mindset of: this is what we are going to win.

“From those first team meetings, to the very first game against Man United, the words and the terminology he would use in those meetings…like: ‘We are going to f*** them. We are going to win the league. We are going to take the trophy off them this year’.”

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho in pop at Pep Guardiola as Special One vows to NEVER take sabbatical and could manage into his SEVENTIES
Sports.content:
JOSE MOURINHO cannot imagine retiring and believes he could still be managing in his 70s.

And the Special One has had a pop at his old rival Pep Guardiola by ruling out ever taking a sabbatical.



Mourinho, 63, returned to Real Madrid this summer for a second spell and signed a three-year contract.

But the Portuguese has revealed in his new Netflix documentary, Mourinho, that he has plenty of fuel in the tank.



Speaking in the doc, Mourinho said: “I cannot even imagine when I am going to stop my life in football.

“I say 10 more years, but maybe more than 10. It’s fun. It was, it is and will always be fun.



“I want to win more titles. I want to win new titles. I want to repeat titles.

“I want to do it in places where I have never been. I want to do it in places where I did before.

“My world is to walk in a football stadium with 50,000 or 90,000 [fans]. I had 100,000. That is my world.

“Without football, there is not something complete in me.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“But I don’t think it is an obsession. I don’t feel it as an obsession.

“It is just when you reach a certain level, you want to stay there forever.”

Mourinho has been in management since 2000, when he was placed in charge of Benfica.

The Special One’s new doc charts his rise from there, including a fiery three years at Real Madrid from 2010 to 2013.



Mourinho repeatedly clashed with Guardiola, who was managing Barcelona, during that period.

Pep ended up taking a break from football after leaving Barca in 2012 and took up the reins at Bayern Munich a year later.

But Mourinho has vowed he will never do the same, as taking time out from coaching would be a sign of weakness.

He said: “Some guys, they need a sabbatical – which is something that I hate. I hate that word.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“For me, sabbatical means weakness. Don’t speak with me about sabbaticals.



“I never need a rest. I will have a rest when he (Mourinho points to the sky) decides to say: ‘Come up’.”

Sports.title: England ace Eberechi Eze launches plans to build 30 new homes – but locals aren’t happy
Sports.content:
THREE Lions hero Eberechi Eze has launched ambitious plans to build 30 new homes as he climbs up the Premier League property ladder.

The Arsenal midfielder has become a director of two companies set up to oversee the project on the edge of the West Sussex village of Horsted Keynes.



It comes after the 28-year-old won the league with Arsenal and helped England claim third place at this summer’s World Cup.

A source said: “Rather than simply investing in buy-to-let properties like many footballers, Eze has entered the far more ambitious world of residential development, taking control of a site with planning permission already in place.



“Football might be paying the bills today, but developments like this can end up making players wealthier than their careers ever did.”

Companies House records show Eze has established EZE10 Residential (Horsted Keynes) Limited and become a director of Macar Homes (Horsted Keynes) Limited alongside Surrey developer Alex MacDonald and his wife Rachael.

The site already has permission for 30 homes, ranging from one-bedroom flats to four-bedroom houses, including nine affordable properties.

But the scheme attracted more than 260 objections, with residents raising concerns over traffic, road safety, over-development and the loss of greenfield land.

Campaigners also warned it would mean felling mature trees and harm the character of the historic Sussex village.

Despite the objections, council planners concluded the benefits outweighed the concerns and granted permission.



The project marks one of the most ambitious property ventures undertaken by a current England international, following footballers including Robbie Fowler, Gary Neville and John Terry into property investment.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli ‘lined up for shock transfer to European giant after entering final year of contract’
Sports.content:
GABRIEL MARTINELLI could be on his way out of Arsenal this summer, according to reports.

The winger lost his place in the Gunners’ first team to Leandro Trossard last season, while Greek winger Christos Tzolis was signed this summer in a £34million deal from Club Brugge.



It has been widely expected Martinelli, 25, would depart for pastures new this summer, even after Trossard’s own exit to Turkish giants Besiktas.

But Martinelli could be set to follow the Belgian to the Turkish Super Lig.



That’s because, according to talkSPORT, reigning league champions Galatasaray have made an enquiry over his availability.

Galatasaray had been in talks to sign AC Milan outcast Rafael Leao and had earmarked Martinelli as an alternative option.



And they have now made contact with Arsenal over Martinelli’s status after failing to engineer a breakthrough in the Leao talks.

SunSport reported earlier in the window that if Martinelli was sold, he would be expected to depart for higher than the club’s current sale record of £35m paid by Liverpool for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

Whether Galatasaray are willing to stump up that sort of money remains to be seen, but it’s understood Arsenal will only sanction an exit for Martinelli if they can find a replacement.

The North London club had been in talks to sign Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, but saw that deal collapse when the Brazilian signed a new deal through to 2032.

However, SunSport looked at six alternative targets Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta could eye this window.

Among them were Paris Saint-Germain and France winger, Bradley Barcola – wanted by Liverpool but rated at £145m by his club – as well as Manchester United and England forward Marcus Rashford, and Athletic Bilbao and Spanish World Cup winner Nico Williams.

But reports have also suggested that Juventus‘ Kenan Yildiz, Atletico Madrid‘s Julian Alvarez, Everton‘s Iliman Ndiaye and Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi are all on their radar too.

A move for the latter star in that quartet seems very unlikely this summer given he is expected to miss at least four months following foot surgery he had at the end of July.

Sports.title: Embattled Gianni Infantino dealt fresh humiliation as local Swiss club snubs chance to back him
Sports.content:
SHAMED footie fatcat Gianni Infantino’s local club have refused to back his leadership of Fifa.

Zug 94, based in the luxury Swiss lakeside town where the embattled £4.8million-a-year chief has a penthouse flat, declined to endorse him.



It comes as Europe’s football governing body, Uefa, considers launching an investigation into his 16-year career there.

Infantino yesterday denied claims made by The Daily Telegraph that Uefa paid off an alleged mistress while he was the organisation’s general secretary.



A Fifa spokesman said he “strongly denies the allegations, and they are categorically untrue”.

It called the allegations part of a “concerted effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president”.

Uefa confirmed a departure payment had been made to the unnamed woman, whose salary was said to have been raised at married father Infantino’s request.

Infantino could be challenged in next March’s Fifa presidential election after Football Associations of several nations, including England and Wales, withdrew their endorsements.

Zug 94, who play in the Swiss fourth division and have an average attendance of 400, also dodged offering its backing.

When asked by The Sun if Zug 94 supported Infantino’s continued leadership, a club spokesman said: “We will refrain from commenting on this matter.”



Infantino switched his tax residency from Zurich to Zug in 2022.

He has a £6,500-a-month penthouse apartment overlooking Lake Zug in the Swiss tax haven.

Fifa pays his rent.

Sports.title: WAGs should be offered counselling by clubs because of struggles with trolls, other women & their partners, study finds
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL clubs should offer counselling to the wives and girlfriends of players, the first study on Wags concludes.

The likes of Becky Vardy and Coleen Rooney might need help because of all they deal with, it is claimed.



Researchers at Leeds Beckett University — who spoke to seven women — found that being a Wag could be an “invasive force that could threaten or harm their identity and self-esteem”.

The Wags, aged between 23 and 34, told of their struggles to deal with online trolls, other women, and their own partners.



One said: “I know girls who sleep with football players and then take their watches or ask for a payout, so they don’t tell their wives.”

Others told of death threats over their appearance.

Another added: “There’s an added pressure of being a partner of a player, 100 per cent.”

They all spoke of their own needs having to “take a back seat” for the men.

The researchers found the Wags played a “critical yet under-recognised role in player well-being and performance”.

However, they said that clubs rarely considered their welfare was important.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Everton in stunning transfer talks over incredible swap involving Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil
Sports.content:
CRYSTAL PALACE and Everton are in talks over swapping Brennan Johnson and Dwight McNeil.

Both players are thought to be keen on moving and the deal will not involve a fee.



Toffees winger McNeil, 26, nearly joined the Eagles on a loan-to-buy in February but the switch collapsed.

Johnson, 25, has had a torrid time at Selhurst Park since his £35million arrival from Tottenham in January, failing to score in 26 games.



The Wales wideman did, however, lift the Conference League.

It was his second European title in two years, having scored the winner for Spurs against Manchester United in the Europa League final 12 months earlier.

McNeil has played more than 100 games for Everton following his move from Burnley four years ago.

The Toffees have signed Hayden Hackney and Tyrique George for £24m from Middlesbrough and Chelsea respectively as well as Merlin Rohl from Freiburg for £19m.

The Toffees also saw key figures getting released, like Seamus Coleman and Idrissa Gueye.

Palace, on the other hand, landed free agents Oscar Mingueza and Takehiro Tomiyasu.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United

Jose Mourinho has spoken for the first time about backing out of a contract to originally join Manchester United following Alex Ferguson by returning to Chelsea

View 3 Images Mourinho was meant to come to United years earlier than he did (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Jose Mourinho has revealed he signed a contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson as Manchester United manager in 2013 only to tearfully go back on the deal and return to Chelsea.

‌



The Scottish great rocked the football world when he announced he was retiring having overseen a 13th Premier League title triumph win during a spell of unrivalled dominance at Old Trafford.

‌



Since then, United have failed to return to the top of the English game, with successor David Moyes sacked after only 10 months in charge.

‌



View 3 Images Ferguson revealed in the documentary he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

In 2016 Mourinho joined the club for two and a half years, but in his new Netflix documentary he revealed he had come to an agreement to take charge of United earlier.

“I go to Chelsea in 2013 but in that period there is something nobody knows,” the Portuguese said in ‘Mourinho’.

‌



“I think I can say because I don’t hurt anyone with the truth, and I think the objective of this work that we are doing is to tell the truth.

“When I left Real Madrid, I signed with Manchester United to go to Manchester United after Sir Alex.”

Mourinho added: “I was, of course, very flattered, because Manchester United has an incredible appeal.

‌



“When I say Real Madrid is the biggest club in the world, I have to say that Manchester United is very, very close.

“But one thing is love for football, and another thing is love for a certain club.

“I think this is more powerful than love for football and, fundamentally, after Real Madrid, I needed to feel that I’m loved.”

‌



Ferguson was one of the footballing figures interviewed for the new documentary and admits he was under the illusion Mourinho was accepting the offer, only for the situation to change in a matter of hours.

View 3 Images Mourinho revealed his decision in his Netflix documentary (Image: Cr. Courtesy of Netflix © 2026)

“Early evening he phoned me and he was crying,” the United great said. “And he says, ‘Alex, I can’t take it – I’ve given my word to Chelsea, and I’m not going to break my word’.

‌



“The reason he gave to me I could understand, but I was disappointed.”

Mourinho had a strong bond with Chelsea after leading them to two Premier League titles, an FA Cup and two League Cups during an unforgettable first spell.

The Portuguese parked differences with owner Roman Abramovich to return to Stamford Bridge after leaving Real Madrid, winning another league crown and League Cup before being sacked in December 2015.

Article continues below

“For me to lose the chance to be the coach to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson was dramatic, but I don’t regret because it was a decision that I made with my heart,” Mourinho, now back in charge of Real Madrid, said.

“And I think it is nature that says something that when you do something for love, you are never doing anything wrong. I think it’s nature. I did it for love.

“I went back with the feeling of, yes, I go home, but with big responsibility because what I did before is history, and you don’t want to destroy your legacy.”

Sports.title: Kyle Walker relishing Championship challenge with Burnley - 'I am not becoming anyone's meme'
Sports.content:
It may be more than 15 years since Kyle Walker last graced the Championship, but his mentality hasn't changed.

The veteran defender has not played in the second tier of English football since the 2010-11 campaign, where he briefly starred in the resolute QPR team that would go on to win the league under Neil Warnock. Back then, at the age of 20, Walker was a young prospect with his whole career ahead of him. He returns to the Championship as one of the most decorated right-back's in English football with 96 caps for his country, six Premier League titles and a Champions League triumph all to his name.

But motivation will not be an issue despite all he has accomplished as he prepares for what will be his first ever full campaign in the Championship following Burnley's relegation.

"I think if I have to get motivated to play football, I should stay in bed in the morning," Walkers says. "It's a job that I'm doing that millions want to do. So if you're not motivated to play football and don't win games, I'm definitely in the wrong job."

‌



Walker turned 36 in May but insists the physical demands of an unforgiving 46-game season in the Championship is no cause for concern. He says his physical powers have not waned, attributing his "genetic gifts" to mum and dad.

Former Premier League star punished under new rule days after completing £20m transfer READ MORE :

After amassing an abundance of accolades in the game, Walker already knows he will be a target for ambitious wingers looking to make a name for themselves. But while Walker accepts he will be a scalp, he is adamant nobody will be turning him into a meme.

"I think they try to create, what is it called, memes now? They’ll try and create memes out of me and I can assure you that I am not becoming anyone’s meme," Walker says.

"So when you come against me, I'll give it 100 percent. If you beat me on the day, you know, you shake hands at the end of the game, and you say it's a good game. I'm not rolling out anything to become a meme."

‌



Walker was earmarked for greatness long before he had a chance to truly get to grips with the relentless cut and thrust of the Championship; Tottenham snapped him up from his boyhood club, Sheffield United, in the summer of 2009 after just a handful of senior appearances.

A return to his beloved Bramall Lane followed in the form of a loan spell but it was his temporary stint at QPR which was the catalyst for the trophy-laden career Walker has gone on to enjoy.

"Playing in the Championship - it grounds you, but it also teaches you. It can be very humbling as well," he adds, referencing the wealth of experience that inhabited said QPR dressing room.

View 4 Images Burnley were relegated from the Premier League last season (Image: Alex Livesey)

‌



"We had a very good team. Neil Warnock took me and I played every game and then I went to Aston Villa for the last part of the season. I fell back in love with football a bit - I wouldn’t say I’d fallen out of love - but I went on loan from Tottenham, got called back and didn't really play as many games as I wanted. And then Harry [Redknapp] let me go back [out] on loan to get some games under my belt.

"I loved it. I probably didn’t want to leave to go to Aston Villa because I was playing football and winning every game, but it was something that I needed to do personally to make that step up to the Premier League."

From there, the Sheffield-born defender never looked back. Months later he won his first senior England cap. He then became a staple in the Tottenham team before a blockbuster transfer to Manchester City, where Walker acquired his taste for silverware.

After eight seasons in sky blue, Walker left City permanently last year with 15 major trophies to his name in order to embark on a new challenge with Burnley; a move which presented Walker with an opportunity to escape the 'noise' that becomes a non-negotiable extra for those who operate at the truly elite level.

‌



He explains: "The scrutiny is not as big, but I think then you probably scrutinise yourself more because you’re so used to achieving and winning a lot more games. You look back at yourself and think ‘What could I have done?’.

"Last season, most of all, it was about the mental game. I can play the game of football; that didn’t stop just because I went to Burnley. But mentally it was different and something that I had to channel into. But then that’s something I can pass onto the younger players now and hopefully give my experience."

View 4 Images Burnley and Wolves will both bid to make an instant return to the Premier League along with West Ham (Image: Matt McNulty)

As Walker alludes to, after almost a decade at a club where success has become almost synonymous, last year was a different experience altogether. The beleaguered Clarets suffered a death by a thousand cuts, winning just four Premier League games all season.

‌



There is an "obligation" for he and those who have stayed at the club to right the wrongs of that chastening campaign, says Walker, who adds that relegation has left a "sour taste" in the mouth.

While some have moved on, he had no qualms about returning to the level that helped truly elevate his career, even if a Championship encore was not on his footballing bucket list.

"It’s our job," he says. "Things aren’t always going to go as planned. This season might not go as planned. It might not be as plain sailing as we all want it to be. But I feel with the quality, what we have in the dressing room, that’s what we should be doing: getting promoted and going back to the Premier League."

Nicky Hayen has been tasked with achieving that feat following a protracted manager search earlier this summer. The Belgian previously impressed with Genk and Walker's first impressions of the 45-year-old have been positive.

‌



"He has been great," says Walker of Hayen. "The information he has given is key, he is very direct and I feel when a manager comes in they can give you sometimes too much information."

Burnley have immediately been installed as one of the favourites for promotion and Hayen will harbour ambitions of emulating the feats overseen by Vincent Kompany. Walker's former Manchester City team-mate masterminded a memorable promotion campaign for Burnley back in 2022-23, losing just three games and racking up an impressive 101 points.

View 4 Images Walker has picked the brains of his former Manchester City team-mate and Burnley manager, Vincent Kompany (Image: Nathan Stirk)

Walker has already picked the brains of the Bayern Munich boss, revealing: "I've spoken to Vinny, I've got words from him. How did he find it after achieving what he’s achieved? He says it’s difficult. It is something that is going to be attached to yourself personally [the expectation to win] but it is also very enjoyable.

‌



"You become a big fish again, and you get a little bit more of the ball, and it's a bit more of the game that I'm used to playing at Manchester City.

"So, hopefully, we can replicate that for when Vinny went up because I think they broke 100 points and kind of tore the Championship apart."

Now in the twilight years of his career, Walker argued that staying up last season would have been equivalent to a seventh Premier League title. That wasn't to be, but a Championship crown would go some way to quenching Walker's insatiable thirst for more achievements.

"There's always losing in football and there's always achieving in football," Walker says. "All the time I've got a football shirt on my back, I'll always give my all and I won't settle for anything less. I've got a bar for myself, but I've also got a bar more importantly for the team, and if anyone falls underneath that, then they will be told that it's not acceptable.

‌



"But hopefully, from what I've seen in pre-season, what I've seen in training, and obviously from the manager and everything like that, we're all going in the same direction — and that's to get this club back to the Premier League."

Sports.title: Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future
Sports.content:
Man Utd decide on giving Marcus Rashford new shirt number in clear hint on future

Marcus Rashford is preparing to make a return to Manchester United after more than 18 months away and, after having his No 10 shirt given to Matheus Cunha, has been given a new number

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is looking to force his way back into Man Utd's first-team picture (Image: Getty)

Manchester United are ready to hand Marcus Rashford a new squad number which serves as the biggest hint yet that he's going to remain part of Michael Carrick's plans.

‌



The forward has just returned to Old Trafford following the end of his loan spell at Barcelona, who opted against signing the Englishman on a permanent deal. Prior to that he'd been on loan at Aston Villa after being frozen out by Ruben Amorim.

‌



During his 18-month-plus spell away from Manchester Rashford's No 10 shirt was given to Matheus Cunha, which cast doubt over where Rashford's future lied.

‌



But the 28-year-old is now back in the fold at United and been handed the No 14 shirt. That shirt had been vacated by Christian Eriksen and will now be taken on by Rashford.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer READ MORE :

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Carrick confirmed that Rashford, who has been afforded an extended break following his involvement with England at the World Cup, would be back with the group ahead of their pre-season trip to Dublin, where United will play Leeds at Croke Park.

The new United boss said on the forward: “I’ve played with him. I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history. We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together. Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie [Mainoo] and Lisandro [Martínez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

‌



United are ready to bring Rashford into the first-team environment and, unless a top European club comes in with a notable offer, he will be remaining at Old Trafford, according to Fabrizio Romano.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been Marcus Rashford's team-mate and also coached him at Man Utd (Image: 2020 Soccrates Images B.V.)

Rashford remains United's top earner on more than £300,000-a-week, which would complicate any sale given the salary demands a buyer would need to stomach.

Article continues below

Rashford scored 14 times last season for the Spanish giants and returns to a team who have continued to bolster their forward line. Last summer they spent £200million on Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. They were all key in the team's rise last season whilst Amad Diallo and Patrick Dorgu are also competition for Rashford.

Man Utd in driving seat to beat Arsenal and Aston Villa to wonderkid transfer

Manchester United, Arsenal and Aston Villa are embroiled in a three-horse race for a highly-touted teenage wonderkid this summer

View Image Louis Page played for Leicester City in the Carabao Cup on Saturday. (Image: Plumb Images/Leicester City FC via Getty Images)

Manchester United are involved in negotiations with Leicester City for Louis Page. However, they will face stiff competition from Arsenal and Aston Villa in their pursuit.

‌



The 18-year-old is thought highly of at the King Power Stadium, as the Foxes brace for his imminent departure as a result of relegation to League One. Having only joined Leicester's first-team last summer, the youngster was awarded the EFL's apprentice of the year award in 2025/26.

‌

‌

While names such as Aurelien Tchouameni, Alex Scott and Carlos Baleba have all previously been mentioned, it appears as though the Red Devils are looking for a youngster to develop at Old Trafford.

Page came off the bench during the second half of the club's 1-0 Carabao Cup victory over Northampton Town on Saturday. Having come through the ranks at the Midlands outfit, he made his senior debut just under a year ago in the Carabao Cup, going on to rack up a total of 22 first-team appearances throughout last season.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star and current transfer target both sent off in pre-season brawl
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star and current transfer target both sent off in pre-season brawl

The pre-season friendly between Bournemouth and Real Batis saw three red cards shown just before half time.

View 2 Images Both Antony and Alex Scott were sent off during the pre-season friendly. (Image: Fran Santiago/Getty Images))

AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott was one of three people sent off during the pre-season friendly against Real Betis on Saturday. The England international was involved in an argument with former Manchester United man Antony, who was also shown a red card.

‌



The two teams met in Spain as they prepare for the new season. But an incident just before the half time whistle means that both teams would play the rest of the game with 10 men.

‌



It unfolded with Real Betis' Nelson Edossa reacting to a foul from Bournemouth defender Bafode Diakate. The Real Betis man kicked the ball at the Cherries' player from close range, which prompted a response from other Bournemouth players. That's when Antony got involved.

‌



Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow READ MORE :

PSG move could hand Marcus Rashford last-gasp Man Utd transfer with Barcelona reunion READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

After joining the melee, he became embroiled in a shoving match with Scott, resulting in both players receiving straight red cards from the referee. At that stage, Bournemouth were leading 1-0, but with each team down to 10 men, they eventually shared the spoils in a 2-2 draw.

It emerged at the interval that new Bournemouth manager Marco Rose had also been shown a red card during half time, forcing him to observe the second half from the press box.

‌



United may well have been monitoring the heated exchange closely, given the club's reported transfer interest in Scott during the current window. The Bournemouth midfielder has been identified as one of several potential options for United as they seek to bolster that area of the pitch.

View 2 Images Bournemouth midfieler Alex Scott was shown a red card during the pre-season friendly. (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

However, they face stiff competition from Chelsea, who have already had a bid rejected. The Blues are reported to have tabled an offer of £64million for the England international, but the Cherries remain firmly in the 'not for sale' camp.

‌



Michael Carrick has already bolstered his midfield options this summer with the signings of both Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. United are eager to bring in a third midfield reinforcement before the transfer window slams shut.

Alongside Scott, the club have been linked with potential moves for Aurelien Tchouameni, Manu Kone and Carlos Baleba.

Antony, meanwhile, struggled to leave his mark during his three years at United. He arrived from Ajax in 2022, netting 12 goals in 96 appearances, before heading to Real Betis on loan in January 2025.

Article continues below

He won over the hearts of supporters at the Spanish club and sealed a permanent departure from Old Trafford last summer.

Sports.title: Brennan secures FedEx Cup Playoffs spot with Wyndham Championship win
Sports.content:
Michael Brennan secured his place in the FedExCup Playoffs as he won the Wyndham Championship by three strokes from Beau Hossler.

Brennan had a run of five straight birdies between the fourth and eighth holes, and recovered from a bogey on the 11th by picking up further shots on the 13th and 18th holes, saving par on the 17th with an excellent second shot after running into the rough with his tee-shot.

Hossler, who shared the overnight lead with Brennan, had kept himself in touch with a birdie on the third and an eagle at the par-five fifth, but then bogeyed the ninth and 12th holes as Brennan surged forward.

"I did great for nine holes," Brennan said. "I felt really good on the front nine. Just playing my game, I was really staying within myself, hitting good shots.

"Felt like I was really in control. Got a little nervous around 10 and 11. I made a really nice par putt on 12 and that kind of steadied me a little bit going through and I'm just glad to make a few putts coming in.

"It's everything. I mean, I don't want to be done playing golf. I feel like I've played the best golf I have all year the last couple weeks.

"Unfortunately, a couple tough Sundays, but outside of that, I've been playing really solidly. This is my sixth week in a row and so seven's a lot, but I think I'm going to be perfectly happy running on fumes next week."

England's Harry Hall finished with a round of 65 to take a share of fifth place, one shot clear of compatriot Matt Wallace who had a share of seventh after he also closed with a 65.

Sports.title: Rahm reigns again after Niemann wins LIV Golf New York
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm clinched the LIV Golf season points title for a third straight year despite finishing tied for 41st at LIV Golf New York, where Joaquin Niemann claimed a three-shot victory for his ninth win in the last three years.

Rahm shot 76 in the final round, but it was still enough for the two-time major champion to secure the season crown for the third successive year since joining LIV Golf.

"The last two weeks haven't been the best, have they," Rahm said. "I would say proud of earlier in the season.

"To start off as well as I did with a few second places and not getting the win and then going to Hong Kong and getting it done when I needed to, having a lead and then basically losing it and birdieing four in a row in the last few holes was probably the most proud moment.

"It's been great. It's been a great year. Again, a little sour taste in my mouth because of how badly I played this week. But it's been something to be proud of.

"After last year and not getting the win, having possibly a question mark over the season-long race, to win twice and do it effectively and win it again definitely feels good."

Sports.title: 'Very pathetic' - Koepka fumes after missing FedExCup Playoffs
Sports.content:
Brooks Koepka labelled missing the FedExCup Playoffs "pathetic" in a brutally honest assessment of his game after a low finish at the Wyndham Championship.

The five-time major champion, back on the PGA Tour after a four-year hiatus with LIV Golf, posted a final-round 70 at Sedgefield Country Club on Sunday.

Koepka was tied for 70th when his round finished, way short of the fourth-place finish he needed to secure qualification for next week's St Jude Championship.

"I struck the ball great," Koepka explained. "It's just all on the greens. I don't know what the deal is.

"Got zero confidence, can't putt. I don't know. There's going to be a lot of changes here soon."

Asked to sum up his disappointment at missing the playoffs, Koepka didn't hold back, adding: "Pretty disappointed. I think it's pretty pathetic that I can't get through.

"Zero top-10s basically in two years. To be in the prime of my career and be as good as I think I am, I think that's very pathetic, disappointing.

"I just need to go home and completely re-evaluate everything."

Sports.title: Stokes fires Durham to One-Day Cup victory over Essex in Gay's absence
Sports.content:
Ben Stokes made a quickfire 43 to help Durham to a 20-run victory over Essex in their One-Day Cup Group B match at Darlington despite the absence of England Test opener Emilio Gay.

In a match reduced to 38 overs a side by early morning rain, Durham were put in to bat by Essex and fell to 30-3.

But former England captain Stokes hit 43 off 27 balls, hitting five fours and two sixes, before Colin Ackermann added an unbeaten 80 that helped them post 229-5.

Essex opener Noah Thain made 76 but the visitors lost the rest of their top order cheaply, and were bowled out for 209.

Gay sat out the match as a precaution after retiring hurt in Friday's loss to Middlesex.

Elsewhere, Jake Libby's fourth century in as many One-Day Cup outings was not enough for Worcestershire as Glamorgan snatched a two-wicket victory off the last ball at Cardiff.

Libby extended his outstanding run as the Worcestershire skipper made 105 off 114 balls in his side's 278-9.

Glamorgan were quickly reduced to 46-3 in reply but Callum Rhys Nicholls (70) and Jack Hope-Bell (58) reversed the trend and captain Andy Gorvin found the boundary from the last ball of the game to snatch the win.

Group B leaders Middlesex eased to an 87-run win over Derbyshire on the back of a 156-run third-wicket partnership between Max Holden (65) and Ben Geddes (109).

Hampshire openers Ali Orr (105) and Ben Mayes (109) put on 225 for the first wicket in their 51-run win over Sussex.

A superb unbeaten 133 from Daniel Bell-Drummond powered Kent to a six-wicket win over Group A leaders Leicestershire to keep their hopes of progress alive.

Nottinghamshire could not take advantage of Leicestershire's loss as Gloucestershire beat them by four wickets with five balls remaining at Cheltenham despite captain Haseeb Hameed's 85.

Luke Procter also made 85 as Northamptonshire secured a seven-wicket victory over Somerset at Wantage Road while Warwickshire secured a two-wicket win over Lancashire.

Sports.title: Samangan stars in Prix Maurice de Gheest
Sports.content:
Samangan gave Francis-Henri Graffard another Group One success with victory in the ARC Prix Maurice de Gheest at Deauville.

Always close to the pace-setting Afandy over the intermediate six-and-a-half-furlong trip, the Aga Khan Studs-owned Samangan battled through the final quarter-mile to master Stolen Kiss and just found the post coming in time to foil the William Haggas-trained Division, who flashed home under James Doyle.

The winner had been fourth in the Prix Jean Prat last time out in which True Love was second, but comprehensively reversed form with the Ballydoyle Classic heroine on this occasion.

Nemone Routh, racing manager for the owners in France, told Sky Sports Racing: "He's a lovely horse, he's very genuine. He was always going to follow Afandy and then he was really brave.

"He could (go to Ascot on Champions Day), but I think he's better on good, firm ground, that's another thing we've found this year. I think if it got too soft he wouldn't go there. He's a relaxed horse and he can get seven (furlongs). It all depends on the ground."

Graffard added: "I am very pleased for the stable. He is a colt we have always held in high regard. Things did not go as planned at the beginning of the season, but he also needed to gain experience.

"His previous races have toughened him up and this victory is the result of the experience he has been able to acquire.

"His next target could be the Qatar Prix de la Foret, provided the ground is not too testing for him. He is a Group One winner and exceptionally well bred, so he has earned his place at stud as a stallion. My job is done!"

Distant Storm boosted star three-year-old milers Bow Echo and Gstaad as he made a winning reappearance in the Prix Daphnis.

Third to Bow Echo in the 2000 Guineas at Newmarket before finding only Gstaad too good in the Irish equivalent, Charlie Appleby's colt had been off since that run at the Curragh.

Returning to the track in Group Three company, Billy Loughnane's mount was a little tight for room before getting out to give chase to well-backed Italian raider Grand Son Of Dark.
