World.title: Jamaica’s Edwards snatches triple jump gold at World U20 Champs
World.content:
In this March 2026 file photo, Jamaica College star Michael-Andre Edwards displays his gold medal after winning the Class 1 Boys’ triple jump final, with a leap of 16.25m., to close out his Champs career. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

OREGON, USA – Michael Andre Edwards thought he would be able to jump “about 16.80m” but surprised himself with a dramatic final round 17.08m (1.1m/s) leap to snatch the gold medal at the World Athletics Under- 20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Edwards, who started slowly, trailed his good friend American Miles Nesmith going into the final round, when he produced the jump of his life on the biggest stage.

After his dramatic win, he said he never expected he would be jumping this far this soon but never thought 17.00m was out of his reach.

He twice bettered his previous personal best of 16.30m set in July, with 16.71m in the fifth round and then his big jump a round later. He joins national under-20 record holder Jaydon Hibbert,17.87m, and James Beckford, 17.29m, as the only Jamaican juniors to jump over 17.00m in the triple jump.

Edwards is also the second Jamaican man to win the triple jump after Hibbert won it in 2022.

This was Jamaica’s first gold of the champions and third medal after Gary Card and Shanoya Douglas won silver medals in their respective 100m finals on Thursday.

Nesmith, who was second to Edwards at the Penn Relays in April, took the silver medal with a personal best 16.79m (1.0m/s) and China’s Zhuoyue Wang was third with 16.36m (0.9m/s).

Edwards, who needed just one jump, 16.00m, to qualify from the prelims, started slowly with a 13.76m (1.4m/s) but qualified for the final with a 16.23m (-0.3m/s) in the third round before he got into second place with 16.71 (0.5m/s) in the fifth round.

-Paul A Reid

World.title: Why Poland’s right-wing split may not save Tusk
World.content:
However, the departure of former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki from PiS complicates the balance of balance of power on the right.

PiS, which ruled from 2015 to 2023, formally ruptured last month, when Morawiecki stormed out, taking 40 MPs with him to form the new Development Plus party, leaving PiS with 147 deputies.

The split between him and party founder and leader Jarosław Kaczyński quickly became acrimonious.

Morawiecki criticized his own government’s decisions on Covid-19 restrictions and its push to tighten Poland’s abortion law, which outraged many women and saw PiS take a long-term hit in public support.

“Although I oppose abortion, I believed the change would lead to catastrophe — a polling collapse. Unfortunately, I was right,” Morawiecki said on the popular YouTube show Rymanowski Live this week.

He is now trying to set up a more moderate center-right party focused on economic growth which is less partisan than PiS. “Today, Poland does not need to get bogged down in ideological disputes,” he said in Monday’s interview. However, he has ruled out ever working with Tusk in the future.

World.title: A new rival is forcing Italy’s Meloni back to her far-right roots
World.content:
While France and other countries tightened border checks, Italy went further and announced it had suspended the EU’s free-movement Schengen agreement with Madrid. Now, in Italian airports, passengers from Spain are asked to join a different line.

Meloni’s office has made clear it has no intention of lifting the controls until at least Aug. 15, escalating the clash with Spain, which retaliated by imposing checks on travelers from Italy.

“We will not back down one millimeter on illegal immigration,” Meloni posted on X while her allies attacked the socialist Spanish government, accusing it of failing to manage migration flows. “Defending our borders, stopping human traffickers, and ensuring effective repatriation will continue to be this government’s policy,” she added.

The clash with Spain is just the latest sign that the Italian leader is doing all she can to secure her core, hard-right electorate in the face of a challenge from the right by Roberto Vannacci, a former general and member of the European Parliament.

With an election expected as early as next spring, Vannacci’s far-right National Future party has been advancing in the polls, overtaking one of Meloni’s coalition partners, the far-right League party, and gaining on another, Forza Italia, according to POLITICO’s Poll of Polls.

For Meloni, who began her political career in the youth wing of Italy’s post-fascist movement, the challenge strikes particularly close to home.

World.title: Israel rejects Trump’s peace plan for Gaza
World.content:
Hamas has said that it would begin disarming, but in recent days an Israeli official said the country still had “serious security concerns.”

The rejection is a blow to peace negotiations the Trump administratoin has been brokering since September. The U.S. president had described the plan, now rejected by Israel, as a “critical step towards Gaza finally being governed by a new Palestinian government” and giving Israel “the security it deserves.”

Israel appears unlikely to pull back significant forces or make other concessions ahead of legislative elections scheduled for October. Netanyahu faces a tough reelection battle, with his far-right coalition partners urging him to keep up the pressure on Hamas and leave forces in Gaza. Opponents also accuse him of failing to prevent the Oct. 7, 2023, attack when Hamas-led militants attacked Israeli communities, killing about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 others hostage. Israel responded with a punishing military offensive that has killed more than 73,000 people, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.

Netanyahu said on Sunday that he is now in discussions with U.S. officials about how to move forward. “They have ideas, some of which are acceptable to us and some of which are unacceptable to us, and we know how to stand up to these things,” he said.

World.title: Russia and Ukraine exchange overnight strikes, WHO confirms warehouse destroyed
World.content:
Another overnight strike on the Zhytomyr region injured three people, Ukrainian emergency services said.

Meanwhile, five people died in a Ukrainian overnight drone attack on the Russian city of Belgorod, the regional crisis centre said on Sunday. Acting governor Alexander Shuvayev said earlier on Sunday that three people were killed and 25 others injured in the “massive terrorist drone attack” by Kyiv. The death toll later rose to five.

Zelenskyy condemned what he described as “ballistic terror” attacks on Odesa, Kharkiv, Pavlohrad, and other regions. “Every such attack on human life serves as a constant reminder – we need more pressure, more sanctions against Russia, and more air defense for Ukraine,” he said.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director-general of the World Health Organization, said on Sunday that a WHO warehouse in Dnipro in Ukraine was destroyed by a strike on Friday.

The warehouse held humanitarian supplies for frontline health facilities. No casualties were reported, as a WHO staff member and drivers managed to evacuate 130 of approximately 300 pallets and left the area before the attack.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros said.

World.title: Germany battling ‘daily’ hybrid warfare attacks, minister warns
World.content:
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt speaks to the media during a news conference at Leipzig airport on Aug. 5, 2026. | Jens Schlueter/Getty Images

Last week’s drone incident in Lepizig just the latest example.

Germany is being hit by hybrid warfare attacks from foreign powers on a “daily” basis, the country’s interior minister has warned, after a drone packed with explosives was found at Leipzig Airport earlier this week.

Espionage, sabotage, cyber attacks and covert actions “with the aim of destabilizing Germany or directly harming it” are a “constant reality,” German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told BILD in an interview on Sunday.

Dobrindt suggested on Thursday that a drone incident at Leipzig Airport may have been an attack by a state actor. The minister has stopped short of specifying which foreign powers are behind the hybrid attacks.

World.title: Magyar’s party backs former supreme court head for Hungarian president
World.content:
The Hungarian Parliament is set to vote on András Baka's candidacy next Tuesday. | Tibor Illyes/EPA

Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s ruling Tisza party said on Saturday that it had nominated former Supreme Court President András Baka to become the country’s next president.

Baka, who worked as a judge on the European Court of Human Rights before being elected to head the Supreme Court, was removed from his post by the Fidesz government in 2011 — a move the ECHR ruled was unlawful.

“Throughout his career, Dr. András Baka has considered the principle of the separation of powers to be of paramount importance and has consistently stood up for the rule of law and judicial independence,” Tisza said in a Facebook post.

World.title: Sánchez-Meloni clash brings back borders — and headaches for tourists
World.content:
Madrid has pushed back forcefully against that narrative, and noted that the migrants could not leave the North African territory because they lack valid IDs required to travel on ferries to mainland Europe.

Spanish authorities and the European Commission this week confirmed that none of the 72,000 people who surged into Ceuta have crossed the Strait of Gibraltar. During a meeting of EU interior ministers on Tuesday, Italian Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi publicly praised Spain for its handling of the situation and expressed Rome’s “sincere solidarity” with Madrid.

Yet despite requests from Madrid, the Italian government has declined to end border checks even after it became clear that there was no risk of the Ceuta crisis spilling into the rest of Europe. Rome’s inaction prompted Spain to issue a statement on Friday threatening to adopt “proportional measures” if Rome did not change course by Aug. 9.

After Meloni’s office responded by declaring “Italy does not accept ultimatums or demands from abroad regarding national security and border control,” Madrid moved to reintroduce its own controls.

Magnus Brunner, the European commissioner for internal affairs and migration, sought to mediate in the dispute.

“I was in contact with both the Spanish and Italian Interior Ministers today. Both confirmed that the internal border controls are temporary,” Brunner said in a post on X. “I stressed the progress we’ve made on tackling illegal migration and that trust between Member States is our most valuable currency.”

World.title: Don Nelson, the second-winnigest head coach in NBA history, dies aged 86
World.content:
Don Nelson, the second-winningest coach in NBA history, who won five championships as a player with the Boston Celtics, died on Sunday at the age of 86.

 

His death was announced by the Golden State Warriors, one of the teams he coached post-retirement across two stints, the first from 1988-95 and then again from 2006-10.

Nelson is one of two coaches in NBA history to have at least 250 wins with three different franchises — Milwaukee, Dallas and Golden State — also serving as general manager for all three franchises.

He was a three-time coach of the year and made the playoffs 18 times in 31 seasons as head coach. He went to the conference finals on three different occasions with the Milwaukee Bucks and once with the Dallas Mavericks, never winning a title.

Nelson introduced what is now known as the point forward, an unorthodox basketball role where a forward—usually a small forward—takes on the playmaking and ball-handling duties of a point guard.

His up-tempo style of offence created a buzz, notably saying that the idea of shifting from the dominant big men of the 1970s to an offence focused on speed and the fast break came from his playing days under Celtics Hall of Fame coach Red Auerbach.

“The league really hadn’t seen an offence like the one we were running, and the results were undeniable,” Nelson wrote in 2016 in The Players’ Tribune.

The legendary coach and player played 11 of his 14 seasons in Boston and was on five Celtics championship teams under four different coaches. He became an assistant coach in Milwaukee after retiring as a player, then took over after coach Larry Costello resigned 18 games into the 1976-77 season.

Nelson coached the Bucks for 11 seasons starting in 1976 and won seven straight division titles. In Nelson’s second season, Milwaukee overcame a 29-point fourth quarter deficit to beat Atlanta 117-115 in regulation time.

At Golden State, Nelson’s “We Believe” Warriors led by Baron Davis upset Nowitzki and the top-seeded Mavericks in the first round of the 2007 playoffs in one of the biggest shockers in NBA history. In his final season as a coach, Nelson mentored rookie Stephen Curry in 2009-10 season.

“One of the big reasons I was drafted by the Warriors was because of Don Nelson. The story is he never liked rookies, but from Day 1 he challenged me and gave me an opportunity to be my best self on the court,” Curry said in a statement released by the Warriors.

FILE - Golden State Warrior's head coach Don Nelson directs the win over the New Jersey Nets 111-79 at Oracle Arena in Oakland, California, on Friday January 22, 2010 AP Photo, Michael Macor/San Francisco Chronicle, file

“He taught me a lot during our one season together and I’ll never forget the night he became the winningest coach in NBA history in Minnesota. We were so happy for him. He had an immeasurable impact on the sport and will go down as one of the greatest minds in the history of the game.”

Nelson retired as the NBA’s career coaching wins leader with 1,335, just ahead of Lenny Wilkens’ 1,332. Nelson kept that top spot for nearly 12 years before close friend and now-retired San Antonio coach Gregg Popovich passed him in March 2022.

He was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2012. In 2025 he received the Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award, presented by the National Basketball Coaches Association.

World.title: 'Ceuta is Spain': Hundreds of people protest Spanish government's response efforts over migrant influx crisis
World.content:
The four religious communities in Ceuta — Christian, Muslim, Jewish and Hindu — brought together hundreds of people in Constitution Square on Sunday afternoon to demand solutions to the migrant crisis and defend coexistence in the city.

 

The protest, held under the slogan "Enough is enough, Ceuta will not surrender", was marked by criticism of the government in Madrid, which some protesters accused of "abandonment".

"Ceuta is not for sale. Ceuta is Spain" and "Sánchez, resign" were among the chants heard from the crowd. Some protesters later continued the demonstration with a march towards the Government Delegation in the city.

Meanwhile, tensions flared in Plaza de los Reyes when Spanish far-right political activist Vito Quiles arrived, with some people in the crowd accusing him of coming to “divide” Ceuta’s residents.

The crisis has also fuelled political tensions over Spain’s decision to temporarily reinstate controls at ports and airports for travellers arriving from Italy, after Rome refused to lift controls it had imposed on passengers arriving from Spain following the events in Ceuta last week.

Ceuta’s President Juan Jesús Vivas met on Saturday with the Minister for Youth and Children, Sira Rego, who travelled to the autonomous city to focus in particular on the situation of unaccompanied migrant minors.

The government has identified 1,342 minors, although others have yet to be registered.

Following the meeting, Vivas insisted that his government’s position is that they should be returned to Morocco. "The only way out is Morocco via the Tarajal border crossing," he said.

The Ceuta leader also described the situation as "absolutely unsustainable" and called on the central government for more resources and security personnel.

The Ministry for Youth and Children, for its part, has put the emphasis on the protection of minors and maintains that each case must be examined individually.

Rego defended family reunification "whenever possible", but recalled that "many of the unaccompanied migrant boys and girls do not have families, so in these cases the autonomous communities must act as their guardians and guarantee their rights".

The minister also said that the government will deploy "all the necessary resources" for the reception process and will guarantee "full support, financial, technical and human, for Ceuta". A technical team from the ministry has also travelled to the city to support the management of reception and coordination with the autonomous communities.

The next point of friction will be the Sectoral Commission on Children and Adolescents, called for 13 August, which will address the transfer of minors from Ceuta.

Vox has announced that its vice presidents with responsibilities in this area in Castile and Leon, Extremadura and Aragon will not attend the meeting. The party has reiterated its opposition to the distribution with the slogan "children with their families".

Four religious communities take to the streets

The four main religious communities in Ceuta called Sunday's gathering in Plaza de la Constitución, aiming to send a joint message of unity and coexistence and to demand solutions to the situation the city is going through.

Vivas himself has called on the people of Ceuta to take part and stressed that the rally is intended to remain above party-political differences.

"This is not anyone’s gathering. It is not a gathering by any political party. It is not a gathering to benefit anyone in particular," he said on Saturday. "It is a call to make clear that Ceuta will not give in, that Ceuta will move forward."

Spanish soldiers escort migrants who had crossed into Spain towards the Spanish-Moroccan border, for their return to Morocco from Ceuta, on Sunday 2 August 2026 Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved.

The president of the autonomous Spanish territory reiterated the need to preserve unity among the population and, despite his criticism of the central government, he noted that he will maintain "institutional loyalty" and a "sense of state".

Vivas believes, however, that after the 2021 border crisis and the current one the government "has stumbled twice on the same stone".

Ayuso, Vox and the PP ramp up pressure on Sánchez

The crisis has also fuelled political confrontation over Spain’s decision to temporarily restore controls at ports and airports for travellers arriving from Italy, after Rome refused to lift the checks it imposed on passengers arriving from Spain following the crisis.

"We let more than 70,000 people enter illegally through Ceuta alone and we ban Italians from entering, a brother country that invests in and contributes to Spain," said Isabel Díaz Ayuso, President of the Madrid capital region.

"It’s spectacular, this turning our backs on the West," she added.

From the PP, its deputy secretary for Economy and Sustainable Development, Alberto Nadal, accused Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s government of having "isolated Spain in the European Union" with its migration policy and called for explanations in Parliament.

The president of Extremadura, María Guardiola, also criticised the government’s response and said that "Extremadura rejects this drift".

"This is not about setting territories against each other, or seeking fractures to mask problems. This is about facing the situation with humanity, seriousness and a firm voice," she stressed.

Vox, meanwhile, has focused its messages in recent hours on rejecting the transfer of minors from Ceuta. In addition to announcing that its regional vice presidents responsible for this area will not attend the meeting on the 13th of August, the party has repeatedly stated its position with the slogan "children with their families".

Italy denounces 'unacceptable' Spanish border measures

Tensions between Madrid and Rome have continued on Sunday, with Italy’s foreign minister and deputy prime minister, Antonio Tajani, describing Spain’s decision to respond to the Italian controls with equivalent measures as "incomprehensible and totally unacceptable".

"We suspended the Schengen area, as required by the Treaties, because something extraordinary happened in Ceuta," Tajani said in an interview to Italian media outlets.

The top Italian diplomat argued that Rome intends to lift the measures once the risk has disappeared and accused Pedro Sánchez of having "intensified" the situation. "We are not against Spain, but we have the duty to protect our borders," he added.

Opposition parties in Italy however criticised Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government for creating what it slammed as an "unfounded" diplomatic crisis.

Spain and Italy have informed the European Commission that their respective controls are temporary.

European Commissioner for Home Affairs and Migration, Magnus Brunner, said on Saturday that both countries had confirmed this provisional nature to him and pointed to signs that Italy may soon lift its measures. Spain's retaliatory measures are set to run through to 7 September.

World.title: Suspected Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan extradited from Dubai to Dublin
World.content:
The alleged leader of an Irish organised crime group has been extradited to Ireland from Dubai to face charges that he ran an international drug smuggling and money laundering empire with tentacles that stretched to the UK, Europe and the United States.

 

Air Tracker data showed an Irish Air Corps plane, which departed from Dubai landing at a military airport on the outskirts of the Irish capital Dublin on Sunday evening, after courts in the United Arab Emirates refused to block his extradition.

The plane is believed to be carrying Daniel Kinahan, aged 49, who is expected to be taken directly to the Special Criminal Court in Dublin where he will face charges of directing an organised crime group.

He will then be held at the high-security Portlaoise Prison about 150 kilometres southwest of the capital, according to Irish media outlets.

The Special Criminal Court handles all organised crime and terrorism cases, as well as others where prosecutors believe the ordinary courts are inadequate to ensure the “effective administration of justice.” Cases are heard by a panel of three judges without a jury.

Huge security operations were reportedly underway to ensure Kinahan faces justice. Protocols include armed police, members of the armed forces and the prison service — which recently acquired a bombproof escort van to transport organised crime suspects, terrorists and other high-risk prisoners.

Captured poster of suspected Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan after Washington ended a $5m bounty following his capture by authorities in Dubai, UAE, in April, 2026 US Department of State

The security precautions come amid allegations that the Kinahans are engaged in a bloody gang war with another Irish organised crime group.

“Since February 2016, the (Kinahan Organised Crime Group) has been involved in a gang war with another group in Ireland and Spain, resulting in numerous murders, including of two innocent bystanders,” the US Treasury Department said in 2022, when it sanctioned six members of the Kinahan gang and three businesses linked to it.

Irish police, with the help of authorities in the UK, Spain and the US, have been pursuing members of the Kinahan organisation for the past decade. They allege that the gang smuggled tens of millions of euros worth of illegal drugs, as well as guns into Europe, then used a network of apparently legitimate enterprises to launder the profits.

Shots of the Criminal Courts of Justice, which handles all organised crime and terrorism cases, as well as other high profile crime cases, in Dublin, Ireland, 9 August, 2026 (cleared)

Daniel Kinahan is believed to have run the day-to-day operations of the gang from his base in Dubai, the US Treasury said, including buying “large quantities of cocaine” from South America, organising its distribution in Ireland and attempting to smuggle drugs into the UK.

Kinahan has also instructed gang members to deliver money to a number of people in prison, including one who was convicted of attempting to murder someone on behalf of the organisation, the US agency added.

In March of 2022, the head of the Kinahan organization in Britain, Thomas “Bomber” Kavanagh, was sentenced to 21 years in prison after he was convicted or orchestrating drug shipments into the UK. Two other men were sentenced to 20 years and 19 1/2 years for their part in the crimes.

Shots of the Criminal Courts of Justice, which handles all organised crime and terrorism cases, as well as other high profile crime cases, in Dublin, Ireland, 9 August, 2026 (cleared)

In September of 2022, Spanish police arrested an Irishman suspected of laundering money for the Kinahan crime group after raiding a property in Malaga on the Costa del Sol.

The group was suspected of registering companies in the UK, Spain and Gibraltar, then creating a brand of vodka promoted in bars and nightclubs along the Costa del Sol to disguise the source of its earnings, according to the UK’s National Crime Agency, which assisted in the investigations.

“The Kinahan organised crime network transcends national boundaries, which is why international law enforcement operations like this are necessary,” the agency said at the time.

World.title: Poland now sixth-largest EU economy, ahead of Switzerland and Belgium
World.content:
According to data from the European statistical office, the value of Poland's GDP at current prices amounted to €922.9 billion in 2025. This means that Poland accounted for 4.9 percent of the economy of the entire European Union. In terms of economic size, only Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands now rank above Poland.

 

Germany remains in first place, with GDP at €4.47 trillion. France generated €2.99 trillion, Italy €2.26 trillion, Spain €1.69 trillion and the Netherlands €1.17 trillion.

This puts Poland ahead of Belgium, Sweden, Ireland and Austria.

Poland leads Central and Eastern Europe

Poland is by far the largest economy in Central and Eastern Europe. For comparison, Romania's GDP in 2025 stood at €380.1 billion, the Czech Republic's at €347.3 billion and Hungary's at €218.8 billion.

The combined GDP of the 27 European Union member states amounted to around €18.8 trillion in 2025. Germany had the largest share – 23.8 percent – followed by France with 15.9 percent and Italy with 12 percent.

Poland's rise is primarily the result of years of economic growth, industrial development, expanding exports and rising consumption and investment. In 2025 Poland's real GDP increased by 3.6 percent, while the economy of the European Union as a whole grew by 1.5 percent.

A large economy does not automatically mean high living standards

Eurostat figures also show the other side of the coin. The sheer size of an economy does not in itself reveal how wealthy its residents are.

Once GDP is calculated per head, Poland still remains below the EU average. According to data cited by Eurostat, Poland's GDP per capita in 2025 was less than 85 percent of the EU average.

World.title: Over 20,000 flee wildfires as British Columbia declares state of emergency
World.content:
Over 20,000 people have been forced to flee fast-moving wildfires raging across western Canada, prompting British Columbia to declare a state of emergency on Saturday as officials warned of "explosive" conditions that could put more communities at risk.

 

Residents were evacuated from Summerland, home to about 12,000 people, and Peachland, home to 8,000, along the Okanagan Lake.

The so-called "Bald Range Fire" was discovered on Friday and nearly doubled in size overnight into Saturday, forcing even emergency officials to flee.

“I had to leave the Emergency Operations Centre to come and get my family to leave this area. We’re heading south,” Erick Thompson, an emergency official with the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen said in a video posted early Saturday.

In a news conference on Saturday, Premier David Eby said a firefighting official compared the fire to a "bomb going off".

BC wildfires escalated fast, like a 'bomb going off'

"The fire goes across the top of the trees," Eby said recounting the official's description, adding that "he described flames on 100-foot (30.5 metres) tree, flames going 200 feet (61 metres) above that, and the fire creating its own weather system, which creates lightning, which then feeds on itself".

While tens of thousands fled, search and rescue teams continued efforts to look for residents that were trapped as the fire advanced.

"Air evacuations are underway for people who remain isolated behind the fire perimeter," Eby said.

Hot spots from the Bald Range wildfire burn on the mountainside above houses in Summerland, British Columbia, late Saturday, Aug. 8, 2026. Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press via AP

National police are also investigating a potential death near Summerland, but current hazardous conditions have prevented authorities from confirming the death.

No official figures have been released yet on casualties or damage caused by the fires.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney thanked firefighters and first responders on X for "working tirelessly to keep people safe".

"The federal government stands ready to help and support the Government of British Columbia in these efforts," Carney added.

As of early Sunday, a total of 102 wildfires were reported across the province, the BC Wildfire Service reported.

Many wildfires remain out of control amid extreme heat, strong winds and prolonged drought conditions across the country.

So far this year, wildfires have burned nearly 4 million hectares across Canada, according to the Canadian Interagency Forest Fire Centre.

Researchers warn that human-caused climate change doubled the likelihood of extreme fire conditions behind this years Canadian wildfires.

World.title: Over 1 million evacuated as Typhoon Dolphin hits China
World.content:
China's east coast has been preparing for the storm's arrival in recent days, with work and transport services suspended in some areas along its predicted path.

 

The centre of the typhoon moved over the coastline near Yuhuan City in Zhejiang Province at about 5:30 pm (09:30 GMT), China's National Meteorological Centre said in an online post.

Maximum wind speeds near the centre were more than 150 kilometres per hour at the time it made landfall, the NMC said. Parts of central and eastern Zhejiang could receive 250 to 500 mm of rain.

Authorities relocated more than 900,000 residents from the city of Wenzhou and opened more than 1,000 emergency shelters.

Nearly 1,400 flights in and out of Shanghai's two main passenger airports were cancelled on Sunday, state broadcaster CCTV reported.

Hangzhou's airport in nearby Zhejiang province saw 270 inbound and outbound flights cancelled, the report said.

Heavy rain, strong winds

The effects were felt as far away as Hong Kong on China's southern coast, where the weather observatory posted a record high temperature of 36.9°C, caused by warm air pushed over the city by Typhoon Dolphin.

With the storm "moving towards the vicinity of Zhejiang and moving inland, its outer subsiding air will persistently bring extremely hot weather to the territory today to Tuesday", the Hong Kong Observatory said.

A woman struggles with her umbrella in strong wind and rain ahead of Typhoon Dolphin at Huangpu District of Shanghai on Sunday, 9 August 2026. Wang Xiang/Xinhua via AP

Typhoon Dolphin brought heavy rain and strong winds to Japan's Okinawa before reaching China.

Seven people in Okinawa suffered minor injuries, including a man aged over 100 who was blown over by gusts, fell to the ground, and hit his head, according to the island's government.

By Sunday afternoon, 5,290 households in Okinawa were without electricity, according to regional utility Okinawa Electric Power.

In Taiwan, dozens of ferry services were suspended, and more than 180 flights were cancelled as the storm brought downpours and strong winds to the island's north on Sunday.

Red alert issued

China's NMC issued a red typhoon alert — its most severe warning — on Sunday morning, forecasting "extraordinary torrential rain" in some areas of central and eastern Zhejiang.

Heavy precipitation is also expected to fall in Shanghai and parts of Fujian, Anhui and Jiangsu provinces through Monday afternoon, it said.

Typhoon Dolphin was expected to weaken after making landfall while moving in a northwesterly direction over eastern China.

In Fujian, nearly 99,000 people were relocated from "risky areas" on Saturday evening ahead of the storm's arrival, state news agency Xinhua reported.

Services on more than 200 ferry routes were suspended in Zhejiang and Fujian, Xinhua said. Work on offshore projects was halted, while 474 construction vessels had been called to port by Friday morning, Xinhua said.

Some train services in affected areas were also suspended on Sunday to ensure passenger safety, state media reported.

Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme heat events more frequent and more intense worldwide.

Typhoon Dolphin's arrival in China comes two weeks after Typhoon Noul lashed southern Guangdong province, declared by authorities at the time as the strongest storm to hit China this year.

Three people were killed, and hundreds of homes were damaged by Typhoon Noul in the Philippines before it reached China.

World.title: Turkey's new opposition party offers hope, but its future is already in jeopardy
World.content:
The launch of the Yeni Party in Turkey promises to energise the country's struggling opposition. But while some polls show it leading, it remains vulnerable – already beset by arrests it says are "politically motivated".

Advertising

In a glitzy video, set to pumping music and shared widely across social media, Ozgur Ozel launched the Yeni Party – "New Party" – vowing to usher in a new era in Turkish politics and end President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s long rule.

Ozel founded the New Party after a court removed him from leading the main opposition party, the Republican People’s Party (CHP).

His rival, former party leader Kemal Kilicdaroglu, 77, who lost every election during his decade in charge of the CHP, replaced him.

Many in the country believe Erdogan played a role in the removal of Ozel, as his popularity grew thanks to tireless campaigning.

Riding the wave

The New Party is settings its sights beyond the CHP’s usual supporters.

"It covers the whole political spectrum in Turkish political life," explains Ozel's advisor Ilham Uzel.

"There are critical elements like democratisation, rule of law, secularism and a pro-Western approach, so we maintain these main pillars. But it is not confined to social democracy; we reach out to every section of Turkish society, including Islamists and conservatives, nationalists and liberals. We have Kurdish supporters."

The New Party is riding a wave of excitement. Ninety-one out of 135 CHP parliamentary deputies have defected to its ranks, joined by dozens of mayors and it is swiftly becoming the main opposition in parliament.

Turkey opposition worries that Europe is sacrificing democracy for security

Some polls show the party soaring above 30 percent, leaving Erdogan’s Justice and Development Party behind, while the CHP’s support has collapsed.

The New Party’s broad approach is finding fertile ground. "Even those who still support the governing coalition, the AK Party and MHP, are unhappy with how things are or how politics is practised, especially regarding economic issues. So there is a push towards change," says political commentator Sezin Oney.

"There is a yearning to change things at the grassroots, and the New Party may be the only party that can represent a new way of doing politics. But they have to live up to it, of course."

Corruption charges

Erdogan has remained in power for more than 20 years partly by exploiting divisions within the opposition, which is made up of conservatives, hardline secularists, and both Kurdish and Turkish nationalists.

The New Party has a key advantage over the strongly secular CHP, whose history is linked to past policies targeting Turkey’s large Kurdish minority and religious conservatives.

"CHP is identified with many bad experiences that the Kurds and conservative people had in past decades," said Mesut Yegen of the Diyarbakir-based Kurdish Studies Center.

"If you look at what Ozgur Ozel says during his speeches, you may clearly see the Yeni Party doesn’t have the baggage of CHP."

Erdogan has also often exploited the CHP’s history, painting it as anti-religious and hostile to Kurdish minority rights. The New Party faces the tricky task of keeping CHP loyalists on board while reaching new supporters.

But for now, simply staying out of jail may be the most pressing concern for its representatives.

Turkey marks a decade since the coup that never was, but never really ended

Several mayors who joined the New Party have been arrested on corruption charges, widely seen as politically motivated. In the past two years, 26 opposition mayors and hundreds of officials have been imprisoned on corruption allegations, compared to two mayors from Erdogan’s AK Party.

"They are cracking down on our party – every other day, mayors are arrested," says Uzgel. "They filed another charge against our leader. Nobody is safe in this authoritarian regime. So Mr Ozel is on the spot, definitely."

Ozel is protected by parliamentary immunity, but Oney warns he may be running out of time.

"Ozgur Ozel might be imprisoned himself once his immunity is removed by a parliamentary vote, that's a possibility. The only immunity he can have is the immunity bestowed upon him by the people. So only public opinion is protecting him. How much can it protect him? We'll see."

With parliament about to break for summer until October, Ozel has a brief window to strengthen his party and rally public support.

World.title: Netanyahu rejects Trump-backed Gaza peace plan
World.content:
The Israeli prime minister says his country will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas fully disarms, putting him at odds with a US-backed roadmap endorsed by the group.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected US President Donald Trump's plan for Gaza, saying Israeli troops would not withdraw from the territory until Hamas was fully disarmed.

"Israel rejects the 15-point document," Netanyahu told a Cabinet meeting, referring to the US-backed roadmap agreed to by Hamas in late July.

The Israeli military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed," Netanyahu said, adding that this included "heavy weaponry, lighter weaponry, all weaponry."

Israel rejects US-led Gaza peace plan To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Netanyahu said Israel remained in talks with Washington despite its objections. He described Trump as "our greatest friend in the White House," but added: "They have ideas; some of them are acceptable to us and some are not, and we know how to stand our ground on these matters."

The White House did not immediately comment.

What does Trump's Gaza plan say about Hamas disarmament?

Trump announced last month that there had been a breakthrough on a 15-point roadmap aimed at ending the war in the Gaza Strip.

The plan drawn up by his Board of Peace calls for Israeli troops to withdraw as Hamas gives up its weapons. An International Stabilization Force would then work alongside a new Palestinian police force to secure Gaza.

Trump hails 'complete disarmament' of Hamas To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Hamas is designated as a terrorist organization by Israel, the United States, the European Union and several other countries.

The group has avoided using the term "disarmament." It says it agreed to hand over its weapons for storage under a US-backed Palestinian technocratic administration that would govern Gaza under the supervision of the Board of Peace.

Hamas has said implementation also depends on Israel meeting its obligations, including withdrawing troops and halting attacks.

"We expect the mediators and the American guarantor to pressure Netanyahu and his government to adhere to the roadmap, and not obstruct the process for internal political and electoral reasons," Hamas political bureau member Bassem Naim said.

Hamas said Sunday it remained committed to the roadmap.

Gaza plan rejected by Netanyahu 'only way forward':

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, said Israel would face no obligations until Hamas had surrendered all its weapons, including assault rifles.

However, Mladenov told Israel's Channel 12 that Israeli troops would eventually have to withdraw "sector by sector" once Hamas' weapons had been collected and rendered unusable.

Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace’s high representative for Gaza, has defended the US-backed roadmap and said talks with Israel are continuing [FILE: May 13, 2019] Image: Mustafa Hassona/Anadolu Agency/picture alliance

"The option we are offering today is the only way forward that ensures this tragedy does not happen again," he said, referring to the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023, which triggered the war against Hamas in the Gaza Strip.

Mladenov said discussions with Israel were continuing and that he hoped for a "positive outcome."

How are Israel's elections affecting Netanyahu's Gaza policy?

The disagreement comes at a politically sensitive moment for Netanyahu ahead of elections scheduled for October 27, Israel's first national vote since the Hamas led attacks that sparked an ongoing Israeli military campaign in Gaza.

The prime minister is running level with or behind rivals in some polls and faces pressure from far-right members of his government who oppose concessions to Hamas.

Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich welcomed Netanyahu's position.

"We went to war with a central goal: the destruction of Hamas," he said. "The [military] cannot withdraw even a millimetre from the Gaza Strip."

US President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have long presented themselves as close allies, but have recently differed over the way forward in Gaza [FILE: July 28, 2026] Image: dpa

The dispute is the latest sign of differences between Netanyahu and Trump. The two leaders are considered as close allies, but have recently disagreed over how to deal with the conflicts in Iran, Lebanon and Gaza.

The Gaza roadmap builds on a US-mediated ceasefire reached in October 2025.

Gaza health officials say more than 1,250 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks since then. The Israeli military says five of its soldiers have been killed during the same period.

Despite the ongoing negotiations over the roadmap, Israeli forces continue to control large parts of Gaza, while most of the enclave's more than 2 million residents have been displaced and are living in a much smaller coastal area, many in tents or damaged buildings.

World.title: Alleged Irish crime boss Kinahan charged with directing criminal organisation
World.content:
Daniel Kinahan is accused of leading the Kinahan organised crime group, an international network linked to drug trafficking and money laundering operations,

Suspected international crime boss Daniel Kinahan landed in Ireland on Sunday after being extradited from the United Arab Emirates.

Following his arrival in Ireland, prosecutors charged Kinahan with directing a criminal organization during a special court sitting.

Kinahan, 49, was arrested in April in Dubai after Ireland issued a warrant for "alleged serious organized crime offenses."

He is accused of being the leader of a cartel linked to drug smuggling and money laundering.

Irish authorities deployed an enhanced security convoy to escort the supsected crime ringleader to court Image: Brian Lawless/PA Images/picture alliance

What do we know about the allegations against Kinahan?

The group is thought to be the most powerful criminal organization in Ireland, with Irish police estimating its wealth at more than €1 billion ($1.15 billion).

The alleged crime boss had lived openly in the UAE for about a decade before his arrest. He moved there from Spain around 2016 after the murder of one of his associates and an attempt on his life.

In 2022, the United States imposed sanctions on Kinahan after linking his organization to some of the world's most notorious crime networks and offered a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest.

The group is linked to a brutal feud with a smaller Irish syndicate that has resulted in 18 murders.

“Since February 2016, the (Kinahan Organized Crime Group) has been involved in a gang war with another group in Ireland and Spain, resulting in numerous murders, including of two innocent bystanders,” the US Treasury Department said.

Kinahan is the second alleged senior member of the cartel to be extradited to Ireland from Dubai. Sean McGovern was extradited in 2024 and was ultimately sentenced to 24 years in prison after pleading guilty to directing organized crime and attempted murder.

Irish media reported that a special security convoy would be deployed to escort Kinahan to the Special Criminal Court, which handles offenses related to terrorism and organized crime.

UAE, Ireland hail judicial cooperation in Kinahan extradition

In a joint statement, the justice minister of the UAE and Ireland called Kinahan "one of the most high-profile individuals sought for prosecution in connection with transnational organized crime."

Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan called the extradition a "landmark of judicial cooperation with Dubai," adding that it "sends a clear message that suspected perpetrators of serious and organized crime will find no safe haven from justice."

Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Helen McEntee hailed the outcome as "the culmination of years of determined work" by Irish authorities under various governments.

World.title: Syria says deal agreed with Russia on future of military bases
World.content:
Under the agreement, Syria will take over management of two Russian bases that were used to support ousted leader Bashar Assad during the Syrian civil war.

Syria and Russia have agreed on the future management of Russian bases on the country's Mediterranean coast.

Russia used the bases to provide military support to former Syrian leader Bashar Assad during Syria's 13-year civil war that ended in 2024.

The Syrian Foreign Ministry announced Sunday that the two nations had signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) after 18 months of negotiations.

The deal effectively means Russia will no longer have military outposts in the Arab country.

Syria says the strategic Mediterranean bases will become joint training centers [FILE: December 2024] Image: Adrien Vautier/Le Pictorium/IMAGO

What will happen to Russia's military bases in Syria?

Syria will take over management of the Hmeimim airport and the commercial berth at Tartus port, Syria's Foreign Ministry said.

State media cited the ministry as saying that the bases would be converted into "joint training and capacity-building centres, within new arrangements that preserve mutual interests."

The facilities will be gradually integrated into the country's civilian administration. The transition is expected to be completed within three months, the ministry said.

Russia has yet to comment on the agreement.

Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani visited Tartus port on Sunday Image: SANA/AFP

Russia trying to build relations with post-Assad Syria

During the civil war in Syria between 2011 and 2024, while Assad was president, Russia was Syria's main ally and military backer.

Assad was overthrown in December 2024, and now lives in exile in Moscow. Current Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa led an alliance of Islamist rebel groups that fought against government forces during the war.

Assad's ouster in 2024 dealt a major blow to Moscow's influence in the region.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has been trying to build ties with Syria's new leadership to protect the future of the only two official Russian military bases located outside the former Soviet Union.

Al-Sharaa has met with Putin in Moscow twice since coming to power in January 2025.

During his last trip, Putin said, "much has been accomplished in terms of restoring our interstate relations."

The Syrian government has been demanding that Moscow extradite Assad.

Syria's leader al-Sharaa in Moscow for talks with Putin To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

World.title: Denmark: Several wounded in suspected gang shooting
World.content:
Police said they believed that the incident was linked to a "settling of scores" within criminal networks.

Three people were wounded on Sunday in a shooting in Denmark.

They do not face life-threatening injuries, the police said.

Police said in a statement they believed that the incident was linked to a "settling of scores" within criminal networks.

"At this time, we cannot provide further information about their condition. The police presumption is that this is a settling of scores within the criminal milieu," the statement read.

Officers had been called to multiple locations in Holbaek, some 70 kilometers (45 miles) west of the capital, Copenhagen.

The incident was reported to police around 3:45 p.m. local time (1345 UTC).

Before the shots were fired, a fight broke out within a larger group in a residential estate, police said

Police said that the perpetrators were seen leaving the scene in a white car, according to preliminary information.

World.title: Germany news: Berlin to step up drone security research
World.content:
Skip next section The Left could work with CDU to keep far-right AFD out of power

08/09/2026 August 9, 2026 The Left could work with CDU to keep far-right AFD out of power

The co-leader of Die Linke ("The Left") on Sunday said the socialist party would do anything in its power to keep the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) out of office.

Luigi Pantisano's remarks on public broadcaster ZDF come with less than a month to go before elections in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD is polling at over 40% and is poised to win an absolute majority in the state parliament in Magdeburg.

Were the AfD to win in Saxony-Anhalt on September 6, it would mark Germany's first far-right state government since World War II.

To prevent that scenario, Pantisano said he would consider supporting the ruling conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) of Chancellor Friedrich Merz, despite Pantisano recently accusing the CDU of implementing "fascist politics."

"We, The Left, have shown in recent years that we take responsibility for this country," Pantisano told ZDF.

If the AfD falls short of an absolute majority, the CDU's incumbent state Premier Sven Schulze would likely have to form a coalition government with The Left.

The AfD has never been in government at either state or federal level, as all other established parties refuse to work with it, under a policy known as the "firewall."

World.title: German kidnapped in Niger released — Algeria
World.content:
Algeria says a German citizen has been released after a "criminal armed group" kidnapped him in Niger two weeks ago.

Algeria said on Saturday that a German citizen kidnapped by an armed criminal group some two weeks ago in neighboring Niger was safe and in the hands of the Algerian military.

The German national was taken in charge by the Algerian army's security services on Friday, according to a statement from the Defense Ministry shared on the official Algerian news agency.

He has now been taken on a special flight from Guezzam in the far south to the Boufarik military base near the capital Algiers, it said, adding that he was in "good health" and would be handed to German authorities "at a later date."

No details were provided on how the German national was freed.

A spokesperson for the German Foreign Ministry told DW it was aware of the case, but added that the government "does not comment on cases involving the abduction of German citizens abroad."

Niger, which has been under military rule since a July 2023 coup, has in the past few years been wracked by violence from jihadis linked to the al-Qaeda or the "Islamic State" (IS) terrorist groups.

World.title: Canada: British Columbia wildfires burning out of control
World.content:
Wildfires have grown in number and intensity across British Columbia, where a state of emergency has been declared. Evacuations are underway, but firefighters say almost half of BC's 102 fires are out of control.

Wildfires raging in the western Canadian province of British Columbia gained momentum, growing significantly in both scale and intensity in a situation already declared a state of emergency on Saturday by British Columbia Minister of Emergency Management and Climate Readiness Kelly Greene.

By Sunday morning, the BC Wildfire Service reported 102 active blazes in the province (up from 70 on Saturday), nearly half of them out of control.

"Over the last 24 hours, extreme fire behavior was seen in southern BC due to the continuous hot and dry conditions," the service said, adding that response efforts were being hampered by "elevated fire behavior coupled with severely poor visibility."

Some 20,000 people have been forced to evacuate because of the fires Image: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/picture alliance

The Bald Range fire — which exploded Saturday and enveloped the 12,000-resident Summerland area — had consumed nearly 10,341 hectares (25,552 acres) of land by early Sunday.

The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said Sunday that it was "investigating to confirm" a possible fatality.

Officials have yet to provide casualty or damage figures, nor have they published a list of missing persons.

British Columbia Premier David Eby, who warned of the dangerous and unpredictable nature of the blaze on Saturday, said, "air evacuations are underway for people who remain isolated behind the fire perimeter."

"To everyone affected, you are not facing this alone," said Eby in a statement, "the entire province is with you."

Canadian media reported the airlifting of more than 50 people from the community of Faulder.

In all, more than 20,000 people have been forced to evacuate the area.

On Saturday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney took to X to thank firefighters and first responders for "working tirelessly to keep people safe."

Carney also pledged solidarity, writing: "The federal government stands ready to help and support the government of British Columbia in these efforts. I'm keeping everyone forced from their homes in my thoughts and hoping they can return safely soon."

World.title: Divers in Italy find ancient Roman shipwreck, amphorae off coast of Sicily believed to be 2,100 years old
World.content:
The wreck is believed to be more than 2,000 years old. Italy's culture minister says it is "one of the most important underwater archaeological" finds in years.

Divers have discovered an ancient Roman shipwreck off the coast of Sicily, Italian police said.

The shipwreck is believed to be 2,100 years old.

The wreck had been found approximately three nautical miles off the coast of Mazaro del Vallo in western Sicily at a depth of 46 meters (150 feet), police said in a statement .

The cultural protection arm of the Italian police (Carabinieri) called it a "significant underwater archaeological site." It added that initial surveys had "identified a Roman shipwreck presumably dating to between the 2nd and 1st centuries BC."

Italian Culture Minister Alessandro Giuli has called the find "one of the most important underwater archaeological discoveries of recent years."

The site also contains "hundreds" of amphorae, which would likely have been used to transport wine.

The diver who found the wreck said he stumbled across hundreds of 'perfectly intact' amphorae Image: Italian Carabinieri Press Office/AFP

How was the ancient Roman shipwreck discovered?

The shipwreck was found after a tip-off from local fishermen. Calling it the "most incredible discovery of my life," Giacomo De Mola described on Instagram how he had stumbled upon the ancient wreck, which he said at first looked like "a simple rock."

"Visibility isn't great. I see a large dark mass and think, 'Just another big rock…' I get even closer. And my heart stops. It wasn't a rock. Beneath me lay an immense expanse of amphorae — hundreds of amphorae that have lain on the seafloor for over 2,000 years. A Roman ship slumbering in the silence of the Mediterranean," De Mola said.

In the post, the diver also included footage of the find.

Local media report that the ship is 21 meters long and 6 meters wide, and that it was mainly transporting Dressel 1A amphorae, tall cylindrical ceramic jars that were mainly used to carry wine.

De Mola said Lamboglia 2 amphorae, presumably from North Africa, as well as a Neo-Punic amphora, were also found.

"An extraordinary testament to the Mediterranean trade routes of over 2,000 years ago," the diver said.

World.title: “Ceuta no se vende”: la ciudad se echa a la calle tras diez días de tensión
World.content:
El malestar acumulado tras la entrada de más de 70.000 personas rompe a voz en grito en una de las manifestaciones más multitudinarias que recuerdan los ceutíes

“Ceuta no se vende. Ceuta es España”. El grito retumba en la plaza de la Constitución, abarrotada de banderas españolas y ceutíes y de miles de manifestantes. Diez días de tensión tras la entrada masiva desde Marruecos de más de 70.000 personas en la ciudad desembocan este domingo en este rincón ceutí, donde el malestar acumulado ya se escucha a voz en grito en una de las manifestaciones más multitudinarias que recuerdan sus habitantes. Las bocinas atruenan sin descanso y el “yo soy español” se repite una y otra vez entre la multitud, cada vez más alto. El manifiesto leído ha reclamado a las autoridades “respuestas” para la crisis, “solidaridad” al conjunto de la sociedad española y “serenidad y unidad” a los propios ceutíes.

El acto apenas ha comenzado cuando desde la tarima piden un minuto de silencio por quienes perdieron la vida intentando llegar a Ceuta. La petición provoca rechazo entre parte del público. “Pues empezamos bien”, se escucha decir a un hombre. El murmullo crece hasta que los propios manifestantes terminan impidiendo que se guarde el silencio. Después suena el himno de Ceuta. Esta vez, la plaza entera corea al unísono. Más de 10.000 personas han acudido a la convocatoria, según la organización; algo más de 5.000 según la estimación de Policía Nacional.

El pulso de la concentración queda marcado entonces por dos consignas. “Presidente, no estás solo”, gritan en apoyo a Juan Jesús Vivas. Apenas unos segundos después, el tono cambia: “¡Sánchez, dimisión!”. Desde la tarima, el presidente de la comunidad hindú, Ramesh Chandiramani, trata de rebajar la tensión y devolver el foco al mensaje que ha reunido a las cuatro comunidades religiosas ceutíes —cristiana, musulmana, judía e hindú—. Una de las ausencias más destacadas ha sido la del delegado del Gobierno en Ceuta, Miguel Ángel Pérez Triano, que no ha acudido a la manifestación, y al que pidieron a gritos su “dimisión”.

Ceutíes reclaman una respuesta ante la grave situación que atraviesa la ciudad autónoma. Reduan (EFE)

Entre quienes escuchan el manifiesto está Lorena Serrano, de 43 años. Es la primera protesta a la que acude desde la entrada masiva a Ceuta, los pasados 30 y 31 de julio. Desde entonces, asegura sentirse “abandonada”. “Es una tristeza grandísima la que tenemos. Solo pedimos que nos ayuden”, afirma, con la mirada puesta en la Península. Para ella, lo ocurrido aquel día fue una “invasión”.

A pocos metros, en un banco del paseo que bordea la plaza, Hamza observa la escena en silencio. Tiene 20 años y llegó a Ceuta desde Marruecos precisamente aquel día. No entiende los gritos ni las consignas porque no habla español, pero sí sabe que no comparte lo que están diciendo quienes se manifiestan. Permanece sentado mientras las voces reclaman “respuestas” a unos metros de él.

Su mirada, sin embargo, cuenta otra historia. Lleva desde entonces durmiendo en la calle y todavía recuerda la dureza del trayecto a nado. “Miré a la muerte a la cara”, dice con la mirada baja. Ahora solo piensa en salir de Ceuta y llegar a alguna de las capitales de la Península, donde espera encontrar la vida mejor que vino a buscar.

Es el contraste que atraviesa la plaza. Mientras Chandiramani insiste desde la tarima en que “esta llamada no nace del rechazo a nadie”, entre el público se escuchan otras voces: “¡Invasores!”. El mensaje de las comunidades religiosas busca marcar una frontera entre la reivindicación y el rechazo, pero las consignas de parte de los manifestantes muestran que esa línea no resulta tan fácil de sostener.

Miles de ceutíes han salido este domingo a la calle en una multitudinaria manifestación. Reduan (EFE)

No ha habido una sola palabra improvisada por parte de los organizadores. Cada frase del manifiesto había sido consensuada previamente para sumar al mayor número posible de manifestantes y reforzar una idea que la ciudad autónoma lleva días repitiendo: la situación es “extraordinariamente crítica” y Ceuta “no puede afrontar sola una situación que supera ampliamente sus capacidades y que afecta al conjunto de España y Europa”. La petición, por eso, es concreta: “una respuesta inmediata” del Gobierno y de las instituciones europeas, con “medios suficientes, recursos humanos y materiales” y “una atención prioritaria a sus fronteras” para hacer frente a la presión migratoria.

“Nosotros no podemos ayudarlos a todos”, le dice una mujer a su acompañante entre el público. Cerca de ellos, otro manifestante levanta un cartel con la fotografía del Rey: “Felipe VI, ven a Ceuta. No seas cobarde”. La tensión se palpa entre una multitud que parece haber esperado diez días para descargar su rabia. Cuando una periodista de Televisión Española intenta hacer una conexión en directo, los manifestantes apostados junto a las vallas comienzan a increparla: “¡Manipuladores! ¡Fuera de aquí!”. Las voces se cruzan y el ambiente se encrespa.

En medio de la protesta, un hombre musulmán, con la bandera de España sobre los hombros, acaba enfrentándose verbalmente con otros manifestantes. Les reprocha la falta de tolerancia. Por un momento, la escena resume la contradicción que atraviesa la plaza: una protesta convocada en nombre de la unidad y la convivencia, pero marcada también por una tensión que, a ratos, se desborda.

Y esa tensión se traslada después hasta las inmediaciones de la Delegación del Gobierno. Allí continúan los gritos y las consignas que han marcado la jornada, mientras los manifestantes reclaman la dimisión del delegado del Gobierno. Pero, poco a poco, el ruido empieza a apagarse. Más de una hora después del inicio de la concentración, la plaza comienza a vaciarse. Las banderas se pierden poco a poco entre los últimos grupos.

World.title: La Marcha Azul de Ceuta descubre brechas en la UE y malestar en Marruecos
World.content:
La avalancha migratoria subraya el descontento interno en el país magrebí, las vulnerabilidades de España y la UE, y deja como legado una potencial crisis humanitaria con miles de menores deambulando por las calles

El exilio es uno de los nombres del viaje. Más de 70.000 personas emprendieron ese incierto viaje en los últimos días de julio y se jugaron la vida en Ceuta para intentar alcanzar el precario estatus de emigrantes en Europa. La población de ese enclave español en el Norte de África se duplicó por unas horas y encendió todas las alarmas. Esa inédita y multitudinaria Marcha Azul, en busca del Mediterráneo y de la bandera europea, sorprendió a las autoridades marroquíes, a las españolas y a las de la UE. Fue una crisis letal: al menos 142 migrantes fallecieron en el intento. Y efímera: unos 2.000, si hay que fiarse de las cifras del Ministerio del Interior, siguen en Ceuta; 70.000 se han marchado ya de vuelta por el hambre, por la constatación de que saltar al Viejo Continente era imposible, quién sabe si por algo más. El grueso de ese episodio estaría solucionado, dicen los cronistas de Madrid. Pero una buena crisis es como el gato de Schrödinger; nunca se sabe si está vivo o muerto. La frontera ceutí, atestada de policías y militares, desmiente cualquier aspiración de vuelta a la normalidad. Y las calles de Ceuta cuentan otra historia: un enjambre de jóvenes, al menos unos 5.000, sigue ahí desafiando las estadísticas oficiales, además de unos cientos de subsaharianos. Han pasado hambre. Duermen en los parques, en las playas, en algunas naves industriales precariamente habilitadas, con ese aire de campamento militar, casi de campo de concentración.

Ese episodio va a tener —está teniendo— consecuencias geopolíticas. Pero a la corta, Ceuta se asoma a una crisis humanitaria si la Administración no acelera. Lo saben los ceutíes; lo intuyen los migrantes. En sus miradas hay una mezcla de miedo y desafío: “Llevamos una semana pasándolo mal, pero no nos vamos a ir”, asegura en la puerta de la comisaría una jovencísima Hiba, 16 años, enfundada en una larga camiseta de Snoopy. Hiba vino andando desde Tetuán, unos 30 kilómetros, y se echó al agua a pesar del riesgo: “Escríbalo: no nos iremos de aquí”, insiste.

La ONG Luna Blanca reparte unas 4500 raciones de comida en Ceuta a los jóvenes marroquíes, este viernes. PACO PUENTES

La crisis, en fin, sigue viva en Ceuta. Y a 250 kilómetros de aquí: en Rabat. Salé, una ciudad pegada a la capital marroquí, es también un gato de Schrödinger: tiene una fachada marítima impecable, esmeradamente cuidada, pero dos pasos más atrás el paisaje recuerda a Beirut, con edificios agujereados, medio derruidos, chabolas y miseria aquí y allá. Ziad, de 17 años, enseña feos cortes en sus brazos. Viene de Ceuta. Las redes sociales le convencieron de que podría pasar a Europa sin dificultad, y se subió a un tren como polizón con un grupo de amigos. Cuando la policía les hizo bajar, agarraron un taxi entre varios y acabaron cruzando a nado. “Fue duro, vimos cadáveres en las aguas. Alcanzamos la playa, pero no había agua ni comida, y sobre todo no había manera de llegar a Algeciras: nos volvimos con algunos porrazos de la policía”, cuenta enrabietado, con una mirada retadora que los prejuicios del cronista relacionan con la ira, pero también con sustancias más mundanas.

No solo son Ceuta y Rabat. Esta es una crisis más geopolítica que puramente migratoria: una crisis híbrida, schrödingeriana. Italia y España están enzarzadas con la suspensión de Schengen, después de una semana lamentable para la unidad europea. Las imágenes del salto son virales: Marruecos y España tienen una crisis reputacional de Campeonato del Mundo. “Me avergüenza ver a esos jóvenes huyendo de Marruecos en televisiones de todo el mundo, rumbo a Ceuta”, ha escrito el premio Goncourt Tahar Ben Jelloun. La Marcha Azul también sigue coleando a 700 kilómetros de Ceuta, en Madrid, tan protagonista como Marruecos de esa relación de vecindad tirante e incómoda. Y a más de 2.000 kilómetros, en Bruselas: esos vídeos van a reaparecer una y otra vez en las campañas electorales de la extrema derecha que se avecinan en los próximos meses, desde Suecia hasta Francia, del Este de Alemania a España.

Barrio de Salé, en Rabat PACO PUENTES Un hombre sentado en la calle junto a un comercio de Rabat, el miércoles. PACO PUENTES Dos mujeres caminan en la calle en Rabat. PACO PUENTES Una lona con banderas de Marruecos en una calle de Rabat. PACO PUENTES Varios jóvenes hacen deporte frente a pisos por demoler en el barrio de Salé. PACO PUENTES Varias personas en en Rabat, el miércoles. PACO PUENTES Varias personas en la playa de Rabat. PACO PUENTES Barrio de Salé. PACO PUENTES

Dejemos que los hechos hablen por sí mismos, que decía aquel estribillo de Les Gottesman. Las entradas empezaron como un goteo, en los primeros días de julio; de repente, espoleados por una vomitona de desinformación en redes sociales, decenas de miles de aspirantes a migrantes se precipitaron sobre Ceuta el 30 de julio. Cuando la riada humana se desbordó, los agentes marroquíes miraron hacia otro lado. Los españoles no pudieron hacer otra cosa. En apenas 48 horas la gran mayoría regresó a Marruecos, como Zaid: no había nada de las perspectivas de llegar al otro lado del Estrecho. Unos pocos miles, los menores como Hiba y los procedentes de países a los que no pueden ser deportados en caliente, siguen ahí a la espera de empezar con los inciertos procedimientos administrativos: Europa es El Castillo de Kafka. La cifra de muertos seguirá aumentando. El lado marroquí de la frontera está militarizado por el temor a otra oleada. Y los ceutíes han reaccionado razonablemente bien, aunque algunas patrullas vecinales han protagonizado brotes puntuales de violencia.

¿Cuáles son las causas? Aquí sí que no se sabe si el dichoso gato de Schrödinger sigue maullando: las razones de ese salto masivo son difusas; las fuentes consultadas apuntan en varias direcciones, aunque siempre con el condicional como maniobra de distracción. Parece claro que una sentencia del Supremo jugó un papel clave: las redes sociales dieron por hecho que quienes entraran por mar no podían ser devueltos, algo que los juristas rechazan de plano. Los bots rusos amplificaron el mensaje de que era fácil llegar a Ceuta. El algoritmo de las plataformas digitales estadounidenses hizo lo mismo. Los Gobiernos español y marroquí han señalado a las mafias de traficantes de personas, pero nadie es capaz de explicar cómo se monetiza una avalancha.

Despliegue de militares y policía en el lado marroquí de El Tarajal en Ceuta, el viernes 7 de agosto. PACO PUENTES

Como en las novelas negras, hay que seguir la pista del dinero. Pero esta vez no parece relacionada con las mafias, sino con algo más prosaico, menos peliculero. Ziad dejó los estudios a los 13 años; Hiba, a los 14. El paro juvenil roza el 30%; hay tres millones de marroquíes menores de 30 años que ni estudian ni trabajan. “La economía de Marruecos se ha modernizado, pero avanza a dos velocidades”, asegura Françoise Conradie, de Oxford Economics. El FMI vaticina crecimientos del PIB de superiores al 4% en los próximos años y hay grandes inversiones en infraestructuras y pujanza en el sistema financiero, el turismo, los puertos y la agricultura, pero a la vez se observa una desigualdad rampante. La renta per cápita es de unos 4.500 euros al año: en España son 30.000. El salario mínimo es de poco más de 300 euros, por los 1.400 españoles. Un maestro gana unos 500 euros; en España son cinco veces más. Esa proporción de uno a cinco se repite una y otra vez: al cabo, la economía marroquí es una décima parte de la española. A eso hay que sumar un Estado de derecho precario, propio de una autocracia envuelta en ropajes de seda. Rabat encarcela a los disidentes y aplasta sin miramientos las protestas juveniles. El malestar está a flor de piel. Cruzar la frontera de Europa es hoy más atractivo que cualquier utopía en ese país que a pesar de las reformas de 2012, cuando las primaveras árabes, sigue siendo una monarquía ejecutiva y absolutísima, en la que el rey Mohammed VI controla en torno el 80% del poder.

El resto del episodio está plagado de puntos ciegos, como en las grandes novelas. “Las crisis complejas suelen tener explicaciones complejas; aún estamos recabando información”, asegura una fuente del Gobierno. La misma fuente admite errores de previsión: a posteriori siempre es fácil detectarlos, pero en este caso son flagrantes. Madrid rechaza que los servicios de inteligencia informasen de lo que venía, pero reconoce que esa frontera debería estar siempre monitorizada. Y añade que no ve indicios de que Marruecos protagonizara un ataque híbrido con intenciones aviesas, a pesar de la miríada de analistas que apunta en esa dirección.

Varios de los jóvenes marroquíes llegados a finales de julio de 2026 a Ceuta, el viernes, en las inmediaciones de la comisaría de Policía Nacional. PACO PUENTES

Esos análisis, aun con los pies de barro, son demoledores: la opinión publicada internacional ha sacudido de lo lindo a Rabat, a Madrid y a Bruselas. Marruecos, según ese relato, ha olido la debilidad de Madrid. Se ha envalentonado después de la visita de Pedro Sánchez a Argelia. Se ve fuerte por el apoyo del trumpismo y de Israel. Y quizá no haya participado activamente, pero miró hacia otro lado y ya usó la migración como arma en 2021. Sánchez y su ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, han impuesto una política de apaciguamiento con continuas concesiones a Rabat, apuntan los más críticos. “Y ahora Rabat quiere más dinero por vigilar, quiere hacer valer aún más sus planes para el Sáhara, ha estrechado lazos con Trump y ha visto cómo este episodio se gestiona miserablemente en la UE”, cuentan fuentes diplomáticas. “No es posible que no lo supieran y no es posible que no lo pudieran parar, a la vista de cómo han barrido las protestas juveniles. Ahora toca revisar las relaciones: no podemos ser el país más abierto con la migración y tener ese agujero en la frontera”, añaden.

Haizam Amirah Fernández, director del Centro de Estudios Árabes Contemporáneos, desarrolla esa partitura: “España y Marruecos no tienen una relación saludable. Madrid está en posición de debilidad. La política de apaciguamiento no funciona, no solo por sus debilidades internas: tampoco hay una mayoría social que respalde las actuales posiciones españolas. Había respaldo social en lo referente al genocidio en Gaza y a la guerra contra Irán, pero no lo hay en el asunto del Sáhara. Rabat considera que puede sacar rédito usando tácticas híbridas y mediante una ambigüedad calculada, aprovechando sus actuales relaciones con Estados Unidos e Israel”. Riccardo Fabiani, del International Crisis Group, va incluso más allá: “Europa es vulnerable a los chantajes”. “La crisis ceutí empezó espontáneamente, pero las autoridades decidieron no intervenir. De esa manera Rabat le recuerda a España que el riesgo está ahí, y envía un mensaje sobre Ceuta y Melilla. EE UU e Israel lo han amplificado, aunque creo que los marroquíes se han pasado de frenada”, añade.

La dimensión europea de la crisis es peliaguda: la frontera acabó resistiendo, pero la unidad europea saltó en pedazos. La reacción inicial de la presidenta de la Comisión, Ursula von der Leyen, señalaba directamente a España. Von der Leyen se alistó a la línea dura patrocinada por Italia, Dinamarca y Finlandia. Hasta 22 países firmaron una carta con ataques directos plagada de medias verdades: relacionaban Ceuta con la regularización que acaba de aprobar España, a pesar de que no hay evidencias al respecto. ¿Conclusión? Josep Borrell, exjefe de la diplomacia europea, colige que “Europa ha entrado en pánico”. Y se explica: “Los ultras salen reforzados. El centroderecha ha hecho un cálculo político salvaje espoleado por el PP español. Y varias cancillerías tenían facturas pendientes con Sánchez y han decidido cobrárselas”. “El resultado es que España está aislada y tiene que reforzar su frontera Sur. La imagen de Marruecos es pésima, aunque refuerza su alianza con Trump. Europa es quien sale peor: cuando llegue el próximo test, en la frontera Norte con Rusia o en la frontera Sur con Marruecos o Túnez, se puede esperar poco o nada de la solidaridad europea”, proclama Borrell.

Varias personas yacen en el polígono de El Tarajal, el viernes. PACO PUENTES Varias personas yacen en el polígono de El Tarajal, el viernes. PACO PUENTES La ONG Luna Blanca reparte, el viernes, unas 4500 raciones de comida en Ceuta. PACO PUENTES Varias mujeres tras recoger una ración de comida repartida por la ONG Luna Blanca. PACO PUENTES Varios de los jóvenes marroquíes llegados a finales de julio de 2026 a Ceuta, en las inmediaciones de la comisaría de Policía Nacional. PACO PUENTES

Desde Bruselas, la vicepresidenta Teresa Ribera no es menos rotunda: “Estas crisis no pueden interpretarse ni abordarse como crisis en un solo país: la protección de las fronteras es un elemento más de la autonomía estratégica europea, al mismo nivel que la energía, la tecnología o las materias primas críticas”, asegura a EL PAÍS. Ribera reclama un cambio de rumbo: “No podemos contar con nuestros aliados tradicionales como hasta ahora. Europa debe prepararse para responder a amenazas híbridas, incluida la eventual utilización de los flujos migratorios como instrumento de presión, siempre desde el respeto al Derecho internacional y a los derechos fundamentales”.

El modelo europeo de gestión de las migraciones se caracteriza por externalizar el control de fronteras a países como Turquía, Marruecos o Túnez a cambio de dinero. En Bulgaria, en Rumania, en Hungría, en Polonia o en los bálticos se han levantado kilómetros de vallas; la España progresista de Sánchez tiene una aproximación distinta, pero en Ceuta y Melilla no tiene nada que envidiar al resto de Europa: en esos enclaves hay dos estupendas vallas coronadas con unos rodillos metálicos que hace poco sustituyeron a las concertinas. Madrid ha conseguido que la UE pague 500 millones a Marruecos para reducir las entradas. Pero Marruecos quiere más: Turquía y Túnez obtienen muchos más fondos. Esa estrategia proporciona a los Estados que prestan ayuda policial a la UE lo que se ha denominado “el arma de la migración masiva”. Bielorrusia la usó contra los bálticos y Polonia en 2021, y Marruecos contra España ese mismo año. En Bruselas, esas prácticas se conocen como “ataques híbridos”. No está nada claro que lo de Ceuta sea exactamente eso, pero las sospechas están ahí.

Un joven en el polígono industrial de El Tarajal (Ceuta). PACO PUENTES

Había dos grandes misterios en las relaciones entre España y Marruecos. Uno de ellos es el espionaje con el programa de Pegasus, que afectó a la plana mayor del Gobierno español. El segundo es el giro español al apoyar el plan de autonomía del Sáhara, que se discutirá en la ONU este otoño. Ya hay un tercero: las causas del aluvión de más de 70.000 migrantes en Ceuta. Boutaina Ismaili Idrissi, profesora de la Universidad Mohammed V, recalca que no se puede concluir que Marruecos usara malas artes. “Se trata de una crisis que pone al descubierto la fragilidad del modelo migratorio europeo. Los controles fronterizos se han convertido en un arma de negociación. La confianza política se esfuma en cuanto aparece una crisis. Y los costes humanos son sobresalientes”, destaca. “Hay una interdependencia asimétrica más que un chantaje marroquí. Hay una vulnerabilidad evidente en el lado europeo, y una frustración, que se junta con otras cosas, entre los jóvenes de mi país. Y hay un contexto geopolítico que influye, aunque no lo reduciría a la caricatura de alinear a Marruecos con Trump y contra Sánchez”, según su tesis.
