World.title: Major Croatian Projects Involve New Bridge, New Tunnel & Railway
World.content:
August the 10th, 2026 – Several major Croatian projects involving a new bridge on Krk, a 14 kilometre tunnel and a railway line to host high speed trains are underway.

By the end of 2029, the reconstruction of the 44-kilometre railway line from Karlovac to Zagreb should be completed. Snjezana Bicak/Poslovni reports that if you want to go from Rijeka to Istria, you will come across a major construction site; there are more and more excavators and tall cranes as you approach the Učka tunnel or exit it, all so that already next year we will have a full-profile motorway and a more comfortable and pleasant drive to the peninsula and along the entire Istrian Y.

You will also encounter works if you travel through Slavonia, especially around Požega. If you fly with Croatia Airlines, its pilots will bring you to your destination in new aircraft. And if you travel by train from Karlovac to Zagreb, for the next four years you will also watch the works from the train, given that, finally, four years after the first tender was announced, construction of the second track on the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac line has begun these days. Thanks to this, passengers from, for example, Karlovac to Zagreb should reach their destination by train in about 20 minutes.

karlovac is going up in the world…

Karlovac Mayor Damir Mandić has said several times so far that this is a big thing for the development of Karlovac, given that a large number of Karlovac residents work in Zagreb, children go to the metropolis to study, and a number of business activities are linked to Zagreb, writes Večernji list.

Karlovac thereby becomes an even more desirable place to live – outside the hustle and bustle of the big city, yet only about 20 minutes away by train, and the same after the construction of the third lane of the motorway connecting the two cities, which is also planned.

Karlovac will truly become a suburb of Zagreb with an excellent transport connection to it, but also to the rest of Croatia, especially towards the Adriatic, which makes it even more attractive for business investments that lead to the opening of new jobs, and then also for living and the arrival of new families.

The start of construction of the lowland railway, at least on this part of the corridor, delights everyone it concerns. This is no small investment; the contractor, the Spanish company Comsa S.A., which signed a contract with HŽ Infrastructure in July for the execution of the project, will reconstruct the existing track, build the second track, carry out the electrification of 44 kilometres of railway, build new bridges, viaducts and power facilities, arrange stations and stops, and construct five facilities for the needs of HŽ Infrastructure in Karlovac. After the works are completed, train speeds of up to 160 km/h are planned. The value is not negligible either: it amounts to 348.5 million euros including VAT, and the deadline for completion of the works is 36 months, i.e. by the end of 2029.

The Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section is only part of the entire lowland railway project that will connect Zagreb and Rijeka on a section 56 kilometres shorter than the current railway connecting the two cities, and the procedures for contracting works on certain sections are underway. The project is complex; the new double-track and fully electrified railway is designed for speeds of up to 160 km/h for passenger trains and 120 km/h for freight trains.

With a total length of about 175 kilometres – 56 kilometres shorter than the existing line – this will drastically reduce travel time. The biggest challenge on the section after Karlovac is overcoming the demanding mountainous terrain, which is why the construction of more than 30 viaducts and tunnels is planned.

a brand new tunnel through velika kapela

The star of the project is the future tunnel through the Velika Kapela massif, 14 kilometres long, which will become the longest in Croatia. For comparison, the Sveti Rok and Mala Kapela tunnels together are a little less than 12 kilometres long. The route also provides for the construction of five new stations and one stop. All of this should be completed by 2036. From just these few points it’s very clear that Croatia is in a major infrastructure boom that has been going on for some time and will last at least another ten years, which is the period planned for the construction of the entire lowland railway corridor that will connect the largest port of Rijeka with the Hungarian border.

“Croatia is currently implementing one of the largest investment cycles in its existence in transport infrastructure, which covers all types of transport, as well as the development of public urban transport and new forms of mobility. Through European sources of financing within the financial periods 2014–2020 and 2021–2027, projects with a total value of around 5.57 billion euros have been contracted and are being implemented in transport infrastructure, of which around 3.45 billion euros relates to non-refundable EU funds.

The stated amount refers exclusively to projects implemented with the support of European funds and financing instruments, through the Operational Programme Competitiveness and Cohesion, the Competitiveness and Cohesion Programme 2021–2027, the National Recovery and Resilience Plan and the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF). The largest part of these investments is directed towards the modernisation of railway infrastructure, followed by the road sector, maritime transport and public urban transport,” the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure told us.

They add that, in parallel with the already contracted projects financed with the support of European funds, the Government is implementing a broader investment cycle of modernisation of the transport system that includes EU funds, the state budget, loans and other sources of financing.

more railway and train projects are in the works

The railway sector stands out in particular, where investments in railway infrastructure worth more than 1.7 billion euros are underway, while an investment cycle worth around 6 billion euros is planned over the decade to come.

This is the total value of planned investments in the modernisation and renewal of the railway network, which will be financed by a combination of different sources, including EU funds. The goal of the investments is to increase the safety, capacity and quality of railway transport and to strengthen Croatia’s connectivity with European transport corridors, the competent ministry adds.

Minister Oleg Butković said that never before has so much been invested in local and regional railways as now, thanks to part of the loan from the European Investment Bank that the Croatian Government secured. He emphasises that Croatian Motorways invest around 50 million euros annually in investment maintenance of motorways, along with investments in the development and modernisation of the motorway network and the introduction of a new electronic toll collection system.

Croatian Roads, for example, have invested around 1.6 billion euros over the past ten years in the construction of new and the reconstruction of existing state roads, while a series of projects with a total value of more than 1.2 billion euros is currently in preparation and implementation.

port infrastructure investments

“We also have a major investment cycle in port infrastructure worth more than 500 million euros, the largest part of which is financed with EU funds. From the Ministry’s budget alone last year, 14.7 million euros was allocated for port infrastructure and the rehabilitation of maritime domain in general use, and a total of more than 118.4 million euros during the terms of this Government. Investments in inland navigation are aimed at increasing navigation safety, improving the navigability of rivers and developing port and berth infrastructure. In the period 2014–2027, more than 200 million euros was invested in inland waterway projects through European funds and other sources of financing, with the largest part of the investments relating to the development of infrastructure on the Danube River and in the Port of Osijek,” the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure adds.

roads and expressways

When it comes to investments in road transport, among the most important projects currently underway is certainly the completion of the construction of the Istrian Y in full profile, including the section from the Učka tunnel to Matulji, with a total value of around 200 million euros.

A network of expressways is also being built across Croatia, among which the most important is the Podravina Y (from Vrbovec – Bjelovar – Virovitica – the border with Hungary), then the Varaždin – Krapina expressway, the Požega expressway with an exit to the A3 motorway, the Solin – Stobreč – Dugi Rat – Omiš expressway, the Nuštar – Vukovar expressway, the Okučani – Stara Gradiška expressway, and the Zlatar Bistrica – Marija Bistrica expressway as part of the Zagreb Ring.

New bypasses are also being built across Croatia: Fužine, Nedelišće, Pušćine, Orebić, Drniš, Zaprešić, Čakovec and other towns, and reconstructions of state roads are underway: the new entrance to Split, the Sisak junction – Sisak, Donja Zdenčina – the bridge on the Kupa, Veli Vrh – Pula, the narrower city ring of Karlovac, the Širina intersection. The introduction of a new toll collection system is underway, and the Križišće – Selce section on the A7 motorway is being built, while the procedure for signing a contract with the consortium of bidders is underway for the Jadranovo – Selce subsection.

A contract has been signed with the contractor for the Križišće – Jadranovo subsection, the first phase of the Selce – Novi Vinodolski section is being built, and project documentation is being prepared for the Novi Vinodolski – Senj and Senj – Žuta Lokva sections. The Rudine – Osojnik section on the A1 motorway is being built, and additional lanes are being added on the Zagreb – Karlovac section of the A1 motorway and the Zagreb West – Lučko section of the A3 motorway. These last two projects in particular will significantly contribute to reducing congestion, especially in the summer months.

For decades, for example, investment in connecting Požega to the A3 motorway was awaited. Požega-Slavonia County Prefect Antonija Jozić said at the signing of the contract with the contractors that the construction of the expressway and the Požega junction will be of decisive importance for the transport accessibility and economic development of Požega-Slavonia County.

“For many years there was talk of a project that is now being realised. Our county will no longer be the appendix of Croatia; we are becoming more accessible by transport, and what we are most looking forward to is that these projects will be a strong driver of the economy,” Jozić said.

Brod-Posavina County Prefect Danijel Marušić emphasised that this project is proof of cooperation and common interests of neighbouring counties. “In my municipality, along this road, economic zones are already slowly being prepared; of course there will be greater circulation of both people and goods, and it is truly a completely different perspective,” Marušić said.

modernisation of the railway system

In addition to roads, the Croatian Government is also investing in the modernisation of the railway system through the renewal of infrastructure and rolling stock.

“In the recent period, the procurement of new trains for HŽ Passenger Transport has been realised, and 70 new low-floor trains are in operation: 55 electric multiple units, 13 diesel multiple units, and one electro-battery and one battery train each. The total value of the procurement amounts to 363.4 million euros,” the Ministry adds.

And they are not stopping there, because a new procurement has already been contracted. Specifically, 6 electro-diesel trains for the Zagreb – Split route, worth 57.3 million euros, which will be put into service this year; then 5 electro-diesel, 4 electro-battery and 4 battery trains with two charging stations, worth €117.9 million, with delivery during 2027 and 2028. There are also 6 electro-battery trains and a hybrid charging station in Kotoriba, worth 53.6 million euros, with delivery during 2028 and 2029. Additionally, by the first quarter of 2029, 228.8 million euros will be invested in the procurement of an additional 25 trains, the competent authorities note.

Preparation is also underway for potential financing of the procurement of an additional 30 new trains from the Social Climate Fund. The new trains will run on more modern tracks, given that major investments in railway infrastructure are also underway.

Specifically, the reconstruction and construction of the second track on the Dugo Selo – Novska line is underway, a project worth around 900 million euros; the modernisation of the Dugo Selo – Križevci and Križevci – Koprivnica – state border with Hungary sections is being completed; and, as mentioned, the modernisation of the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section worth 280 million euros has begun.

Numerous projects for the renewal of local, regional and international lines are also underway, including the Pitomača – Kloštar, Generalski Stol – Oštarije, Ogulin – Moravice, Karlovac – Ozalj, Knin – Zadar, Osijek – Koška and other sections.

that isn’t all…

“When it comes to investment in port infrastructure, in the previous period 25 projects were contracted through which 14 ports were built or reconstructed, including the ports of Tkon, Crikvenica, Cres, Unije, Sućuraj, Korčula, Baška, Žigljen, Zadar, Split, Stinica, Vela Luka and others. In the new financial period, investment in port infrastructure continues through projects with a total value of 267.64 million euros. These include projects for the reconstruction and expansion of the ports of Novi Vinodolski, Rovinj, Murter, Krk, Rab, Prvić Šepurine, Perna, Prigradica, Split, Kaštela, Vrsi, Ika and others,” the Ministry of Maritime Affairs revealed.

Among the more important projects related to inland navigation, the completion and development of the bulk cargo terminal in the Port of Osijek, the arrangement and improvement of the waterway of the Danube River, and the construction and development of port infrastructure for inland freight transport stand out. The leaders of Slavonian cities and counties are particularly looking forward to these projects, given that they will contribute to the development of economic activities across Slavonia.

Minister Oleg Butković also said that the goal of these significant investments is to increase the share of river transport in total freight traffic, connect Croatian ports with European transport corridors and further relieve road traffic.

World.title: Will New Toll Collection System Reduce Croatian Traffic Jams?
World.content:
August the 9th, 2026 – Will the new toll collection system set to come into force next year actually manage to reduce the infamous Croatian traffic jams on the motorways?

As Poslovni reports, the much anticipated installation of more than 220 portals on motorways across Croatia is currently underway. Appearing on HTV’s programme Studio 4, the director of the Traffic Sector at HAC (Croatian Motorways), Hrvoje Ordulj, touched on the new toll collection system, which is expected to become operational during 2027.

More than 220 portals are currently being installed on motorways throughout Croatia, and a large part of the infrastructure has already been put in place, reports HRT. “We expect all the portals to be installed by October, and the system could go live during next year,” he said. However, he did warn that not even the new system will be able to completely eliminate the country’s well known summer congestion. “Regardless of barriers or the new toll collection system, traffic will stand still if the load is too high,” Ordulj stated.

Major projects: Učka, Novi Vinodolski and Matulji

Speaking about future projects, Ordulj announced the continuation of construction of the Novi Vinodolski bypass, the completion of the Matulji junction, and the connection of Istria and Kvarner with a full-profile motorway.

“We expect that in the first quarter of next year Istria and Kvarner will be connected by a full-profile motorway,” Ordulj said. He added that works on the sections between Križišće, Jadranovo and Selce will intensify after the end of the summer tourist season.

World.title: Croatia Could Face Natural Gas Problems in Autumn
World.content:
August the 9th, 2026 – Croatia could end up facing natural gas problems this autumn, with underground natural gas storage facilities being filled poorly.

As for natural gas prices, Grozdanić says that prices in the European Union have risen to a little over 60 eurps per megawatt-hour (MWh). Poslovni reports that towards the end of summer, concerns about the supply and prices of energy sources in the colder part of the year always begin. This year they have been spurred by the conflict in the Middle East that shows no sign of ending, as well as by the extreme drought that has left river levels at record lows, affecting the operation of hydropower plants and the Krško Nuclear Power Plant.

Midweek, the Krško NPP, the electricity production of which covers 16 percent of domestic market needs, temporarily and preventively reduced the reactor’s output by 20 percent due to the risk of overheating of the water in the Sava River, writes Miroslav Filipović for N1.

“This isn’t a limitation for technological reasons, but for environmental reasons, i.e. for the protection of the bio-environment and the temperature of the Sava River,” energy expert Ivica Jakić explained this move by the Krško NPP to our portal.

the situation with electricity

Neither Jakić nor energy expert Igor Grozdanić expect that, despite all the difficulties, the electricity supply will be endangered this autumn.

“There will be enough electricity on the market thanks to the nuclear power plants over in France, and let’s not forget that the Czech Republic and Slovakia together have eight nuclear reactors which, like the Krško NPP, are cooled by air coolers and are not dependent on the amount of cooling water from rivers or lakes,” Jakić said.

“If nothing extraordinary or catastrophic happens, I don’t expect shortages or problems in the electricity supply. And if prices rise, they will not rise too much,” Grozdanić said. Croatia imports a significant share of its electricity from Bosnia and Herzegovina, where it is produced in thermal power plants that operate without difficulties. In addition, Jakić notes that electricity is purchased under contracts, so-called futures, at a pre-agreed price, whereby the supplier is obliged to deliver it at a fixed price and within a fixed delivery period.

petrol and petroleum products

After four consecutive price reductions, the first summer price increase of petroleum products followed in mid-July — only diesel fuel, and not a large one. But two weeks ago all fuels rose significantly: LPG by five cents per litre, eurosuper 95 by eight cents, and eurodiesel by as much as 16 cents per litre.

Next Tuesday a new price increase is expected, but only for diesel fuel. According to RTL’s unofficial information, a litre of eurosuper 95 should be two cents cheaper, while eurodiesel and blue diesel should rise by three cents per litre. The exact amount will be known on Monday when the Government decides on a possible intervention in prices. Grozdanić doesn’t really expect major shocks regarding fuel prices this autumn.

“As for fuels, the situation is more stable than on the markets of other energy sources in our country. Regardless of the situation in the Middle East, prices are always higher in summer because of the tourist season,” he says.

natural gas is where the problems could arise

However, there could be problems with natural gas, Grozdanić notes.

“The fact is that underground natural gas storage facilities are being filled poorly. But that is expected because prices are very high for this time of year. The American-Iranian war has reduced the gas supply and everyone is waiting to see how the situation in the Middle East develops. The situation is interesting because European natural gas stocks have fallen to their lowest level since 2011. Under current market conditions it does not pay anyone to fill the storage facilities. Gas storage facilities need to be filled before winter, but people are still waiting,” he says. Gas stocks across EU storage facilities are currently a little below 58 percent, Grozdanić emphasises, and the fill level of the Okoli Underground Gas Storage is roughly the same.

On Friday, PSP Okoli was at 57 percent fill. The Croatian Government decided at the end of July that by 1 October the fill level of the Okoli storage must be at least 85 percent, with an allowed deviation of up to five percent.

As for natural gas prices, Grozdanić says that prices in the European Union have risen to a little over €60 per megawatt-hour (MWh). “This autumn the gas price could be in the range of 55 to 75 euros per MWh,” Grozdanić concluded.

World.title: Meet Krapje – The Wooden Croatian Village Hidden Within a Nature Park
World.content:
August the 9th, 2026 – Beautiful, secluded Krapje is often called the wooden Croatian village, and it is hidden deep within a beautiful nature park, far from the coast.

Despite being relatively unheard of abroad, Krapje is actually one of the best-preserved traditional villages most people will ever see. It holds the status of a cultural heritage monument of the Republic of Croatia and is considered one of the pearls of the gorgeous Lonjsko Polje Nature Park.

Posavina is one of the rare parts of Croatia where traditional wooden villages can still be seen today, the kind that were once a common sight along the course of the Sava. Putni kofer writes that charming oak houses, wide courtyards, farm buildings and a way of life adapted to the river have shaped this region for centuries, and one of the places that has preserved this valuable heritage almost in its original form is Krapje. Located in the municipality of Jasenovac, on the left bank of the Sava in Sisak-Moslavina County, this picturesque village is today counted among the finest examples of traditional architecture in Croatia.

most of the houses in the croatian wooden village are over 100 – and still standing despite their construction style…

Nikola Cutuk/PIXSELL

Only about a hundred people actually live in Krapje, and because of its exceptionally well-preserved architecture it was declared a village of architectural heritage in 1995. It is first mentioned in written sources as early as the 14th century and got its name from the fish krap (carp). But Krapje’s greatest hallmark is the traditional Posavina architecture. The village has more than 80 wooden houses typical of central Posavina, holds the status of a Category A cultural heritage monument and is considered one of the pearls of Lonjsko Polje Nature Park.

Most of the houses are more than a hundred years old. They were built from oak planks joined with wooden pegs and are recognisable by their covered external staircases, porches, protective canopies and richly decorated railings and columns. Their facades all face the street, while farm buildings, stables, haylofts and storerooms, are located at the rear.

a true haven for all kinds of birds

Even the method of construction was no accident. Because the Sava frequently flooded the surrounding area, durable oak wood that could withstand water was used for the houses, while living quarters were placed on higher floors. Besides its architectural heritage, this part of Posavina is also known for its unspoiled nature.

Between Krapje and nearby Drenov Bok lies Krapje Đol, a special ornithological reserve spanning an impressive 25 hectares. It has been protected since 1963 and includes an old branch of the Sava and a valuable wetland habitat overgrown with lush vegetation. Thanks to this environment, more than 500 pairs of birds nest there, among which spoonbills stand out in particular.

One of the must-see places in the village is the Krapje Visitor Centre, located in a complex of restored wooden Posavina houses. It houses a multimedia hall, a gallery and a souvenir shop, and you can also rent a bicycle or canoe and set off on the Border Guards’ Trail that begins in the centre’s courtyard.

At house number 48 you can view the ethnographic collection of the Palaić family with more than 170 items that show the everyday life of the former border guards and the traditional crafts characteristic of Posavina. Every year the European Heritage Days in Krapje are also held in the village, dedicated to the preservation of its rich architectural and cultural heritage.

a rich natural world awaits visitors

While you’re there, be sure to try the biggest local speciality, carp on a spit (šaran na rašljama). Finally, a stay in Krapje can easily be combined with exploring Lonjsko Polje Nature Park, one of the largest and best-preserved floodplain areas in Europe. The park is known for its rich plant and animal life, especially storks. It also includes the famous village of Čigoč, which was declared the first European Stork Village back in 1994.

World.title: What are The Main Issues With Summer Traffic Jams in Croatia?
World.content:
August the 9th, 2026 – There are an array of very particular issues causing the infamous summer traffic jams up and down Croatia, with queues stretching for kilometres on the motorways.

The awful queues at Lučko, stoppages near Sveti Rok and kilometre-long traffic jams towards the coast have not spared Croatian motorways this year. Nor have they ever so far. Poslovni reports that Hrvoje Ordulj, Director of the Traffic Sector at HAC (Croatian Motorways), spoke as a guest on HRT’s programme Studio 4 about summer delays being practically unavoidable, but that drivers often make the situation worse by disregarding traffic rules.

“These long queues will remain unavoidable for some time yet. We all want to get to the coast and we all want to return from the sea at the same time,” Ordulj stated, before pointing out that the problems aren’t only at the toll booths themselves, but are a result of the very configuration of the roads and the large number of vehicles that pour southwards through Croatia at the peak of the summer season.

Why do traffic jams form at Lučko and Sveti Rok?

Ordulj explained that at Lučko as many as seven or eight traffic lanes merge and then narrow down to only two. “You can’t reduce traffic from seven lanes to two and expect everything to function normally. A particular problem lies with the Sveti Rok tunnel, where traffic sometimes has to be temporarily stopped for safety reasons. Traffic in the tunnel mustn’t come to a total stop. If an accident or breakdown occurs, the entrance to the tunnel is automatically closed,” Ordulj explained.

He added that HAC operators continuously monitor the situation on the motorways and, when they assess that traffic density is too high, temporarily close the entrance to the tunnel in order to prevent dangerous situations.

“Foreigners respect the limits, croatian drivers much less”

One of the topics of the conversation was also drivers’ traffic culture. Ordulj openly admitted that Croatian drivers often ignore speed limits, especially in roadworks zones. “As a rule, you’ll notice that drivers with foreign registration plates respect the speed limits, unlike a lot of Croatian drivers who overtake until the last moment and cut in front of other vehicles,” he said.

He particularly appealed to drivers to respect dynamic signalling and the rules on forming an emergency corridor. “When traffic stops, the driver can’t possibly know whether it is an accident or just another ordinary jam. That’s why the emergency corridor should be formed immediately,” he concluded.

World.title: Meet the Croatian Dead Sea On a Dalmatian Island Paradise
World.content:
August the 8th, 2026 – There’s a so-called Croatian dead sea, tucked away on a southern Dalmatian island paradise, just a stone’s throw away from the hustle and bustle of Dubrovnik.

Hidden away on an island in the very far south of Croatia lies an unusual lake that shares its name with the saltiest sea in the world. In summer it is a popular swimming spot. Just a few hundred metres from the famous Dubrovnik lies the island of Lokrum. Putni kofer writes that this beautiful little island of small size and great diversity is a must-visit destination for a trip from the Mediterranean pearl and offers peace and beauty that can rarely be experienced elsewhere. But did you know that Lokrum also hides the Croatian Dead Sea? That is exactly what an unusual lake is called that has become one of its most popular swimming spots in the summer months.

The Croatian Dead Sea – 30 metres wide and 10 metres deep

The island of Lokrum itself is believed to have got its name from the abundance of sour wild orange trees that once grew on it, derived from the Latin word for sour fruit, acrumen. Its highest peak, Glavica, is 96 metres high, and on the southern part of the island there is also a small lake. That is precisely the Croatian Dead Sea!

It is 30 metres wide and, at its deepest point, ten metres deep. Its southwestern shore is not kind to visitors, but the northeastern one is. That is why the Croatian Dead Sea has become one of the favourite swimming spots on the island, especially for families with small children.

This natural wonder is actually a saltwater lake connected to the Adriatic Sea by a narrow channel. The enclosed natural cove is ideal for swimming because there are never any waves in it, and the water is shallow and warmer than that on the open sea. In summer the lake on the island of Lokrum is full of bathers and tourists, so it is best to visit it out of season or in the early morning hours. Nearby there is also a natural stone arch that locals call “Buža”, a favourite backdrop for photographs among tourists. The Croatian Dead Sea was of interest to numerous researchers and travel writers who, as early as the 19th century, analysed and described the chemical composition of its seawater. Today this lake is part of the Natura 2000 ecological network, and its condition is regularly monitored.

the island of plants…

Over many millions of years, the rocks have been extremely tectonically disturbed, as evidenced by the systems of cracks and faults that are gradually widened by karstification and the erosive action of the sea. Thus a former erosional depression in the relief, today known as the Lokrum swimming area, was filled with the sea in the youngest geological period, the Quaternary. You can very easily reach the island by regular boat lines from Dubrovnik. This pearl of the southern Adriatic was first protected as early as 1963, and since 1976 it has had the status of a special forest vegetation reserve. Hundreds of plant species grow on it, including 70 species of eucalyptus.

Besides the botanical garden and the beaches, the biggest attractions are also the abandoned Benedictine monastery and the castle on the southern part of the island. You can simply walk across Lokrum, but if you really want to enjoy it and explore it in more detail, we definitely recommend setting aside a whole day.

World.title: No mercy for corrupt officials as Al-Zaidi widens Iraq crackdown
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s anti-corruption effort has shown no signs of stopping, with arrests and investigations ranging from senior Oil Ministry officials to MPs, former provincial leaders, and other government figures since he assumed office.

One of the main early instances involved Adnan Al-Jumaili, the former deputy oil minister for refining affairs, whose imprisonment was a key development in the probe.

Statements gathered from Al-Jumaili assisted authorities in expanding their investigation into a larger network of politicians and officials accused of profiting from government contracts and state resources.

That probe culminated in a spectacular operation on June 28, when Iraqi security forces blocked off access to Baghdad’s highly defended Green Zone and conducted coordinated raids on political and government heavyweights.

Iraq’s national news agency first claimed 47 arrests, including 12 current parliamentarians, a former legislator, a former aide to former Prime Minister Mohammed Shia Al-Sudani, and a top Oil Ministry official.

According to sources inside Iraq’s anti-corruption authorities, there were 67 people held during the first phase of the “Dawn Crackdown”.

Ali Maarij, Iraq’s Deputy Oil Minister for distribution and another key player in the country’s energy industry, was among those held.

According to prosecutors, the larger investigation turned up claims of the misuse of public resources, government contracts, and commissions for personal or political gain.

Authorities also recovered a considerable quantity of assets related to the investigations. Iraq’s Supreme Judicial Council said in July that 375 kg of gold had been confiscated as part of the al-Jumaili probe, with more cash and gold found in subsequent operations.

Instead of finishing with the first Green Zone attacks, the campaign lasted all of July.

Between July 20 and July 26, Iraqi police apprehended 31 persons in seven corruption cases, reflecting the government’s escalating enforcement campaign.

So far, August has delivered a slew of high-profile cases.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, was held as authorities investigated claims involving public finances, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court for a separate inquiry.

On Sunday, police detained Hashem al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company, on suspicion of corruption regarding a Ministry of Defense contract.

The specifics of the alleged infractions and the contract’s worth have not yet been released.

The financial impact of the crackdown is becoming significant.

The Eco Iraq Observatory said on Sunday that police had recovered around 482.6 billion Iraqi dinars ($371.6 million) in stolen assets, including cash and gold.

Taken together, the arrests convey an increasingly clear message from Al-Zaidi’s government: senior political ties, legislative standing, or positions inside major ministries should not exclude people from scrutiny.

However, arrests alone will not decide whether Iraq eventually succeeds in combating corruption.

Success will be predicated on transforming the present campaign into long-term institutional transformation via open government contracts, improved audits, digital financial systems, independent investigations, and tighter controls over public funds.

This is especially crucial as Iraq pursues tens of billions of dollars in foreign investment and works to strengthen economic ties with the United States, Europe, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and other Gulf nations.

Investors need to be confident that predictable rules govern contracts and public institutions rather than political interference.

The crackdown has also received backing from key international partners.

During a phone call with French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday, Macron reaffirmed France’s support for Iraq’s anti-corruption drive and economic reforms, as well as continued cooperation on counterterrorism and strengthening the capabilities of the Iraqi armed forces.

But the problem goes beyond financial corruption.

Al-Zaidi has committed to reinforce state power and bring armaments under government control, adding to the administration’s already arduous task of dealing with entrenched political and economic interests.

Iraq’s long-term goal must consequently be greater than capturing people.

Baghdad needs institutions strong enough to prevent corruption and foreign intervention from resurfacing under new political networks, whether sponsored by Iran or another external entity.

If Al-Zaidi can combine rigorous enforcement with due process and institutional change, the campaign might greatly boost trust in the Iraqi government.

Without such institutional improvements, even hundreds of arrests risk becoming a momentary crackdown rather than the long-term transformation Iraq requires.

World.title: Iraq opens its first IMAX cinema in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has inaugurated its first IMAX theater at the Iraq Mall in Baghdad, introducing the premium large-screen movie format to the nation for the first time.

Sarwa Abdul Wahid, the Acting Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Antiquities, formally opened the new Iraqi Cinema branch in the mall, adding to Baghdad’s fast expanding entertainment and leisure sector.

According to IMAX’s official listing, the Iraq Mall site in Baghdad has an IMAX with Laser auditorium and stadium seating.

The launch allows Iraqi consumers to see important worldwide movies in IMAX without having to fly abroad, like Christopher Nolan’s 2026 blockbuster The Odyssey.

The film, starring Matt Damon, Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Charlize Theron, Robert Pattinson, and Lupita Nyong’o, was the first feature film filmed exclusively on IMAX film cameras.

The Odyssey has also emerged as one of 2026’s greatest box office triumphs, earning more over $260 million globally in its first weekend.

Iraqi Cinema is now offering daily IMAX screenings of the film at its Iraq Mall location.

IMAX brings another worldwide entertainment option to Baghdad, as Iraq seeks additional investment in retail malls, restaurants, hotels, theaters, and other leisure developments, while also growing its domestic tourist and entertainment sectors.

World.title: Iraq arrests senior Trade Ministry official Hashem Al-Sudani
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi prosecutors detained Hashem Al-Sudani, the director general of the state-owned General Automobile and Machinery Company (GAMCO), on Sunday for suspected embezzlement in a contract with the Ministry of Defense.

The contract’s specifics, including its value and the particular alleged infractions under investigation, have not been released. Al-Sudani’s arrest is part of Iraq’s growing anti-corruption effort, which targets prominent government officials, legislators, and business leaders.

The new arrest comes as Baghdad ramps up the “Dawn Crackdown,” an anti-corruption operation that began on June 28 by Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi to probe big crimes involving public contracts and state finances.

The initiative has gained traction among senior and politically connected individuals.

Recently, police arrested former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, also known as Abu Mazen, while former Finance Minister Taif Sami was allegedly called by the court as part of a separate inquiry.

Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and reclaiming public monies, with authorities attempting to show that probes would extend to officials regardless of party or institutional affiliation.

Corruption has long been a major impediment to Iraq’s growth, depleting state resources, degrading public services, and deterring private and international investment.

The ongoing arrests imply Baghdad’s new effort is spreading to official institutions, but anyone arrested or interrogated has not been convicted and is still subject to due process.

World.title: Five dead in new Russia, Ukraine strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Russian strikes killed two people and wounded dozens across Ukraine overnight Saturday and Sunday, while a Ukrainian drone attack killed three people in Russia’s Belgorod region.

The World Health Organization denounced a strike that destroyed a warehouse in Ukraine holding medical supplies.

More than four years after the start of Russia’s large-scale offensive against Ukraine, both countries are ramping up long-range strikes. The resulting civilian casualties led the United Nations to condemn both sides last week.

Russia is relying on “ballistic terror,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday on social media, stating that 61 missiles of various types had been fired at Ukraine this week.

“More pressure, more sanctions against Russia and more air defence for Ukraine are needed,” he added.

The two people killed by a Russian drone strike were in the major northeastern city of Kharkiv, where four floors of a residential building were also destroyed, said Zelensky.

Twenty-three people were also wounded, according to regional governor Oleg Synegoubov, sharing images of a gutted building with emergency services working at the scene.

Zelensky said eight people had also been wounded overnight in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port, and residential buildings.

He condemned another “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, in the Dnipropetrovsk region that wounded nine people, including four children.

– WHO condemns warehouse strike –

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro had been destroyed in strikes on Friday.

“I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care MUST STOP. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros in a post on X Sunday.

“Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!”

In Russia, a Ukrainian drone attack on the border city of Belgorod killed three people, according to the region’s acting governor, Alexander Shuvaev.

Twenty-five people, including children aged four and nine, were also wounded, he added.

Fires broke out in cars, two apartment buildings, and a house, said Shuvaev.

A video released by Russian media shows an apartment building engulfed in flames at night, watched by residents gathered across the street.

On the front line, the Russian army said Sunday they had captured two small villages in Ukraine’s eastern Donetsk region. The claim has not yet been independently verified.

One of them, Vasiutynske, is about 10 kilometres (six miles) from the city of Kramatorsk, a Ukrainian urban and logistical hub.

– Zelensky defends strikes –

Zelensky, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s responses to Russia’s attacks — including strikes on oil refineries, air-defence systems and radar stations — as “truly just responses”.

“The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said.

On Thursday, United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned both sides for their repeated attacks on civilian areas.

“Attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure are a clear violation of international humanitarian law, and must stop immediately,” he said.

The Russian invasion, which began four and a half years ago, continues with prospects of a peace agreement largely stalled.

World.title: Como sign England defender Chalobah from Chelsea
World.content:
Milan – Como have completed the signing of England centre-back Trevoh Chalobah from Chelsea for a reported fee of 30 million euros ($34.5 million), the Serie A club announced Sunday.

The 27-year-old has penned a five-year deal with Cesc Fabregas’s ambitious side, who will play in the Champions League for the first time this season.

“I can’t wait to bring my experience to the team, feel the incredible atmosphere at the stadium, and connect with the fans,” said Chalobah, who made 151 appearances for Chelsea.

“I will give my absolute all every single day to make history together.”

Como pipped AC Milan and Juventus to Italy’s fourth and final Champions League place last season.

Scudetto holders Inter Milan had also been heavily linked with a move for Chalobah, before reportedly deciding the asking price was too high.

“Trevoh is an important signing for us and a player who represents the level of ambition we have at this club,” said Como coach Fabregas, a former Chelsea midfielder.

“He is a leader who can raise the level of the team, and I am very happy that he has chosen Como.”

Chalobah was part of the England squad which finished third at the World Cup last month, after receiving a late call-up as a replacement for the injured Tino Livramento.

He could make his Como debut when they visit Udinese in their Serie A opener on August 22.

World.title: Iraq steps up digital transformation of banking and customs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is speeding up preparations to digitize its financial and customs systems, with Finance Minister Falih Sari and Central Bank Governor Nizar Nasser Hussein considering tighter integration of electronic payments, customs processes, and government financial data.

The conference, which included members from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), aimed to accelerate electronic linkages between Iraq’s customs and payment systems.

Sari urged authorities to speed up implementation as part of measures to modernize financial management, streamline trade processes, and create a more efficient environment for companies and investors.

The talks also focused on increasing cooperation between fiscal and monetary agencies, including digital data interchange and upgrading Iraq’s banking infrastructure, while maintaining financial stability and meeting government financial responsibilities.

The revisions are part of Iraq’s larger transition from cash-heavy and paper-based institutions to a more integrated digital financial infrastructure.

Baghdad sees modernization of banking, payments, and customs as more crucial as the government strives to bring its financial system closer to international norms, increase transparency, and make it simpler for Iraqi and foreign enterprises to do business.

The drive also supports broader banking changes in Iraq, as the government seeks deeper connectivity with the international financial system and encourages private sector development.

World.title: PSG sign France full-back Digne from Villa
World.content:
Paris – Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne has joined Paris Saint-Germain on a three-year deal, the European champions announced Sunday.

The 33-year-old French international, who grew up in the Paris region, returns to PSG, where he played for two seasons between 2013 and 2015.

“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain,” Digne said in a statement on the Ligue 1 champions’ website.

“I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.

“I can’t wait to start this new chapter and put all my experience at the service of the team.”

After PSG, Digne spent time on loan in Serie A with Roma before signing for Spanish giants Barcelona, who were then coached by current PSG boss Luis Enrique.

He moved to the Premier League in 2018, firstly with Everton, then four years later joining Aston Villa.

At Villa Park, he won the Europa League under Unai Emery last season.

Capped 64 times by his country, Digne became France’s first-choice left-back over the course of the 2026 World Cup.

Digne is PSG’s second major signing of the summer transfer window after fellow French international Maghnes Akliouche arrived from Monaco.

He could make his debut for his new club against his former employers Aston Villa on Wednesday in the UEFA Super Cup in Salzburg.

However, long term it is likely his principal role will be to provide cover for PSG’s starting left-back, Nuno Mendes.

World.title: Former Iraq finance minister Taif Sami summoned in widening corruption probe
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Former Iraqi Finance Minister Taif Sami has been officially summoned by a court and put on a judicial wanted list as authorities broaden a corruption probe that has reached high political and government officials, according to sources.

Sami is thought to be outside Iraq and has not been captured.

The alleged court action is part of an inquiry and does not prove misconduct or lead to a conviction.

The revelation comes as Iraq’s new administration steps up its anti-corruption effort, which has already resulted in the detention of important political personalities and bureaucrats.

Former Salah al-Din governor Ahmed al-Jubouri, often known as Abu Mazen, was detained in Baghdad recently on suspicions of misusing public contract funds.

A close acquaintance was also arrested as part of the inquiry.

The new charges stem from a big operation in Baghdad’s highly protected Green Zone in late June, when Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service detained numerous officials as part of a larger corruption probe.

According to reports at the time, authorities were looking into claims involving government contracts and huge sums of public money.

Sami, the previous administration’s finance minister under former Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammad Shia Al-Sudani, was one of Iraq’s most significant economic leaders, responsible for handling the federal budget, government expenditures, and financial ties between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.

The purported summons therefore implies a potentially major extension of the probe against individuals who formerly held top positions inside the Iraqi state.

Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s administration has prioritized combating corruption and improving state institutions as part of its domestic agenda to boost public trust and reassure international investors.

With the arrest of Abu Mazen and the rumored legal proceedings against Sami, Iraq’s anti-corruption campaign is gaining traction among established political players.

However, the claims are still being examined, and individuals who are being arrested have the right to due process.

World.title: 'Only 3 of 13 exams cancelled': Students reject Jharkhand govt's '98% demands met' claim
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand students protesting irregularities in recruitment exams rejected the Hemant Soren-led government's claim that 98% of their demands have been accepted. They said only three of the 13 exams they wanted cancelled have been scrapped.

The students accused the JMM-led government of âspreading liesâ and said they would continue their peaceful protest. They have also called for a âVidhan Sabha Marchâ on Monday and appealed to students, political parties and the public to join the protest.

At a presser, a student leader said, âThe Jharkhand government is spreading lies that it fulfilled 98 per cent of our demands. It cancelled only 3 of 13 exams sought by us.â

The protesters are demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in all recruitment exams conducted by the state. Student leader Ravindra Paswan accused the government of insisting on a CID probe, which he claimed was known for âcover-upsâ.

The students said their protest would remain âpeaceful and democraticâ and warned that they would not allow anti-social elements to disrupt the agitation.

The protest entered its 17th day on Monday.

World.title: To bypass Bosphorus & Hormuz, Russia moots direct rail link to India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Russian deputy PM Marat Khusnullin has suggested exploring a direct rail link from Moscow to the âIndian Oceanâ to avert risks associated with the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz, amid ongoing conflicts, including in West Asia, that have stalled the ambitious India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor.

Bosphorus is a narrow, natural strait in Turkey that connects Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara.

âA rail link to the Indian Ocean should also be explored. Risks related to the Bosphorus and the Strait of Hormuz might require alternative routes: through Turkmenistan, Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan. Any options providing access to India are acceptable,â he told Russian news agency TASS.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Experts said constructing a rail link spanning two continents and four countries would be a gigantic challenge.

Apart from logistical difficulty and cost, for any option to extend the rail link to India, New Delhi would have to deal with the fact that it would pass through Pakistan, and a lot would depend on obtaining an iron-clad guarantee for securing cooperation and commitment of the hostile neighbour to protect the railway and cargo.

The statement does not provide a detailed construction plan, cost estimate or timeline. However, if such a corridor is eventually developed, it could create a direct overland rail freight route linking Russia with India while offering an alternative to traditional maritime shipping routes.

Among railway corridors linking multiple nations, Yiwu-Madrid is the longest freight train line in the world â spanning a little over 13,000 km, it connects Chinaâs Yiwu to Spainâs Madrid, traversing eight countries.

World.title: Dope test of turbulent Air India flight’s pilot ‘not negative’, sent for confirmation, says government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The captain of Air Indiaâs August 4 Phuket-Delhi flight, which experienced a sudden loss of altitude of about 300 feet, was subjected to a psychoactive substance (dope) screening test on arrival, whose result was ânot negativeâ and has been sent for confirmatory tests, the aviation ministry said Sunday.

TOI had exclusively reported on Sunday that the pilot of the turbulence-hit flight may have failed the dope test.

The ministry has classified the incident, which led to 17 people being hospitalised, as serious and said the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) will probe it.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âFurther action, as appropriate, will be taken based on the outcome of the investigation and confirmatory test results,â it said.

Air India pilots grounded till probe is over

Directorate General of Civil Aviation rules stipulate that âin case the screening test (for psychoactive substances) is non-negative, the employee shall be immediately removed from the safety-sensitive duty till a confirmatory report is received.

In case of positive confirmatory test for the first time, the concerned employee shall be referred by the organisationâ for de-addiction.

Multiple passengers and cabin crew members on board the Airbus A320 operating as AI 2379 were injured when it suddenly lost altitude. The plane later landed safely in Delhi. âAs standard operating procedures following such an occurrence, both flight crew members underwent the prescribed psychoactive substance screening test. The screening test in respect of the pilot-in-command (PIC) indicated a result requiring confirmatory testing.

Samples have been sent to the designated laboratory for confirmatory analysis, and the final report is awaited,â the ministry statement added.

Both pilots have been taken off flying duty by the DGCA, pending investigation.

World.title: India among top nations in quantum technology, says science minister Jitendra Singh

Asked when India would become a manufacturing hub, Singh said, âIt indicates that progress is happening at a very fast pace, both in manufacturing and in technology, and unlike I think a decade and a half back, today we are at the same level as any other country in the world...â

World.title: Government may be going slow on FCRA to woo DMK, NCP(SP) for delimitation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The passage of FCRA amendment bill is not in Lok Sabha's agenda for Monday as Parliament's monsoon session enters its last week, giving rise to the view that government may be going slow on the contentious piece of legislation to sweeten the deal for parties such as

and NCP(SP), which are opposed to its provisions and are being seen by the governing alliance as prospective backers for its delimitation exercise.

Sources said the meeting of LS's business advisory committee, where upcoming agenda items are finalised, on Monday will give more clarity as a schedule for discussion on the bill should be fixed if it has to be taken up for passage in the remaining four days of Parliament's monsoon session ending on Aug 13. Monday's agenda includes the introduction of four bills but makes no mention of the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill.

Government may prefer full-fledged debate on FCRA to address criticism against the bill

The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on March 25 but has not been taken up for discussion yet, amid fierce protest from opposition parties and minority groups, especially Christian bodies.

Christian groups, which are a major recipient of foreign funding, have decried the proposed amendments, saying it threatens their charitable works and will allow the government to seize their assets if their FCRA licence is withdrawn or not renewed.





What has, though, made things politically trickier for the BJP is the support extended by DMK president M K Stalin to the demand of a delegation representing churches of different denominations in their meeting with home minister Amit Shah that the bill be either withdrawn or sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

With the government looking to assuage DMKâs concerns to get it on board before it makes a fresh bid for Parliamentâs nod for its delimitation exercise, coupled with implementation of the womenâs reservation law from 2029, it may not like to put the regional party on the defensive by bringing up the FCRA bill, some MPs said.

Supriya Sule of NCP SP, another party being eyed by the government as a probable supporter for the amendment bill, has also opposed the FCRA bill.

Mizoram CM Lalduhoma had told the media after joining a group of Church bodies from his state for a meeting with Amit Shah on Thursday that he was told that a debate on the bill is expected to be held on Aug 12.

The continuing impasse in Parliament due to the oppositionâs protests has added uncertainty as the government will prefer a full-fledged debate so that the home ministry could address the criticism around the bill.

World.title: ED charges against RCom, Reliance Infra in 40k crore bank fraud
World.content:
NEW DELHI: ED filed two chargesheets, one each against

(RCom) and Reliance Infrastructure Ltd, on Saturday before a special court here, naming Gautam Doshi, Sateesh Seth, Amitabh Jhunjhunwala and the two entities of Anil Ambani's Reliance Group as the accused for offences of money laundering and defalcation of bank funds of over Rs 40,000 crore.

In its chargesheet against RCom, the agency has said that "the proceeds of crime are quantified at Rs 40,186 crore, the outstanding sum defaulted on by the entities to a consortium of banks and financial institutions".

The role of the accused in the raising, deployment, concealment and projection of the funds, including false certification of end-use of $1 billion in FCCB proceeds, was also highlighted.

ED sought confiscation of properties worth Rs 8,078 crore attached earlier in the case, belonging to Reliance Communications and its promoters and directors, including assets of Anil Ambani.

The chargesheet against Reliance Infrastructure Ltd said, "Probe revealed an organised scheme to divert public funds from four NHAI-awarded toll-road projects: Trichy-Karur (NH-67), Trichy-Dindigul (NH-45), Salem-Ulundurpet (NH-68) and Jaipur-Reengus (NH-11). The projects were financed through NHAI grants and loans from banks and financial institutions. Approximately Rs 187 crore was siphoned off during Sept-Oct 2010.

World.title: Jharkhand student protests: Security tightened, prohibitory orders clamped ahead of march
World.content:
The Jharkhand Police has imposed prohibitory orders around the assembly premises and made elaborate security arrangements across the city in view of Monday's (August 10, 2026) 'Vidhan Sabha March' called by students who have been protesting for more than two weeks against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in the state.

Also read | Jharkhand government cancels JPSC exam; protests to continue till CBI probe ordered, say students

BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged on Sunday (August 9) that the party's State unit president Aditya Sahu has been "put under house arrest".

Mr. Bauri, also the party's state general secretary, said the government will "not be able to achieve success by deploying security personnel outside Mr. Sahu’s residence".

All necessary security arrangements are being made in view of the proposed picketing at the state assembly, the officer said.

“In view of the possibility of unrest during the students’ proposed march to the state assembly, the police administration has been put on alert,” ADG (Headquarters) Manoj Kaushik said.

He urged the students, who will participate in the march to protest in a "peaceful and disciplined" manner as they have shown their discipline in the ongoing protest here for over two weeks, he said.

"It is their responsibility to ensure that anti-social elements and troublemakers are prevented from joining the march," the ADG said.

Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyone’s responsibility.

"We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.

A prohibitory order has already been promulgated within a 750-metre radius of the Vidhan Sabha building from August 6 to 12. The order will be in place between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. on these days, he said.

Such an order was also imposed from Sunday (August 9) midnight in Jamshedpur in view of the protest march in Ranchi, an official statement said.

The Ranchi district administration has made an appeal to agitating students to refrain from participating in any kind of aggressive demonstrations.

It also cautioned against violence and illegal activities during the protest march to the assembly.

Protesters alleged that hundreds of students coming to the state capital from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by the police forcefully.

The students' protest entered its 16th day on Sunday (August 9), while six of them are on hunger strike protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Iran ties Strait of Hormuz reopening to U.S. concessions on several demands
World.content:
Iran said it was nearing a final pact with Oman to define new shipping lanes between them through the Strait of Hormuz, but reiterated that the U.S. must meet other conditions, including compensation and an end to sanctions and military threats, before the strategic waterway is reopened.

Also read | Mecca Agreement | A new triple alliance in West Asia

A U.S. official told Reuters on August 7, 2026, that Iran and Oman were close to a deal that ⁠could pave the way for restoring safe passage through the strait, a major conduit for oil and gas shipping before Iran blocked Hormuz in response to U.S. and Israeli attacks on Tehran that began in late February.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Aragchi said on August 9, 2026, that an agreement with Oman on the strait was in its “final stages,” but reiterated comments made on August 8 that Tehran would not reopen the channel unless the U.S. met certain demands.

Also read | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

Iran and the U.S. are not engaged in direct talks, and Tehran will not start them ⁠as long as Washington breaches an interim deal signed in June, Mr. Aragchi said, adding that messages were being exchanged through intermediaries.

World.title: Meta will soon face another high-stakes trial in U.S.
World.content:
With two convictions and nearly $1 billion in damages already stacked up, Meta will face another trial starting this week about alleged harms to children in a case brought by four U.S. states.

Also read | Meta faces Tennessee trial over allegations Instagram was designed to be addictive

The federal trial, one of the most consequential among a myriad of legal proceedings targeting social networks in the United States, will begin Wednesday (August 12, 2026) with jury selection at a federal court in Oakland, near San Francisco.

Opening statements are expected to start next week on August 18, with the trial lasting for roughly six weeks, followed by a verdict in early October.

The attorneys general of California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey allege the largest social media network in the world deliberately made Instagram and Facebook addictive for children.

And they are demanding a long list of restrictions on how Instagram and Facebook operate for minors, as well as up to $1.4 trillion in penalties — nearly Meta's entire market cap which exceeded $1.5 trillion on Friday (August 7).

CEO and founder Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses the prosecution plans to call to the stand; he also testified six months ago in a separate case that took place in a Los Angeles court.

While Mr. Zuckerberg has been known to spend an increasing amount of time living at his home in Hawaii, the company's headquarters in Menlo Park is about an hour's drive from the courthouse.

‘Facebook Files’

The Oakland trial is the culmination of a standoff that began in late 2021, when a former employee, Frances Haugen, leaked thousands of pages of internal research, dubbed the "Facebook Files," which showed that Meta had internally measured the potential harm Instagram was causing to some teenage girls, while publicly downplaying the impact.

The revelations triggered a joint investigation by dozens of states, which two years later resulted in a complaint filed by around 30 state attorneys general.

Four states will now attempt to prove their case together in Oakland.

TikTok, Snapchat and Google-owned YouTube have also been sued by thousands of families, school districts and prosecutors across the country in various local, state and federal lawsuits.

In a landmark trial that concluded in March, Meta and YouTube were convicted by a Los Angeles jury, which found both companies were responsible for a teenager's social media addiction.

That jury awarded the teenager $6 million.

On Thursday (August 6, 2026), a judge in New Mexico ordered Meta to implement product changes and pay more than half a billion dollars in damages to the state to fund the treatment and prevention of harms caused by Facebook and Instagram.

A jury in New Mexico previously ordered Meta to pay $375 million after it found the company liable for endangering children by making them vulnerable to predators on its platforms, among other harms.

Meta has appealed, or intends to appeal, all of these decisions.

Meta is "confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts," Meta told AFP in a statement Thursday (August 6).

The company intends to argue that mental health is an industry-wide issue, and that some of the states' claims are protected by free speech laws.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

Immunity over content

The four states in the Oakland trial accuse Meta of violating their consumer protection laws, in addition to a federal law that protects children's data, known as COPPA.

They allege that multiple features were designed to keep minors hooked, particularly infinite scrolling, excessive notifications and "like" counts.

It's a strategy that focuses on how apps are designed, not what is posted on them, essentially sidestepping the broad immunity internet sites enjoy in the U.S. regarding content created by their users.

The staggering $1.4 trillion in alleged damages comes from estimating the number of affected users in the four states.

However, the jury will have only an advisory role and Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers — who oversaw major trials between Apple and Epic Games, and Elon Musk and OpenAI — will decide on penalties, if Meta loses the case.

Parents of teenagers allegedly harmed by social networks might watch from inside the courtroom, as they did in Los Angeles, while the rest of the country can follow the proceedings from an audio-only livestream on YouTube.

World.title: China slams India’s move of formally naming 27 places in Arunachal Pradesh
World.content:
China on Sunday (August 9, 2026) slammed India’s latest move of identifying 27 locations in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard names on its official map as “self-deception which runs counter to the improving momentum in bilateral relations and could complicate efforts to properly handle border issues.”

In response to frequent attempts by China to rename some places in Arunachal Pradesh, India on Friday (August 7, 2026) formally identified 27 places — including land, passes, a lake and a monument — in the border State by their standard names on the official Indian map.

The Global Times, China’s Communist Party-run newspaper carried a report which said, “China has been carrying out standardization of geographical names in the region for a long time. At a time when China-India relations are showing signs of improvement and leaders from both countries are expected to engage through multilateral platforms, any unilateral action by India that escalates the border situation shows no point and will not serve the broader interests of bilateral relations.” Qian Feng, director of the Research Department at Tsinghua University’s National Strategy Institute, was quoted.

Mr. Qian said India should avoid turning border issue into a larger dispute, as such actions could stifle the improving political ties between the two countries, the report further said.

“China does not recognize Arunacla pradesh”

According to the report, Since 2017, China’s Ministry of Civil Affairs has released six batches of standardized names for locations, with a total of 112 names announced as of April 2026. These names cover villages, mountain passes, rivers and peaks, accompanied by standardized Chinese and Tibetan names as well as geographic coordinates. Chinese Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a routine press briefing on April 14 that China does not recognize Arunachal Pradesh.

Quoting Mr. Guo, the report added, “China-India relations are generally stable at the moment. China’s commitment to improving and growing China-India relations has not changed. We hope the two sides will work in the same direction and act more in ways conducive to bilateral relations.”

The newspaper also added that, India’s latest naming of 27 locations is a unilateral administrative move and does not alter the legal status of the area, quoting Guo Xuetang, a professor at the center for South Asia and Indian Ocean Studies under Shanghai International Studies University.

According to Mr. Guo Xuetang, India’s move is an attempt to strengthen its claim of control over the area and create additional leverage in future boundary negotiations. However, such actions have no practical meaning and will only undermine the atmosphere for negotiations between the two countries, the report added.

The report further said that Mr. Guo said the only way to resolve the China-India boundary issue is through equal negotiations and a fair settlement based on historical and legal principles, while unilateral actions that create tensions or change the status quo will only harm mutual trust and border stability.

World.title: Kanwar Yatra 2026: Traffic restrictions in Delhi, U.P., and Haryana
World.content:
Kanwar Yatra, or the annual pilgrimage of people from the Ganges River to their local temples, is underway and will conclude on Tuesday (August 11, 2026).

The festive pilgrimage began on July 30 and will conclude on August 11, 2026 on the day of Shivratri.

U.P. CM Yogi showers flowers on Kanwariyas, describes Kanwar Yatra as unparalleled example of devotion, unity

Owing to the heavy pedestrian and pilgrimage traffic, specific advisories have been issued by authorities to ease commute of citizens, especially in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, and Haryana.

Here’s your guide to what’s open and what’s closed.

Region/State Affected areas and restrictions Duration of restrictions Recommended Alternate Routes Delhi • Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida–Kalindi Kunj road, and Okhla Bird Sanctuary • GT Road (Apsara Border to Yamuna Bridge) closed for general traffic August 11–12, 2026 • Avoid Kalindi Kunj, GT Road, and Wazirabad Road. • Use designated alternate corridors like NH-9 and NH-44. Gurugram (Haryana) • Heavy vehicle movement entering Delhi via Haridwar return paths • Travel corridors toward Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad August 9 – 11, 2026 • Use Dwarka Expressway. • Use KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk. Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh) • Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) • Heavy pilgrim traffic on NH-58 / Delhi-Meerut route August 9 – 12, 2026 •Use NH-09 as primary alternative route • Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha: Take NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.

Delhi

The Delhi Traffic Police, in a post on X on August 10, 2026, said that “traffic congestion is likely on Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida, Kalindi Kunj-Noida road and the connecting roads towards Okhla Bird Sanctuary.” It especially warned commuters not to use the routes leading through Kalindi Kunj junction, to plan commutes in advance and to allow sufficient additional travel time.

Delhi CM assures kanwariyas will not face any difficulties

TRAFFIC ADVISORY



Traffic movement in and around Kalindi Kunj Junction is likely to remain slow and congested till 12.08.2026 due to heavy movement of Kanwariyas during the ongoing Kanwar Yatra and ongoing road repair work on the Okhla Barrage–Kalindi Kunj stretch.



📍ADVISORY… pic.twitter.com/dzqYI092mO — Delhi Traffic Police (@dtptraffic) August 9, 2026

Gurugram, Haryana

Gurugram traffic police, on August 8, detailed alternate routes for heavy vehicles to take to enter the national capital of Delhi owing to the ‘Kanwar Yatra’ pilgrimage and the return of the ‘kanwariyas’ from Haridwar.

It asked commuters to “use Dwarka and KMP expressway via Panchgaon Chowk” as travel corridors to Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad may also be affected.

This advisory is in effect till August 11, 2026 and the traffic police also attached maps for easy referencing for citizens.
