Shortly before the event, police summoned the movement’s local coordinator, Valeria Klyuchnikova, and questioned her over possible involvement in terrorist activity. Officers told her that the motorcade had to be approved by the city administration and law enforcement authorities.

Klyuchnikova was later detained while picking up a package containing the movement’s flag and several T-shirts. Police confiscated the flag and one T-shirt before releasing her.

This article was produced with the support of Media Network

World.title: Armenian Catholicos Garegin II attends first hearing in criminal trial
World.content:
Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

A court in Armenia‘s Armavir region has begun hearing the criminal case against the Catholicos of All Armenians and six bishops who serve on the Supreme Spiritual Council. Garegin II attended the hearing in person.

Clergy members and politicians gathered outside the courthouse. Lawmakers from the opposition Armenia Alliance and I Have Honour Alliance left parliament during the afternoon and travelled to Etchmiadzin to show their support for the Catholicos. Dozens of worshippers also gathered outside, periodically chanting “Your Holiness” and singing traditional Armenian church hymns (sharakans).

Prosecutors accuse the Catholicos and the senior clergy of obstructing the enforcement of a court ruling.

Garegin II removed Bishop Gevorg Saroyan, head of the Masyatsotn Diocese, from his post. Saroyan is one of the senior clerics who joined Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan’s campaign to “reform the Church”. The bishop challenged his dismissal in court. The court ordered his temporary reinstatement as head of the diocese until it reaches a final decision in the case. However, before the court could rule on the merits, the Supreme Spiritual Council, led by the Catholicos, also defrocked him. The council argued that the courts have no jurisdiction over the Church’s internal affairs.

Lawyer Ara Zohrabyan says the Catholicos faces criminal prosecution for carrying out his “ecclesiastical and canonical duties”.

He argues that state interference in the Catholicos’s decisions violates the principle of Church autonomy, the constitutional relationship between the state and the Church, and freedom of religion.

“In this criminal case, the court will examine not only the charges against specific individuals, but also another fundamental question: whether the secular authorities can interfere in the internal life of the Church and criminalise the exercise of the canonical authority of the Catholicos of All Armenians,” the lawyer said.

The trial comes after tensions between the government and the Church steadily escalated.

About a year ago, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan called for the Catholicos to step down. He first argued that Garegin II could not lead the Church because he had broken his vow of celibacy and had a daughter. He later accused the Catholicos of having links to foreign intelligence services. The ruling Civil Contract party has also included the removal of the “de facto head of the Church” in its election manifesto.

Members of the ruling party accuse the Church of interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy. The parliamentary opposition rejects that claim. Opposition lawmakers argue that it is the government that is unlawfully interfering in the Church’s affairs.

First hearing ends after 30 minutes as judge recuses himself

Shortly after the hearing began, Judge Hakob Manukyan announced that part of the proceedings would take place behind closed doors because they would involve “personal information”. He said the information concerned both himself and the Catholicos’s lawyer.

“A few minutes later, lawyer Ara Zohrabyan told journalists: “The judge has recused himself. He has withdrawn from hearing this case.”

According to Zohrabyan, the judge said he had once granted him his licence to practise law, which could “raise doubts about his impartiality”. Zohrabyan said he did not believe this constituted valid grounds for recusal.

“However, he refused to take part in this disgraceful trial. The very fact that the Catholicos is standing trial is deeply troubling. The case will now go to another judge.”

After the hearing, the Catholicos of All Armenians and his supporters headed to the cathedral to attend a church service and pray together.

Garegin II: “The authorities are trying to bring the Church under their control”

After the service, the Catholicos addressed those gathered outside the cathedral. He said the authorities were taking steps to undermine the Church’s authority, restrict its autonomy and bring it under their control.

“The authorities are persecuting the Church and the clergy. They have arrested and restricted the freedom of a number of clergymen, benefactors and other patriotic individuals through unlawful and fabricated criminal cases,” he said.

The Catholicos dismissed the charges against himself and the six clergymen as groundless.

“We remain steadfast in our faith and determination to defend our rights, which are guaranteed both by our country’s Constitution and by the fundamental principles of international law.”

Opposition declares a “day of shame”

Marianna Gakhramanyan, an MP from the opposition I Have Honour Alliance, said:

“Today is a day of shame. The Catholicos of All Armenians, our spiritual father and the head of our Church, is standing trial in Etchmiadzin. It is shameful and unprecedented. This is an attack not only on the independence of the Armenian Apostolic Church but also on Armenia’s Constitution, which clearly states that the political authorities have no right to interfere in the affairs of the Church and that the Church is separate from the state.”

“Who is defending the Church – us or you?” asks ruling party MP

Commenting on opposition lawmakers who came to support the Catholicos, Civil Contract MP Artur Hovhannisyan said:

“The Church has begun interfering in Armenia’s domestic and foreign policy.”

He also referred to the allegations that the Catholicos had violated his vow of celibacy:

“We are the ones standing with the Church. We are the ones defending the Church. You are defending clergymen who broke their vow of celibacy, who engage in politics and use religion and the Church to protect themselves from the consequences of breaking that vow and taking part in politics. Anyone who has broken the vow of celibacy should leave the Church.”

The ruling Civil Contract party’s election manifesto also outlines plans to reform the Church. Under the proposal, the “de facto head of the Church”, as Pashinyan’s team refers to the Catholicos, should leave office. The plan calls for the election of a locum tenens, the adoption of a new Church charter containing “mechanisms to preserve centuries-old traditions”, and, ultimately, the election of a new Catholicos.

Comment

Political analyst Tigran Grigoryan told Reuters:

“Pashinyan has come to see the Church as a political threat and as an institution capable of supporting the opposition and various political parties in their efforts to gain power.

“The case against the clergy fits into a broader pattern of selective justice pursued by Pashinyan’s government, under which leading opposition figures have been arrested and some of their property has been confiscated by the state.”

Catholicos of All Armenians appears in court

World.title: Azerbaijan FM in Kyiv: gas for Ukraine, visit to Irpin, Ukrainian drones
World.content:
Azerbaijani FM visits Ukraine

Azerbaijan‘s Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov paid an official visit to Ukraine on 6 August.

It was the first visit by an Azerbaijani foreign minister to Kyiv since the start of Russia‘s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Bayramov began his visit with a trip to Irpin, where he viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones and laid a wreath at a memorial to fallen defenders at Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry.

He also held meetings with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, President Volodymyr Zelensky, Head of the Presidential Office Andriy Yermak, Defence Intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov and National Security and Defence Council Secretary Ihor Klymenko.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

One of the most notable announcements was Azerbaijan’s stated willingness to supply Ukraine with natural gas if needed.

The two sides also discussed the possible use of Ukraine’s underground gas storage facilities to strengthen regional energy security.

These developments are significant both regionally and internationally, particularly in the context of Azerbaijan’s relations with Russia.

In mid-July, Bayramov met Sergei Lavrov in Moscow and said the “difficult period” in bilateral relations was over and that ties had been fully normalised. A few weeks later, in Kyiv, he reaffirmed Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, while also signalling Baku’s interest in expanding energy cooperation.

The visit illustrates Baku’s multi-vector foreign policy. While maintaining dialogue with Russia, Azerbaijan has continued to provide humanitarian assistance to Ukraine and has expressed its readiness to support the country in the energy sector if required.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

Symbolic and practical significance of the Irpin visit

Irpin was one of the towns where the Russian advance on Kyiv was halted in 2022. Hundreds of civilians were killed during the fighting, and more than 70% of the town’s housing stock was destroyed.

Azerbaijan has contributed to Irpin’s reconstruction.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿@Bayramov_Jeyhun met with @Kyrylo_Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine 🇺🇦 during his official visit to Ukraine.



The sides commended the intensive political dialogue and high-level contacts… pic.twitter.com/ZAf6bdfRkd — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

The minister laid flowers at the bust of academician Zarifa Aliyeva in the park named after her, and visited the Zarifa Aliyeva Linguistic Lyceum and Irpin Central City Polyclinic, both rebuilt with Azerbaijan’s support. He was also briefed on future reconstruction projects, including plans to restore the town’s House of Culture.

In his statement, Zelensky said Bayramov had visited a school, a hospital and a rehabilitation centre supported by Azerbaijan. The visit to Irpin was seen as a demonstration of humanitarian solidarity with Ukraine, as well as Azerbaijan’s willingness to share its experience in rebuilding territories recovered from occupation.

I received Azerbaijan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, @Bayramov_Jeyhun. This is the Minister’s first visit to Ukraine since the beginning of Russia’s full-scale invasion. He began his visit in Irpin, where he visited a school, a hospital, and a rehabilitation center supported by… pic.twitter.com/7HTLIaz3EF — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) August 6, 2026

The visit to a town devastated by Russian forces, together with Bayramov’s review of reconstruction efforts and Azerbaijan’s continued support, was seen as underscoring Baku’s intention to reaffirm its longstanding position despite the “normalisation” of relations with Moscow, particularly its commitment to the principle of territorial integrity.

Following the official welcoming ceremony at the Foreign Ministry, Bayramov and Sybiha viewed an exhibition of Ukrainian-made drones. They then laid a wreath at the Memorial to the Fallen Defenders of Ukraine and observed a moment of silence in their honour.

Meetings and gas supply pledge

During expanded talks with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, the two sides discussed their strategic partnership, trade, energy, transport, humanitarian cooperation and regional security. Bayramov reiterated the need for an early end to the fighting and a diplomatic settlement based on international law, while reaffirming Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders.

He said Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded 50 million US dollars. Bayramov also highlighted reconstruction projects in Irpin and rehabilitation programmes for children.

During his meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky, the discussions focused on Russian attacks, the situation in the Black Sea, the disruption of grain export routes, defence cooperation, and cooperation in the energy, oil and gas, and agricultural sectors.

Zelensky thanked Azerbaijan for its energy and humanitarian assistance, as well as for maintaining constructive dialogue. Bayramov, in turn, spoke about the post-conflict situation in the South Caucasus and reconstruction efforts in the territories regained by Azerbaijan.

As part of his official visit to Ukraine 🇺🇦, FM of Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 @Bayramov_Jeyhun visited the Embassy of Azerbaijan in Kyiv.



The Minister met with the Embassy staff and received a comprehensive briefing on the Mission’s activities. pic.twitter.com/UPqN5Hn9rx — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 6, 2026

At a joint press conference, particular attention was drawn to Bayramov’s remarks on possible gas supplies: “If the need arises, we will be ready to supply gas to our friendly Ukraine.”

He highlighted SOCAR’s long-standing presence on the Ukrainian market, as well as the importance of Ukraine’s underground gas storage system – the largest in Europe – for regional energy security.

The statement can be seen as signalling Azerbaijan’s willingness to contribute to the diversification of Ukraine’s energy supplies, while also supporting alternative routes for Caspian gas exports to Europe. Against the backdrop of Russia’s strikes on energy infrastructure in southern Ukraine, Baku’s offer also underscores the importance of competition and diversification in the energy sector.

During meetings with Kyrylo Budanov and Ihor Klymenko, the sides also discussed regional and international security, as well as prospects for energy cooperation. They reaffirmed their commitment to the principles of state sovereignty, territorial integrity and the inviolability of internationally recognised borders.

Expert: “Azerbaijan will continue to provide Ukraine with political, economic and humanitarian support”

lkhan Shahinoglu, head of the Atlas Research Centre and a political commentator considered close to the Azerbaijani authorities, wrote that the visit is being closely watched by Russia:

The Kremlin will closely monitor Jeyhun Bayramov’s meetings in Kyiv. Azerbaijan’s partnership with any country is an exclusive sovereign right, and no other state has the right to interfere in that process.

At the same time, Russia, which is waging a war of conquest against Ukraine, closely watches those who cooperate with Kyiv. President Ilham Aliyev‘s response to the same question from Ukrainian journalist Gordon, asked at the Shusha Global Media Forum two years in a row – that ‘Ukraine should not reconcile itself to occupation’ – angered chauvinistic circles in Russia. They believe Azerbaijan should accept the annexation of Crimea and the occupation of Ukrainian territories.

Just as Jeyhun Bayramov visited Moscow some time ago, he has now travelled to Kyiv. Ukraine is Azerbaijan’s partner, and Baku will continue to provide it with political, economic and humanitarian support.”

World.title: Giga Avaliani case: Two more arrested 10 months after Georgian teacher’s murder
World.content:
Two more arrested in Giga Avaliani murder case

Two more suspects have been identified in the high-profile murder case of a 28-year-old teacher in Georgia. On 5 August 2026, two teenage girls – Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili – were arrested.

Giga Avaliani, a mathematics teacher, was killed in October 2025. Five people have already been convicted over his murder, while the trial of a sixth defendant is still under way. With the arrest of the two girls, the total number of suspects in the case has risen to eight – all of them minors.

The arrests of Nia Imnadze and Anastasia Beruashvili, after several convictions had already been secured, mark an unexpected and significant development in the Giga Avaliani case.

Nia Imnadze was one of Giga Avaliani’s former students and the girlfriend of the principal defendant, Aleksandre Gabashvili. Prosecutors accuse her of incitement to commit the crime.

According to local media, Anastasia Beruashvili is a friend of both Nia Imnadze and another convicted defendant, Giorgi Rikadze. She has been charged with failing to report the crime.

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics tutor, was returning home late on 1 October 2025 when he was attacked outside his apartment building. He fell into a coma following the assault and died on 24 October without regaining consciousness. Investigators say the attack was motivated by jealousy and what they describe as “unwanted communication with a girl”. The defendants have given a similar account. According to their version of events, Avaliani sent sexually explicit messages to his student Nia Imnadze, who told her boyfriend, prompting him to confront the teacher. Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, rejects that account. She says Nia had been skipping lessons and that Avaliani informed the girl’s mother, angering the student. According to Kupatadze, the attack was planned afterwards.

The Giga Avaliani case has become one of Georgia’s most high-profile criminal cases in recent years. Much of the public attention surrounding it has been driven by Avaliani’s mother, Eka Kupatadze, who campaigned for what she said should be a thorough and impartial investigation. Her efforts also helped generate significant public pressure over the handling of the case.

From the outset, Kupatadze maintained that Nia Imnadze bore primary responsibility for what had happened and repeatedly called for her arrest. The recent detention of the two girls has therefore raised new questions.

But the key question remains: if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, why were the two girls not arrested earlier? Was their detention the result of new evidence, or did it come only after sustained public pressure and Eka Kupatadze’s campaign?

Detention of two girls

Both girls were arrested late on the night of 5 August, in what appeared to be coordinated operations. News of the arrests first emerged through a video of Nia Imnadze’s detention, which was released by her lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili.

The footage is deeply distressing. It shows a large number of police officers arriving at Nia’s home. Her mother, visibly distressed, pounds on the front door, shouting: “Come in, all of you!”, “Maniacs!”, “Murderers!”, “Do you know that Niako is innocent?!”

The girl’s father, meanwhile, tells the police: “You are going to make me do something the whole of Georgia will be talking about. If you treat my child so unjustly, I will do it.”

Police officers try to calm the distraught parents.

“Why are you taking my child? On what grounds? What does the court order say?!” the mother asks.

“The lawyer has reviewed the court order,” one of the officers replies.

“Giorgi, on what grounds are they arresting her?” the mother asks the lawyer.

“On the basis of a court order containing only formal wording, nothing specific,” the lawyer replies.

Nia sits in the hallway on a sofa, curled up with her face buried in her hands. The video is being filmed by her lawyer, who occasionally strokes her hair.

Shortly after the video was released, reports began circulating on social media that the second girl, Anastasia Beruashvili, had also been detained. No footage of her arrest was made public, but the Ministry of Internal Affairs later confirmed that she had been taken into custody.

During her arrest, Nia Imnadze became unwell and was taken to hospital, where she spent the night. On 6 August, she was transferred to a pre-trial detention centre. Anastasia Beruashvili was also taken there.

Minors charged in Giga Avaliani's murder case in Georgia – read more Five people have already been convicted in connection with Giga Avaliani’s murder: Aleksandre Gabashvili – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. He was the principal defendant in the case and was found guilty of organising a group assault and intentionally inflicting grievous bodily harm as part of a group, resulting in the victim’s death. Giorgi Rikadze – sentenced to 10 years and five months’ imprisonment. A friend of Aleksandre Gabashvili, he was convicted on the same charges. Demetere Chikovani – sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was convicted of attempted intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm in the Avaliani case, as well as organising group violence in connection with the case and four other incidents. Ani Naskidashvili – sentenced to five years and three months’ imprisonment. She was found guilty of failing to report a particularly serious crime. Another minor – sentenced to three years’ imprisonment. He was convicted of giving false testimony. The nature of the false statements has not been disclosed. His case was heard behind closed doors, lawyers involved in the proceedings are bound by a non-disclosure order, and the teenager’s parents have declined to speak to the media. According to TV Pirveli, the boy is named Luka Klatkin. Giorgi Malania – arrested in July 2026 and charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. Malania is the son of a former senior Interior Ministry official, who served as deputy interior minister between 2016 and 2019. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered.

Eka Kupatadze’s reaction

“Georgia has won another battle against the killers of a healthy, innocent and talented young man – Giga Avaliani!” Eka Kupatadze said in response to the girls’ arrests.

Giga Avaliani’s family has always maintained that those who carried out the attack were not the only people involved. They have consistently called on investigators to identify and prosecute all those who may have played a role in the crime.

The family has paid particular attention to the alleged role of the two girls. Eka Kupatadze has repeatedly said that they knew the attack was being planned.

Until recently, however, prosecutors had taken no apparent action against additional suspects, prompting repeated criticism of the investigation from Avaliani’s family.

Kupatadze even appealed for help to Ekaterine Khvedelidze, the wife of Bidzina Ivanishvili, the founder of the ruling party and widely regarded as Georgia’s “informal ruler”. Khvedelidze replied to her letter, expressing sympathy and support for the mother who had lost her son.

“As far as I am aware, the investigation has not yet been completed. I am confident that the relevant state authorities will see it through to the end and that all the circumstances will be thoroughly examined, so that no question surrounding the terrible tragedy that has befallen you remains unanswered,” Ekaterine Khvedelidze wrote in her reply.

Formal charges

On the evening of 6 August, both girls were formally charged.

Nia Imnadze at the time of her arrest

Nia Imnadze has been charged with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm committed by a group. The offence carries a maximum sentence of 13 years’ imprisonment.

Anastasia Beruashvili has been charged with failing to report a particularly serious crime, an offence punishable by up to seven years’ imprisonment.

Under Georgian law, sentences imposed on minors are reduced by one quarter.

“The investigation conducted by the Ministry of Internal Affairs under the supervision of the Prosecutor’s Office established that, in September 2025, Nia Imnadze began taking mathematics lessons with Giga Avaliani. The accused, Nia Imnadze, told her friends Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Malania that her teacher, Giga Avaliani, had allegedly shown her excessive attention. By doing so, the accused incited Aleksandre Gabashvili to attack Giga Avaliani together with his accomplices,” the Prosecutor’s Office said in a statement.

According to the statement, Aleksandre Gabashvili, together with Giorgi Rikadze, Giorgi Malania and Demetere Chikovani, “decided to act on that incitement.”

What defence says

The defence has denied all the charges.

According to Nia Imnadze’s lawyer, Giorgi Lekishvili, there is no evidence in the case to support the allegation that she incited the attack.

The lawyer also rejected reports that prosecutors had obtained data and messages from Meta, and that the arrests followed an examination of those materials.

“Criminal proceedings cannot be based on suspicion. They must be based on lawfully obtained evidence, and no other standard can override that principle,” Lekishvili told reporters.

Ketevan Vardanashvili, the lawyer representing Anastasia Beruashvili, made similar arguments. She said Anastasia had not witnessed any crime and that she and Nia Imnadze had seen each other only once, for a few minutes.

“They had no friendship and no contact,” the lawyer said.

As for Anastasia’s relationship with the convicted defendant Giorgi Rikadze, Vardanashvili said that “even if she was his girlfriend, that does not mean she had any knowledge of the crime.”

Complaint or incitement?

The arrests of the two girls have sparked intense debate on social media. Many commentators agree that everyone responsible for Giga Avaliani’s death should be held accountable and that justice should be served. Many have also expressed sympathy for Eka Kupatadze.

At the same time, some have questioned the actions of the law enforcement authorities. They have asked whether prosecutors have sufficiently strong evidence against the two girls, particularly Nia Imnadze, who faces a lengthy prison sentence if convicted.

The Prosecutor’s Office statement says only that Nia Imnadze told her friends that Giga Avaliani had allegedly shown her excessive attention. It does not explain whether she knew an attack was being planned or whether she urged her boyfriend to take any specific action.

“Does complaining to friends amount to incitement?” some social media users have asked.

Others have also questioned why, if prosecutors had sufficient evidence, the girls were arrested only 10 months after the murder. Some have asked whether the arrests were prompted by Eka Kupatadze’s campaign, and whether political influence may have played a role.

Those questions also remain unanswered.

Timeline of Giga Avaliani's case – read more 1 October 2025 – The attack

Giga Avaliani, a 28-year-old mathematics teacher, was attacked outside his home in Tbilisi. 24 October 2025 – Death

After spending 23 days in a coma, Giga Avaliani died. November–December 2025 – First arrests

Four minors were arrested: Aleksandre Gabashvili, Giorgi Rikadze, Demetere Chikovani and Ani Naskidashvili. April 2026 – First convictions

Tbilisi City Court found Aleksandre Gabashvili and Giorgi Rikadze guilty and sentenced each to 10 years and six months’ imprisonment. Demetere Chikovani was sentenced to six years and nine months’ imprisonment. He was later convicted over separate violent offences committed at a different time, increasing his total sentence to nine years and nine months. June 2026 – Another conviction

The court sentenced Ani Naskidashvili to five years and three months’ imprisonment for failing to report the crime. July 2026 – Another arrest

Giorgi Malania was arrested. According to prosecutors, he was charged with aiding and abetting the intentional infliction of grievous bodily harm committed by a group. His trial is still under way and no verdict has yet been delivered. August 2026 – Two more arrests

Two more minor girls were arrested: Nia Imnadze, Giga Avaliani’s former student and the girlfriend of the principal convicted defendant, and Anastasia Beruashvili, described as a friend of Nia Imnadze and the girlfriend of the second convicted defendant.

Broader picture

From the outset, the Giga Avaliani case came to represent more than a single criminal investigation.

It exposed a range of systemic problems, most notably a lack of public trust in investigative authorities. The case also highlighted shortcomings in Georgia’s juvenile justice system, as well as concerns over the protection of the rights of both victims and defendants.

Many observers questioned the release of footage showing Nia Imnadze’s arrest, particularly as it was made public by her lawyer. Some argued that the video was intended to generate public sympathy for his client.

“Unfortunately, public trust in the justice system – the police, the Prosecutor’s Office, the courts and other institutions – is now so low that victims, defendants and lawyers increasingly see shaping public opinion as the only way to obtain justice. They then seek to use public pressure to their advantage,” lawyer Londa Toloraia wrote.

In her view, this reflects a profound crisis affecting both citizens and the justice system itself.

“You no longer trust the state, even when it may actually be making a lawful decision.”

Toloraia also raised a number of questions about the arrests of the two girls: What evidence were they based on? Why did they take place 10 months after the murder? And why were they carried out at night, when Georgian law restricts procedural actions during nighttime hours, particularly in cases involving minors?

“How much influence does public opinion have over the justice system? A great deal. It is extremely difficult to withstand public pressure. And where institutions are fully politicised, it becomes virtually impossible to make a decision that is unpopular with the public,” she argued.

She stressed that legal standards must be upheld even when dealing with those accused of serious crimes – especially when the defendants are minors.

The Avaliani case has also exposed a darker side of public reaction. Following Nia Imnadze’s arrest, social media was flooded with hostile comments directed at both her and her family. Many users described her as the main culprit and called for severe punishment. Others went further, posting comments about the suffering they believed awaited her in prison.

A second group of social media users expressed concern about the tone of those comments. Toloraia addressed the debate in a lengthy social media post.

“Children are not born criminals. Before demanding that they be lynched, we should first ask why they became who they are,” she wrote, adding that juvenile crime in Georgia has reached one of its highest levels in recent years. She argued that the state’s response has focused on opening a “special prison” for children rather than preventing youth crime. A state in which parents who have lost a child must seek justice through public mobilisation, while institutions make decisions according to fluctuations in public pressure, is a broken state,” Toloraia concluded.

World.title: Odesa in summer 2026: Life between sea and war. VIDEO
World.content:
Beaches, bomb-damaged homes and explosions in broad daylight. In the summer of 2026, Odesa is caught between its traditional seaside resort atmosphere and the constant threat of Russian attacks. While some people relax by the sea and stroll through the city centre, others sift through the rubble left by the latest strike.

JAMnews visited Odesa to show what life in the city looks like today.

Odesa and the surrounding region remain frequent targets of Russian strikes. Residential neighbourhoods, critical infrastructure and port facilities have all come under attack.

Russia has carried out combined attacks using drones and missiles, seeking to overwhelm Ukraine‘s air defence systems.

The impact of these attacks is visible across the city. Residential buildings have been damaged, windows blown out and flats destroyed. Strikes have also hit Odesa’s historic centre, including heritage buildings and universities.

Ports in Odesa Region, along with the logistics hubs and warehouses that support them, are also regularly targeted. Attacks on port infrastructure have disrupted Ukraine’s transport network and Black Sea export routes.

The strikes often occur in broad daylight, when the streets are busy, cafés and shops are open, and beaches are filled with residents and visitors. At any moment, the familiar sounds of the city can be interrupted by explosions, air defence fire or the buzz of attack drones.

On several occasions, missiles have been intercepted directly over the coastline while beaches were crowded with people.

Today, it is possible to spend the day at the beach and the night in a bomb shelter.

World.title: “Russia’s annexation of Georgia’s regions would not go unanswered” – embassies on 18th anniversary of August war
World.content:
France, Germany, Italy, Britain: Russia’s annexation of Georgia

France, Germany, Italy and the UK issued a joint statement marking the 18th anniversary of the 2008 Russo-Georgian war, reaffirming their support for Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.

18 years after the Russian aggression, we reaffirm our full support to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Georgia within its internationally recognized borders. We welcome Republic of Naoero’s decision to withdraw its recognition of the so-called independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

We urge states that have established diplomatic relations with these entities to follow this example,” the statement said.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia).

The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

August 7, 2026 marks 18 years since the start of the Russo-Georgian war over South Ossetia. In the 2008 war, 412 Georgian military personnel and civilians were killed, along with 365 people on the Ossetian side. Some 20,000 ethnic Georgians were displaced. Georgia also lost control of 125 more villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). The independence of South Ossetia and Abkhazia is recognized by Russia, Nicaragua, Venezuela and Syria.

France, Germany, Italy and the UK condemned Russia’s military presence in Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

ЭWe reiterate our condemnation of Russia’s ongoing military presence in the occupied breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia in violation of international law as well as Russia’s obligations under the six-point agreement of 12 August 2008.

Russia’s ongoing militarization of Georgia’s occupied territories poses a serious threat to the security of Georgia and to regional and European stability,” France, Germany, Italy and the UK said.

The statement also referred to rulings by the European Court of Human Rights.

In October 2025, the court found Russia responsible for a number of violations in the occupied regions, including the use of excessive force, ill-treatment, unlawful detention and restrictions on movement between Georgian-controlled territory and areas occupied by Russia.

“We urge Russia to implement the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights relating to this situation and to fully fulfil the commitments it made on August 12 and September 8, 2008,” the statement said.

The four countries also expressed concern over recent developments in South Ossetia.

They said the so-called “Agreement on Deepening Alliance and Cooperation,” signed by Moscow and the de facto authorities in South Ossetia on May 9, 2026, further violates Georgia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and is incompatible with international law.

“This is a clear violation of international law. This document, as well as the appointment of a Russian citizen to head the region raise concerns on a possible full-fledged annexation of the region, which would not go unanswered,” the statement said.

Support for the Geneva International Discussions, co-chaired by the EU, OSCE and UN, was reaffirmed.

They said it is the only format that allows the parties to work towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

The statement also stressed the importance of the EU Monitoring Mission in Georgia and said its work would continue to be supported in the future.

News in Georgia

World.title: Child safety worker union alarmed by possible removal of key reporting tool
World.content:
The Queensland government has been accused of attempting to remove a key reporting tool depicting just how under-pressure child safety workers are.

The Together Union, which represents child safety officers, said the Department of Child Safety has proposed removing the workload management tool in its latest bargaining agreement offer.

The union's assistant secretary, Dee Spink said the tool shows how many children workers are responsible for at any given time.

"We're actually seeking to expand the workload management tool as part of this bargaining process, and the department has told us they want to remove it," Ms Spink said.

Together Union assistant secretary Dee Spink. (ABC News)

Child safety and youth justice workers have been under protected industrial action as part of their bargaining period since August 3.

The union said Child Safety Minister, Amanda Camm and the Director-General Belinda Drew had not attended any bargaining sessions.

Ms Spink said she did not expect either to appear at every meeting.

"But what we do expect is that they will back up their words about wanting to fix the crisis in child safety with actions," she said.

Child Safety Minister Amanda Camm has been under pressure after recent statistics showed the number of children in residential care had soared. (ABC News)

Ms Spink said all options are on the table as part of the bargaining process, including walking off the job.

When questioned about the removal of the reporting tool, Premier David Crisafulli seemingly contradicted his own department and said he didn't think it should be withdrawn.

"I think it makes complete sense to keep it the same," he said.

" My view is that it should remain as it is, so there's a benchmark. "

The premier did not commit to making a directive ordering the reporting tool remain.

Opposition leader Steven Miles accused the government of trying to hide data from Queenslanders.

He was also scathing of Minister Camm, calling for the premier to sack her and condemned her failure to attend union bargaining agreement meetings.

"That's not good enough for Crisafulli government ministers to continue to say that it's not their job to work with their workforces, to meet with their unions and to get positive outcomes," Mr Miles said.

Opposition leader Steven Miles called on the premier to sack Child Safety Minister Amanda Camm. (ABC News: Lucas Hill)

Concerns over vacant positions

The latest stoush between the union and the government comes after it tabled its response into a landmark child safety inquiry.

As part of its response, the government released new data which showed a record number of children were in residential care, at almost 3,000 in March.

It accepted 32 out of 52 recommendations and accepted in principle a further 16.

Ms Spink said the proposal to remove the workload management tool strips the public of its ability to see if the changes are working.

Children in residential care in Qld higher than ever The Queensland government has handed down its response to the Child Safety Inquiry.

"[This] offer proposes removing one of the few mechanisms that allows workers — and ultimately Queenslanders — to see whether the system is actually improving, while failing to address the excessive workloads, unpaid overtime and retention issues identified by the Commission of Inquiry," she said.

The union also raised concerns about the number of vacancies for child safety officers.

Ms Spink said she's been told there are over 100 jobs that have not been filled across the state.

"And there is nothing in the [bargaining offer] that would address that," she said.

When asked for comment, the Minister for Child Safety referred to the premier's statement.

World.title: Head aims to maintain opening spot ahead of busy 12 months
World.content:
Travis Head can envisage himself continuing to open the batting for Australia at the end of next year's Ashes.

The positive mindset of the back-to-back Allan Border Medal winner is no surprise.

Head was a revelation in home conditions in last year's Ashes series with three centuries after moving up from the middle order.

Ahead of the opening Test against Bangladesh in Darwin, the 32-year-old was asked if his order switch was short-term or whether it could work across the 20 or more Tests Australia will play in the next 12 months.

There was a sense that Head's move up the order against England was intended to counter their ultra-aggressive "Bazball".

It worked so well that the term "Travball" was coined.

Prior to the home Ashes, his stints as an opener had been short-lived.

Travis Head scored three centuries as an opener in the last Ashes series. (Getty Images: Eurasia Sport Images/Ayush Kumar)

Head was unstoppable on home tracks in the Ashes series, but he will face a variety of surfaces in Australia, South Africa, England and India in the next 12 months.

He says he is not worried about playing in different conditions.

"I feel like I have been adaptable in the places that I have played," Head said.

"In India and England I have opened the batting, which is a slightly different to Australia.

"Everything is going to be different, but what I have been able to do over my career is problem solve the best that I can and work through challenges — whether they are green wickets or flat wickets.

"It will look different in every Test match or every series. I am trying to be as calm and consistent as I can."

Whether Head stays an opener will depend largely on how he performs and also on the displays of the middle order.

Tweaks may be made but right now Head plans to be opening in the final Test of next year's away Ashes series.

"I think it will work," he said.

"If I have done it for [another] 20 Tests and I am sitting there in a few years and I have opened the batting the whole time … I would have done an OK job and been consistent, contributed and had a good partnership with Jake [Weatherald].

"It is a new challenge coming here and a new challenge in South Africa in a month's time and I am looking forward to the challenge."

International cricket coach Joe Gatting has posted videos of how Head plans for a variety of scenarios and surfaces and he is expected to continue to find the best approach in all conditions.

"We have a lot of footage and we couldn't be more resourced in that space. I'll continue to do that," Head said.

AAP

World.title: ICAC questions lobbyist's role with 'toxic' Reformers
World.content:
Lobbyist Jeremy Greenwood said a right-wing Liberal Party factional group at the centre of a corruption watchdog inquiry became so "toxic" he encouraged his friends to leave it.

The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) is examining allegations prohibited donations were funnelled through third parties to support conservative Christian group, the NSW Reformers, and advance the interests of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif.

The inquiry is also examining allegations involving Mr Greenwood's former company, Beckington, which is alleged to have been used to conceal political donations as payments for lobbying and government relations work.

The inquiry had previously heard money from Mr Nassif's company, Toplace, was allegedly channelled through companies linked to Mr Greenwood before being distributed to some Reformers members.

Mr Greenwood fronted ICAC for the first time on Monday. (Supplied)

During his first day of evidence, Mr Greenwood said the Reformers eventually became a source of professional trouble for him and that the group was causing him "a lot of grief personally".

"This might surprise you, but I actually told them all to get out of the Reformers at some point," Mr Greenwood said.

During his evidence, Mr Greenwood became combative at times and disagreed with suggestions he wanted the group to continue to advocate for matters he personally supported or "thrive as a movement".

"I privately told all of them to not keep going … it became so toxic so no, I disagree with that," Mr Greenwood replied.

Reformers involvement downplayed

Mr Greenwood downplayed his involvement with the group, telling the inquiry he was more interested in policy than factional politics.

He told the commission he was working with Nationals senator Matt Canavan in 2018, while his friends and Reformers co-founders, Christian Ellis and Robert Assaf, were becoming increasingly involved in efforts to recruit conservative Liberal Party members.

Mr Greenwood said he considered himself "all about the Nationals" at the time and did not regard himself as a member of the Reformers or involved in the group's recruitment activities.

"It was always at a social level ... most of the engagement I had with these guys would have been at a pub or I've been dragged into a group chat," he said.

Mr Greenwood said he was interested in the group's conservative social policies and would have attended some events featuring speakers, including one with former broadcaster Alan Jones.

"If Alan was going and speaking, I would have wanted to go. Yeah, I like Alan. He's great," Mr Greenwood told the inquiry.

Dr Dwyer questioned Mr Greenwood's level of involvement with The Reformers. (ABC News: Timothy Ailwood)

Counsel Assisting Peggy Dwyer SC argued it was clear that Mr Greenwood was supporting the group's activities and events.

Dr Dwyer said: "Can I suggest this to you ... You are at pains to try to distance yourself from the Reformers, but in fact, it's abundantly clear that you were supporting their work in 2019." Mr Greenwood replied: "I counted 30 times a witness in here said, 'I'm not a member of the Reformers'. I am at pains because how many people have to say I'm not a member of the Reformers? Nobody has said I'm a member of the Reformers." "I've told you that from time to time in social settings, I would give advice and yes, I supported their issues."

Mr Greenwood also told the inquiry Mr Ellis wanted to give evidence to ICAC, despite declining to appear before the commission.

The key figures in ICAC investigation Eight weeks of public hearings by the ICAC that could change the NSW Liberal Party forever begin on Monday.

In her opening statement, Dr Dwyer said Mr Ellis, who now lives in the UK, went to "significant lengths to avoid process servers".

Dr Dwyer said he had cited family commitments and the timezone difference for not participating in the inquiry.

Mr Greenwood said he remained in contact with Mr Ellis and recently visited him in the UK, but was not sure of any plans for him to return to Australia.

World.title: Accused Chinese people smuggler denied bail in Cairns court
World.content:
An alleged people smuggler has been denied bail after his fishing-trip alibi was dismissed because he had 10 illegal migrants in his hotel room and no evidence of an interest in fishing.

Sydney-based Chinese national Hao Wang has been charged with smuggling Chinese citizens, after being arrested in Weipa on western Cape York Peninsula on June 30.

Cairns Magistrates Court today heard Mr Wang had driven a rental car from Cairns three days earlier, a distance of more than 800km that can take more than 10 hours.

It is alleged that early on June 30, a group of people without visas came ashore at Pennefather River, about 50 kilometres north-west of Weipa.

Magistrate Michael Dalton said Mr Wang was arrested by AFP and Border Force officers at Weipa's Heritage Shopping Centre that afternoon on the grounds that he himself was an unlawful non-citizen.

The 10 migrants were then found in a room at the Albatross Hotel.

Magistrate Dalton disagreed with defence lawyer Aaron Dunkerton's comments that the prosecution case was weak.

"I have an unlawful non-citizen painter who lives in Sydney, who is in Weipa — a very, very long way from home — and you wouldn't Adam-and-Eve it, but the unlawful non-citizens have been found in his hotel room booked by him," Magistrate Dalton told the court.

"That's a remarkable coincidence."

To which Mr Dunkerton replied: "I accept how it appears."

Magistrate Dalton also rejected Mr Dunkerton's reasoning that Mr Wang had been on a fishing trip, saying fishing off Weipa was "not for novices", and there was no evidence of an interest in the activity.

"Weipa is not for people who might be beginning dropping a line in the ocean," Magistrate Dalton said.

Mr Dunkerton said evidence that WhatsApp messages to a phone in Indonesia — the country the migrants had come from by boat — were circumstantial.

"It's entirely unremarkable in my submission that there's a text message to an Indonesian number on the same day. We live in a global world," Mr Dunkerton told the court.

But Magistrate Dalton refused bail, saying Mr Wang was a flight risk.

"Given that he has connection to the people-smuggling offence, I do hold concerns that he may be able to use those connections to leave this country," he said.

But Commonwealth prosecutor Chris Moore said that even if Mr Wang had been granted bail, the attorney-general would have acted quickly to take Mr Wang to an immigration detention centre.

Hao Wang's case will return to court in Cairns on October 1. (ABC News: Conor Byrne)

Mr Moore said the immigration minister had been notified about Mr Wang's case.

"Whether he takes that into account or whether there's some other factors at play in determining what should be done with him," he said.

The offence Mr Wang has been charged with has a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, with a mandatory non-parole period of at least three years.

The court heard Mr Wang arrived in Adelaide in 2012 to study at St George's College, but had not had a valid visa for at least two years.

He has a three-year-old daughter with his ex-partner in Sydney.

World.title: Geelong Cats board holds crisis meeting over concussion deal
World.content:
Geelong is about to reply to the AFL's "please explain" as the Cats brace for a potential massive penalty over the secret concussion deal with Jake Kolodjashnij.

Amid speculation over the futures of Geelong chief executive Steve Hocking and AFL chairman Craig Drummond, the club board held a crisis meeting on Monday to work out its response to the league.

Also on Monday, Geelong captain Patrick Dangerfield said the club had "buggered up", but strongly defended Hocking.

Pressure has been mounting on Geelong and the AFL since it emerged last Thursday that the Cats struck a secret agreement with Kolodjashnij, who had a history of concussion.

Drummond apologises AFL chair Craig Drummond issues a statement apologising for his part in the Jake Kolodjashnij concussion contract saga.

"We acknowledge this has been a challenging time for Jake, our club and Geelong supporters," Cats president Grant McCabe said in a statement on Monday.

"The board has met this morning to discuss our response to the AFL's letter. That will be submitted by end of day Tuesday, 11 August.

"This will provide the club with the chance to detail the actions it took in navigating this complex matter. We welcome this opportunity.

"The club remains committed to providing our players with the highest standard of care and support."

Hocking was Cats chief executive and Drummond was the club president when the deal was struck two years ago with Koladjashnij.

The Geelong defender signed a waiver that meant he effectively took on legal responsibility for future brain trauma in a bid to indemnify the club and its medical staff from potential court action.

On the weekend Hocking defended the club in a radio interview and argued there was not a lot they would do differently.

"As a leader it's really important to take ownership and just lead through this. It's not easy to do, but I wouldn't change too much — we are a really good football club," he said.

"I know there are people out there who say culturally we are maybe not as strong as we have been, but we do so much right and occasionally there might be one or two per cent we don't get right.

"In this case that will be proven, I would suggest, that will be proven with the 'please explain'. We don't get everything right."

Drummond also released a statement in which he apologised over the deal. He added he would not be involved in the AFL's assessment and deliberation of the Kolodjashnij situation.

On Monday, Dangerfield told Fox Footy that Hocking was one of the most "placid" people he had met and gave him his full support.

"He's a man of the highest integrity … we're lucky to have him," Dangerfield said.

But he acknowledged mistakes had been made.

"Clearly there were some parts that we buggered up as a club. We can be better," he said.

AAP

World.title: A golden mic, a 'clunky start' but Sandilands returns to the air
World.content:
"The golden microphone is on" were the five words that heralded a new era for Kyle Sandilands, but not everything went to plan.

When he moved his lips after the introduction, the audience tuning in for his new digital program heard nothing, with dead air lingering for five seconds.

The moment was emblematic of the teething issues that plagued the beginning of Kyle Sandilands Live, the subscription-only podcast looking to reinvent the controversial shock jock after his decades on commercial radio came to an end earlier this year.

"Well hi, we're off to a clunky start everyone," Sandilands eventually said.

As the seasoned presenter ploughed on to introduce the show's new personalities, audio played loudly and for a touch too long, briefly drowning Sandilands's commentary.

"The brand new Kyle Sandilands Live program, it is a new invention, it is live, we're all here," Sandilands said.

"And it's a digital mess behind the scenes."

Dead air, echoing audio and other teething issues

His longtime friend and manager Bruno Bouchet chimed in.

He had skipped sleep over the course of a week to help develop the show.

"If everything went smoothly, it would've been worse, not sleeping … and everything like that," Mr Bouchet said.

"But you know, it all went to shit."

Sandilands pushed back: "It didn't go to shit, I just can't hear, I can't hear any audio.

"I would imagine … the man speaking behind the microphone should be the main one that hears what's going on."

The show's first few minutes acknowledged the efforts that come with building a podcast quickly, as Sandilands tried to capitalise on media interest from a settled court dispute, and popularity from his radio and TV career.

NSW premier shows support by being first guest

New South Wales Premier Chris Minns visited the show as the inaugural guest, bringing with him "golden" scissors for a ribbon cutting.

But subscribers barely got to witness the moment, as it took place in the background and was obscured by a pylon and staff member.

Sandilands praised Mr Minns for being a Labor politician with appeal beyond his party, and brought up a recent chance meeting in the Blue Mountains.

Premier Chris Minns on Kyle Sandilands Live's first episode. (Supplied)

He also asked the premier for his opinion on his old show's cancellation.

"I was worried for you, I was worried about the show," Mr Minns said.

"There's not many shows in radio or TV or ratings history that don't keep going when they're number one.

" I was concerned for you, but I'm glad this is up and running, this is fantastic. "

Sandilands described the program as a work in progress.

"Well would you call it up and running? I feel it's half up and running."

The dawn of a new Kyle Sandilands show

It is Kyle's first day on air after being sacked by ARN from his show co-hosted with Jackie O Henderson in February. (Supplied)

Six months have passed since an on-air dispute with Sandilands's longtime radio co-host Jackie 'O' Henderson led to the eventual demise of his breakfast show on Kiss FM.

In February, owner ARN Media told the Australian Stock Exchange Jackie O had "given notice that she cannot continue to work with Mr Sandilands".

It signalled the ending of radio contracts with the duo paid a combined $200 million.

Sandilands launched the new show after negotiating a multi-million-dollar out of court settlement over his termination from ARN. (ABC News: Jamie McKinnell)

Separate wrongful termination cases were launched by Sandilands and Jackie O against ARN Media in the Federal Court.

Sandilands settled his dispute with his former employer in June for $12.09 million, well under the $85 million he initially sought.

The deal also included a provision where ARN Media would receive 19.9 per cent of the revenue from Kyle Sandilands Live for three years, in exchange for providing $1.5 million in advertising.

Jackie O has not settled her dispute and was seeking $82 million in compensation for wrongful termination.

World.title: Phones across western Cape York down again
World.content:
Telecommunications across western Cape York suffered another outage this morning just hours after services were restored following a bushfire which crippled the network over the weekend.

Telstra northern Queensland general manager Rachel Cliffe said the latest outage was the result of a "secondary power-related fault" at a base at Mapoon, north of Weipa.

"That's secondary to what Mother Nature did on the weekend," she said.

Telstra has confirmed the latest five-hour outage was caused when the site's battery backup was exhausted after a power outage in the area.

All services across the region jave been restored after Telstra sent a technician to connect the tower to a portable generator.

"Some of our bigger sites have more power backups and some of our smaller sites don't, it's all engineered for the power reserves that are needed," Ms Cliffe said.

"Typically it's the power reserves needed before we can get a technician to that site before it goes down.

"We again apologise … this is a secondary fault to the one we had related to the bushfire on Saturday through Sunday."

That outage saw mobile phone reception affected in the towns of Weipa, Mapoon and Aurukun as well as Mission River, Napranum and Rocky Point, with services down for almost 30 hours.

Customers were unable to make any calls, including to Triple Zero (000), from around 5pm on Saturday evening until 10pm last night.

Ms Cliffe has defended the time it took to restore services, saying crews needed to be deployed from Cairns to repair significant damage to infrastructure.

"Unfortunately, a bushfire burnt our pit and burnt our optic fibre that was in the pit," she said.

"It doesn't take two minutes to do [fix] this … we needed to replace large lengths of optic fibre and connect them in.

"Of course, we never, ever want this type of incident to occur and we do apologise to the customers impacted."

Business impact

Local businesses including the Weipa Campground were thrown into chaos when the initial outage hit over the weekend.

Campground manager Angela Burr said losing access to internet services had the biggest impact on the business.

"We've had previous phone issues as it is, but once we realised it was attached to the internet, it was a bit of a scramble to work out how we were going to proceed for the rest of the afternoon," she said.

At the time of the outage, guests were arriving and Ms Burr was unable to confirm who had booked, who had paid, and which sites were available for walk-ins.

She said the business had to go back to basics to get through.

The Weipa Campground was impacted by the initial Telstra outage. (Supplied: Weipa Camping Ground)

"[We took] down very detailed information of our guests, trying to have a pretty good memory on which sites have been booked and which sites are available," she said.

"We did have to set up Starlink, which did take some time to get active, but thankfully we were back fully operational by the following day, so Sunday, although slower, it still worked well."

She said all guests who hadn't been able to pay before the Starlink was set up did the right thing the following morning.

"Luckily enough, we weren't affected financially by this," she said.

"It hit us hard, the realisation of how much we truly rely on this system."

Better solutions needed

The community of Mapoon, about 80 kilometres north of Weipa, was affected by both outages.

The shire's CEO Chad King said council had set up additional free wi-fi yesterday but the inability for residents to make Triple Zero calls made for an anxious weekend.

"I think we might've dodged a bullet but it is a scary thought to know you could be here having a heart attack, suffering domestic violence issues … but you can't get contact with the outside world," he said.

The western Cape York community of Mapoon in far north Queensland is home to around 500 people. (ABC News: Brendan Mounter)

Mr King said Telstra removed fixed lines to the community during the NBN rollout and were now reliant on a single phone tower which the outage highlighted as a "single point of failure".

He said better services in the bush were needed.

"We need to think about how we make these telecommunications more resilient given that we're so reliant on them now," Mr King said.

World.title: WNBA player claims 'white privilege' saw her ejected after foul
World.content:
DiJonai Carrington of the Chicago Sky has been ejected after being called for a Flagrant 2 foul on Sophie Cunningham of the Indiana Fever.

Minutes after the eviction on Saturday (local time), Carrington posted on social media the words "WHITE PRIVILEGE" and tagged the Fever.

Cunningham, who is white, was shooting a fast-break lay-up in the first quarter when Carrington, who is black, came from behind and hit her in the head and neck, knocking her to the court as the shot went in.

Cunningham said she thought the foul in the 90–86 Indiana win was "absolutely" intentional.

"Clearly I think it was unnecessary," Cunningham said.

"I've never really spoken to her and I have no beef with her, but I guess she has some pent-up stuff."

DiJonai Carrington had little to complain about, most suggested. (Getty Images: Michael Reaves)

Fever coach Stephanie White had a different view of the play.

"It was a hard foul," White said.

"I don't think that DiJonai intentionally came out to get her across the neck like she did, but it did happen, and I thought it was the right call."

Cunningham got up immediately, charged toward Carrington and pushed her as she was held back by a teammate.

"I popped up," Cunningham said.

"I'm not going to let anyone just do that to me. I think everyone knows that. I think that's why she did it, because she wants attention."

Sophie Cunningham had to be held back after popping up after the foul. (Getty Images: Icon Sportswire/Melissa Tamez)

The play was reviewed and upgraded to a Flagrant 2 after the referee said there was wind-up, impact and follow-through on the foul.

Sky coach Tyler Marsh said he had not seen a replay of the play, but that seeing it live, he thought Carrington was making a play on the ball and that he did not believe it warranted a Flagrant 2 foul.

"I haven't looked at that play since, so I really don't know if it was justified or not," he said.

"But, that's what I thought in the moment."

Marsh was then asked about Carrington's social media post.

"I have to get back to you on that because I'm just now hearing about that," he said.

"So yeah, we'll handle that."

But Cunningham had plenty to say about the post.

"I think the league is taking care of that," she said.

"This has nothing to do with race. Last year, I did the same thing and I got kicked out. And I deserved to be kicked out. There's no reason even to play that card."

In the third quarter, Fever star Caitlin Clark was assessed a technical foul after she made contact with a referee when she was forced out of bounds.

WNBA champs rubbish claims of Clark jealousy The outsized spotlight on Caitlin Clark has prompted some to suggest others in the WNBA are jealous of her, but two champions of the league say that is nonsense.

The technical was Clark's eighth of the season, triggering a one-game suspension for Indiana's next game if not rescinded by the league.

"She said I ran into her," Clark said in a post-game television interview.

"I've already watched it on the tape, so we'll let the league decide. But it wasn't intentional or anything, so I'm hoping it's getting rescinded,"

A few hours after the game, Clark got her way. The WNBA rescinded the technical foul.

Cunningham has frequently come to Clark's defence after physical play by opponents and has become one of the higher-profile players in the league this season.

AP

World.content:
Updated NationalQueenslandCrime Teens ‘armed themselves’ before attending party where 21yo died, police say William Davis and Cloe Read Updated August 10, 2026 — 1:50pm ,first published August 10, 2026 — 7:12am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Four teenagers charged over the bashing murder of a 21-year-old man were part of a group who went to a house party armed with weapons and a plan to harm people, police allege. Detectives from Queensland’s Organised Crime Gangs Group are now part of the investigation into the death of Jongkuch Achiew, who was found lying severely injured in a suburban street by police after they were called to the out-of-control house party. Achiew died at Princess Alexandra Hospital after succumbing to head injuries he suffered at the gathering at Bahrs Scrub, a suburb in Logan south of Brisbane, in the early hours of Sunday, July 26. Loading Four male teenagers, aged 18 and 19 years old, were arrested and charged on August 6 following investigations by homicide detectives.



On Sunday evening, four more teenagers aged 17 and 18 were arrested and charged with murder. The teenagers were arrested after police stormed a house in Morayfield about 5pm, although they reside in Acacia Ridge, Sunnybank, Inala and Doolandella. Speaking on Monday morning, Detective Inspector Ian Galpin said police would allege the group had a plan to harm people and armed themselves with various weapons, before attending the party. “What the police will allege is that this group attended this location with a common purpose of causing harm to people at that address,” he said. He would not elaborate on the types of weapons allegedly carried by the group.



When asked whether the alleged murder was gang-related, Galpin confirmed the Organised Crime Gangs Group had joined the police investigation. However, he said police liaison officers had been working closely with community leaders to address any concerns. Jongkuch Achiew, 21, died in hospital less than a week after he was found with significant head injuries on a suburban Logan street. Nine “Together they have done an amazing job at addressing any suggestion or tension within the community,” Galpin said. “I can tell you that everyone that we have spoken to, they want nothing but peace within their community and that’s why I’m confident there won’t be any further retaliation.”



He said police were continuing to work with the community to address concerns. There was a large crowd at the party, but police said they could not estimate the number of people in attendance.



Three 18-year-old men charged on Sunday – Morad George, Jason Marik, and Benito Bikanye – had their cases briefly mentioned in Brisbane Magistrates Court on Monday. Their cases were adjourned to August 24. The case of the 17-year-old boy, who cannot be named under Queensland law, was heard in the Childrens Court. Police were called to reports of a large disturbance at a Bahrs Scrub property in Logan just after 2am on July 26. Nine News Police have carried out 14 search warrants across Logan, South Brisbane, and Ipswich as part of the murder investigation. Galpin said it was possible more charges could be laid. When asked about Achiew’s family, Galpin said it had been a very emotional and difficult time for them.



A message attributed to Achiew’s family, and posted to a social media group representing members of the Biong community from South Sudan, thanked police and other first responders for their efforts. “This is a life cut far too short, and a loss felt profoundly by all who knew and loved him,” it said. Loading Police were called to the house party on Discovery Boulevard just after 2am following reports of a large disturbance. They found significant damage at a house and vehicles along the street.



People allegedly fled the scene as soon as officers arrived, and Achiew was found with significant head injuries on a nearby street. He was rushed to Princess Alexandra Hospital in a critical condition but died after his life support was switched off six days later. A 22-year-old Heathwood man has also been charged with one count of contravening an order about information necessary to access information stored electronically. World.title: Teachers offered $2000 sign-on bonus as Labor fights to stop third strike
World.content:
Breaking PoliticsVictoriaEducation Teachers offered $2000 sign-on bonus as Labor fights to stop third strike Alex Crowe Updated August 10, 2026 — 1:39pm ,first published 12:59pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Victorian educators would get a $2000 bonus with the signing of a pay and conditions offer from the state government, as the new education minister attempts to avoid statewide school strikes planned for next Wednesday. Teacher, principal and education support staff salaries would still rise by at least 28.3 per cent over the next four years as per the previous offer, but those at the top of their salary bands would receive a 1 per cent annual lump-sum payment, plus the one-off payment at the start of the new agreement. Education Minister Gabrielle Williams and Premier Ben Carroll. Eddie Jim Australian Education Union Victorian president Justin Mullaly said the offer came a day after the premier committed the state government to signing a full funding agreement with the federal government before the November state election. “Victoria needs full funding for public schools and pay and conditions that reflect the value of the important work public school staff do for Victorian families and communities,” Mullaly said.





Lucy Honan, a spokesperson for the union’s left faction, said they will vote against recommending the deal to members and will call to push on with industrial action. Teachers, principals and support staff will stop work for 24-hours on August 19, the third strike this year, if it is rejected. The union had originally sought a 35 per cent pay increase over three years, which would mean graduate teachers would start on more than $107,400 by 2028 and experienced teachers would earn more than $159,300 by 2028. Members rejected an in-principle agreement endorsed by 120 of its elected council members in June, under which teachers’, assistant principals’ and principals’ salaries would have increased by between 28.3 per cent and 32.4 per cent over four years.



Under the in-principle schools agreement, a graduate teacher’s pay would have increased from the current $79,589 to more than $114,731 by 2029 and an experienced classroom teacher’s pay would have increased from the current $118,063 to $151,419 by 2029. Teachers would also have received a lump sum payment of 1 per cent of their salary each year. Thousands of Victorian teachers and support staff walked off the job in July as part of their campaign for better wages and conditions. Wayne Taylor Union leadership has signalled that signing a long-term agreement with the Commonwealth to fully fund public schools, as set out by the Gonski reforms, is crucial to pay negotiations. Victoria’s two-year federal funding agreement is set to expire at the end of 2026. It is the only state or territory not to reach an agreement with the Commonwealth, though both parties have signalled that a deal is imminent. Premier Ben Carroll said negotiations with the Commonwealth were ongoing and it remained a top priority.



Related Article Updated

Education Teachers prepare to strike again as pay negotiations falter “I said to the prime minister when I spoke to him during the week, education was one of my priorities,” he said. Carroll said he’d always wanted to work constructively with the union and his door was always open to its representatives. “I am urging them not to strike next week. Kids should be in the classroom learning,” he said. “It was a very close vote last time, and I’m sure we can get there.” The public school educators’ pay negotiations have broader implications for the sector and its about 40,000 Catholic school staff, who are currently negotiating their own enterprise agreement. Catholic teachers have had pay parity with Victorian public school teachers since the 1990s.

World.title: Want to travel with a tennis champion or famous author? Board a ship
World.content:
Last week anyone who happened to be sailing with Explora Journeys in the Mediterranean had a brief chance to encounter tennis superstar Jannik Sinner, on board Explora II sailing between Genoa and Marseille for an overnight stay to promote his wellness collaboration with the cruise line.

Sinner participated in a Q&A session and charity gala dinner, and made appearances at private coaching and wellness sessions available to a few select guests. No word on whether he’ll make further appearances but, as brand ambassador for the cruise line, I expect he will.

Jannik Sinner aboard Explora II.

Jannik Sinner is one of the biggest stars to recently grace a cruise ship, but in the past Katy Perry, Kelly Clarkson, Sheryl Crow and yes, even Taylor Swift have performed at sea. Themed cruises have seen the likes of Beach Boys, Kiss, The Walking Dead, New Kids on the Block, and the cast of Star Trek make appearances.

You’ll have to keep a lively lookout for the release of such cruises, which are booked out by fans before you can shout “anchors aweigh”. Many cruise lines, however, have special guests on board who, while they mightn’t have the same celebrity status, are equally experts in their field.

Three 18-year-old men charged on Sunday – Morad George, Jason Marik, and Benito Bikanye – had their cases briefly mentioned in Brisbane Magistrates Court on Monday. Their cases were adjourned to August 24. The case of the 17-year-old boy, who cannot be named under Queensland law, was heard in the Childrens Court. Police were called to reports of a large disturbance at a Bahrs Scrub property in Logan just after 2am on July 26. Nine News Police have carried out 14 search warrants across Logan, South Brisbane, and Ipswich as part of the murder investigation. Galpin said it was possible more charges could be laid. When asked about Achiew’s family, Galpin said it had been a very emotional and difficult time for them.



A message attributed to Achiew’s family, and posted to a social media group representing members of the Biong community from South Sudan, thanked police and other first responders for their efforts. “This is a life cut far too short, and a loss felt profoundly by all who knew and loved him,” it said. Loading Police were called to the house party on Discovery Boulevard just after 2am following reports of a large disturbance. They found significant damage at a house and vehicles along the street.



People allegedly fled the scene as soon as officers arrived, and Achiew was found with significant head injuries on a nearby street. He was rushed to Princess Alexandra Hospital in a critical condition but died after his life support was switched off six days later. A 22-year-old Heathwood man has also been charged with one count of contravening an order about information necessary to access information stored electronically.
